question: How was midwifery knowledge primarily passed down in ancient times?

options.A: Orally from one generation to the next
options.B: Via written medical textbooks
options.C: Through formal university degrees
options.D: Through government licensing exams

explanation: Before formal schools existed, experienced women shared their trade by word of mouth and practical demonstration with younger women in the community. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which statement best describes how ancient societies viewed childbirth?

options.A: As an illness that required prolonged bed rest in a ward
options.B: As a surgical procedure requiring a team of doctors
options.C: As a natural and domestic event managed by women
options.D: As an administrative duty handled by village leaders

explanation: Childbirth took place at home and was treated as a normal part of life handled by female community members rather than a disease managed in a hospital. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h1)

question: Where did the shift in childbirth take place during the 18th and 19th centuries in the West?

options.A: From hospitals back to private homes
options.B: From community centers to open-air markets
options.C: From homes into formal medical institutions
options.D: From herbalist huts to spiritual shrines

explanation: The Western medical movement brought laboring women out of their domestic environments and into hospitals for delivery. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h2)

question: What was a major consequence of the medicalization of childbirth in Western history?

options.A: Pregnancy became entirely free of any complications
options.B: Childbirth was increasingly treated as a medical condition
options.C: Hospitals stopped using surgical instruments entirely
options.D: Traditional midwives gained higher social status

explanation: As doctors took over maternity care, normal labor began to be viewed and managed as an illness or medical event needing intervention. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h2)

question: Who typically served as the primary maternity care providers in pre-colonial Nigerian communities?

options.A: University medical professors
options.B: Government public health officers
options.C: Traditional Birth Attendants
options.D: European trained surgeons

explanation: Respected community women, known as Traditional Birth Attendants, provided the frontline support for pregnant women across indigenous Nigerian societies. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in a remote pre-colonial setting needed comfort during labor. What intervention was most likely used by her local birth attendant?

options.A: Electronic fetal heart rate monitoring
options.B: Intravenous fluid therapy
options.C: Cesarean section under general anesthesia
options.D: Abdominal massage and local herbs

explanation: Indigenous care relied on natural remedies, physical comfort measures like massage, and traditional support systems rather than modern medical technology. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h3)

question: What was the primary initial purpose of introducing Western medicine during the early colonial era in Nigeria?

options.A: To completely eliminate all herbal medicine
options.B: To establish free university hospitals nationwide
options.C: To train local villagers in advanced surgery
options.D: To care for colonial officers and expatriates

explanation: Western medical services were initially brought in to protect the health of British administrators and foreign workers stationed in the territory. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h4)

question: How did the arrival of colonial health services affect maternity care in Nigeria?

options.A: It forced every pregnant woman to give birth in Europe
options.B: It immediately ended all maternal mortality across the country
options.C: It introduced formal training schools and Western delivery techniques
options.D: It completely integrated traditional birth practices into medical boards

explanation: Missionaries and colonial authorities set up the first maternity homes and began training local women in Western-style midwifery concepts. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h4)

question: What major shift occurred in midwifery education in Nigeria after independence in 1960?

options.A: Education was moved entirely out of hospitals and into factories
options.B: Training became strictly based on informal apprenticeships
options.C: Curricula were formalized and aligned with structured institutions
options.D: All midwifery schools were closed down by the government

explanation: The post-independence era focused on building organized educational programs with standardized curricula to train Nigerian healthcare workers. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why were post-independence health reforms necessary for Nigerian nursing and midwifery?

options.A: To replace foreign personnel with trained indigenous professionals
options.B: To ban all forms of traditional remedies from the country
options.C: To reduce the number of hospitals operating in rural areas
options.D: To make healthcare entirely dependent on foreign grants

explanation: A newly independent nation needed its own qualified local workforce to run hospitals, maternity centers, and public health programs effectively. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which organization is legally responsible for registering and disciplining midwives in Nigeria?

options.A: The Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.B: The Nigerian Red Cross Society
options.C: The West African Health Organization
options.D: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the statutory body established to control and regulate the education and practice of the profession. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary function of professional associations such as the National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives?

options.A: To build private commercial hospitals across the country
options.B: To set legal penalties for criminal offenses in courts
options.C: To advocate for worker welfare and uphold professional ethics
options.D: To import pharmaceutical drugs from overseas manufacturers

explanation: Professional associations exist to protect the interests of their members, promote high ethical standards, and support professional growth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is a major challenge faced by modern midwives working in various parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Having too many doctors and no patients to care for
options.B: Bridging global standards with local infrastructural gaps
options.C: The complete absence of pregnant women in rural areas
options.D: An absolute surplus of high-tech maternity hospitals

explanation: Midwives must strive to deliver high-quality global care standards even when working in facilities that may lack basic equipment or steady power. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h7)

question: A midwife is posted to a rural primary health center with limited equipment and high maternal mortality. What approach best reflects the modern role of the midwife in this setting?

options.A: Referrals only, offering no primary care services on-site
options.B: Combining clinical care with public health education and advocacy
options.C: Focusing solely on routine deliveries without community outreach
options.D: Refusing to work until a major surgical theater is built

explanation: Modern midwives act as educators and public health leaders who actively engage their communities to improve health outcomes despite resource limits. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T1#BMP211_U1_T1_h7)

question: Which international body sets the essential competencies required for basic midwifery education and practice?

options.A: International Confederation of Midwives
options.B: World Health Organization Regional Office
options.C: International Council of Nurses
options.D: West African Health Organization

explanation: The ICM is globally recognized for setting the core standards and essential competencies that define basic midwifery training and practice worldwide. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does the official definition of a midwife specifically emphasize partnership with women?

options.A: To reduce the total number of hospital visits required during the antenatal period
options.B: To respect women's choices and encourage active participation in their own care
options.C: To ensure the midwife takes sole legal blame if a birth complication occurs
options.D: To make sure relatives do not interfere with medical procedures in the labour ward

explanation: Midwifery practice centers around a woman-friendly approach that honors individual autonomy, informed consent, and shared decision-making throughout pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is a primary duty of a midwife during the postnatal period?

options.A: Assessing uterine involution and checking lochia
options.B: Administering chemotherapy for gestational trophoblastic disease
options.C: Fitting permanent contraceptive implants like tubal ligation
options.D: Performing major abdominal surgery for fibroids

explanation: Checking how the uterus contracts and monitoring lochia are standard postnatal assessments to ensure the mother is recovering safely after childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h2)

question: A midwife notes that a baby born five minutes ago has a slow heart rate and is struggling to breathe. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait for the attending pediatrician to arrive before touching the infant
options.B: Conduct immediate newborn resuscitation and provide thermal care
options.C: Discharge the mother and baby home immediately to reduce clinic stress
options.D: Prescribe oral antibiotics for suspected neonatal sepsis

explanation: Immediate resuscitation and keeping the newborn warm are core lifesaving responsibilities expected of every trained midwife during intrapartum and neonatal care. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must a midwife clearly understand the legal limits of their professional scope of practice?

options.A: To guarantee that they receive a higher salary than general nurses
options.B: To prevent practicing outside legal boundaries and ensure patient safety
options.C: To avoid having to document routine clinical procedures in patient files
options.D: To make sure they can perform major surgeries without a doctor present

explanation: Knowing what procedures are permitted prevents malpractice, ensures timely referrals, and protects both the mother and the legal standing of the midwife. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following procedures is NOT within the standard scope of practice for a basic midwife?

options.A: Repairing a first-degree perineal tear
options.B: Performing an elective Caesarean section
options.C: Conducting a normal vertex vaginal delivery
options.D: Administering routine postpartum oxytocin

explanation: Major abdominal surgeries like Caesarean sections require specialized medical training as a doctor or obstetrician, falling outside the routine scope of a midwife. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h3)

question: What does professional autonomy mean for a practicing midwife?

options.A: Prescribing any medication available in a standard retail pharmacy
options.B: Taking full personal responsibility for clinical decisions during normal childbirth
options.C: Running a private maternity hospital without any government oversight
options.D: Working completely alone without ever needing to consult a doctor

explanation: Autonomy grants the midwife the legal and professional independence to make clinical judgments and manage uncomplicated pregnancies and births on their own authority. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is collaborative care necessary even though midwives practice autonomously?

options.A: Doctors usually prefer to handle all normal antenatal visits themselves
options.B: Midwives are not permitted by law to touch patients without a doctor's written note
options.C: Complications can develop suddenly, requiring rapid medical intervention and referral
options.D: Collaborative care eliminates the need to document clinical findings in registers

explanation: Because childbirth is dynamic and unpredictable, teamwork and established referral networks ensure high-risk cases receive advanced medical care without delay. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which regulatory body is legally empowered to control and supervise midwifery education and practice in Nigeria?

options.A: Federal Ministry of Women Affairs
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating education, setting standards, and licensing nursing and midwifery professionals across Nigeria. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h5)

question: A midwife continues to practice in a rural clinic despite her professional license having expired two years ago. What regulatory violation has occurred?

options.A: Violating patient confidentiality by discussing case notes publicly
options.B: Overstepping the collaborative referral boundary for normal deliveries
options.C: Failing to obtain informed consent before conducting a vaginal exam
options.D: Practicing illegally without a valid license from the NMCN

explanation: Operating with an expired license violates Nigerian health laws and subjects the practitioner to disciplinary action by the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary mission of the International Confederation of Midwives?

options.A: Funding community health clinics in developing nations
options.B: Licensing hospital administrators and maternity staff
options.C: Writing national nursing and medical school exams
options.D: Achieving safer childbirth for all women globally

explanation: The organization focuses its global efforts on ensuring safer childbirth and promoting quality midwifery care for every woman and newborn. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why does the ICM set international standards for midwifery education and practice?

options.A: To collect membership dues from registered practitioners
options.B: To replace local ministry of health laws entirely
options.C: To prevent doctors from working in maternity wards
options.D: To unify midwives worldwide under a shared professional vision

explanation: Global standards give midwives across different countries and cultures a common purpose and unified professional identity. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h1)

question: How many main categories structure the ICM Code of Ethics framework?

options.A: Ten
options.B: Two
options.C: Six
options.D: Four

explanation: The framework is organized into four distinct categories covering practice, relationships, the practice environment, and professional obligations. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h2)

question: A midwife working to improve poor hospital lighting and staff shortages in her unit is addressing which category of the ICM code?

options.A: Professional Obligations only
options.B: Midwifery Practice alone
options.C: The Midwife's Practice Environment
options.D: Personal Financial Management

explanation: Working conditions, safety, and operational resources fall directly under the practice environment category of the ethical code. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h2)

question: What does professional accountability primarily require a midwife to do?

options.A: Work independently without ever consulting doctors
options.B: Take responsibility for her clinical decisions and actions
options.C: Blame assistant staff when labor complications arise
options.D: Follow hospital traditions without questioning them

explanation: Accountability means owning one's clinical choices, acknowledging mistakes, and ensuring safe patient outcomes. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h3)

question: What action must a midwife take when faced with a clinical situation beyond her scope?

options.A: Seek immediate consultation or refer the patient
options.B: Attempt the procedure anyway to gain experience
options.C: Wait until the next morning shift begins
options.D: Send the patient home without telling anyone

explanation: Recognizing personal limits and seeking help promptly protects the mother and baby from potential harm. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h3)

question: What core principle guides the midwife's relationship with childbearing women according to the ICM?

options.A: Respect for human dignity and autonomy
options.B: Enforcement of uniform cultural practices
options.C: Strict obedience to hospital administrative rules
options.D: Complete financial control over medical bills

explanation: The code emphasizes treating every woman with dignity and honoring her right to make independent choices about her body and care. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is obtaining proper informed consent essential during maternity care?

options.A: It replaces the need for documenting vital signs on a chart
options.B: It legally protects the hospital from paying financial fines
options.C: It honors the woman's right to understand and choose her care
options.D: It shortened the overall duration of the first stage of labor

explanation: Informed consent is about respecting autonomy, ensuring the woman understands procedures, risks, and alternatives before agreeing. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is required for effective collaboration within an interprofessional healthcare team?

options.A: Strict subordination of midwives to senior physicians
options.B: Complete agreement on all personal political beliefs
options.C: Working separate shifts to avoid direct contact
options.D: Clear communication and mutual professional respect

explanation: Good teamwork depends on open, respectful communication and valuing what each professional contributes to patient care. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h5)

question: A doctor and a midwife disagree on the immediate management of a postpartum hemorrhage. What should guide the midwife's next action?

options.A: Waiting until the morning shift changes to decide
options.B: The safety and immediate clinical needs of the mother
options.C: Winning the argument to protect her professional pride
options.D: Ignoring the doctor completely and leaving the room

explanation: Patient safety is always the overriding priority during professional disagreements in clinical emergencies. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why does the ICM code require midwives to advocate for gender equality?

options.A: Because midwives are required to run for local political offices
options.B: Because poor social status and discrimination directly impact maternal health
options.C: Because hospitals require gender equality training certificates
options.D: Because gender issues are unrelated to clinical birth outcomes

explanation: Women who face discrimination and lack societal power experience higher rates of preventable maternal illness and death. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an expected advocacy role for a midwife under the ICM code?

options.A: Defending the human rights of vulnerable women
options.B: Speaking out against gender-based violence
options.C: Challenging harmful traditional pregnancy practices
options.D: Enforcing mandatory hospital fees for poor patients

explanation: Enforcing fees that block vulnerable women from care runs contrary to human rights advocacy; midwives should advocate for equitable access instead. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h6)

question: A student midwife in a rural Nigerian clinic notices a senior colleague shouting at a laboring woman for crying out. According to the ICM code, what should the student understand?

options.A: The student should ignore it because she is junior in rank
options.B: Verbal disrespect violates the core principle of treating women with dignity
options.C: Shouting is an accepted standard procedure in busy rural clinics
options.D: Only physical abuse is unethical, so shouting is acceptable

explanation: Respectful maternity care forbids verbal abuse or disrespect, regardless of how stressful or busy the clinical environment is. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h7)

question: How can Nigerian midwives best apply global ethical standards when working with limited medical supplies?

options.A: By charging patients high private fees for basic gauze and gloves
options.B: By refusing to work until the federal government supplies equipment
options.C: By abandoning evidence-based practices entirely in favor of guessing
options.D: By advocating for patients and delivering compassionate, resourceful care

explanation: Ethical practice under resource constraints involves maximizing safety, showing compassion, and advocating for systemic improvements. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T3#BMP211_U1_T3_h7)

question: Name the federal body responsible for regulating midwifery education and practice in Nigeria.

options.A: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.B: National Universities Commission
options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.D: Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria is the sole statutory body established by law to regulate the education and practice of nurses and midwives in the country. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary reason the NMCN sets and enforces standards for midwifery education and practice?

options.A: To reduce the number of private maternity clinics operating
options.B: To ensure midwives receive high salaries after graduation
options.C: To promote traditional birth attendants across rural communities
options.D: To safeguard and protect the health of the public

explanation: Every regulatory action taken by the Council ultimately aims to ensure safe, competent care for mothers and babies, thereby protecting the public. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following describes the independent legal scope of a registered midwife?

options.A: Prescribing any medication available in the national formulary
options.B: Performing major obstetric surgeries independently in community clinics
options.C: Treating severe medical diseases diagnosed during pregnancy
options.D: Managing normal pregnancy, childbirth, and the postnatal period

explanation: A registered midwife is specifically trained and legally authorized to independently manage uncomplicated pregnancies, normal deliveries, and postnatal care. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h2)

question: A midwife working in a primary health center notices a mother showing signs of prolonged, obstructed labor. What is the correct legal and professional action?

options.A: Attempt a vacuum extraction delivery despite lacking formal certification
options.B: Wait patiently at the clinic until the following morning to see if progress occurs
options.C: Promptly refer the patient to a higher-level facility with medical officers
options.D: Administer heavy doses of oxytocin to speed up the delivery immediately

explanation: Recognizing complications that fall outside the normal scope of practice and making a timely referral is a core legal and professional duty of a midwife. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is patient autonomy particularly important when providing antenatal and maternity care?

options.A: Pregnant women possess advanced medical degrees prior to admission
options.B: Women have the right to make informed choices regarding their own bodies and health
options.C: Hospital management requires written consent forms for statistical records
options.D: Midwives are legally absolved of all responsibility if a patient refuses treatment

explanation: Autonomy ensures that healthcare respects individual dignity by allowing mothers to participate actively in decisions affecting their pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following actions represents a direct violation of patient confidentiality by a midwife?

options.A: Discussing a patient's private diagnosis loudly with friends outside the ward
options.B: Documenting vital signs accurately inside the official patient medical record
options.C: Informing a nursing student about normal physiological changes in labor
options.D: Sharing emergency clinical details with the attending obstetrician on duty

explanation: Sharing private clinical information outside the circle of direct patient care breaches confidentiality and violates professional ethics. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of Continuing Professional Development (CPD) for registered midwives?

options.A: To increase hospital revenue through mandatory seminar registration fees
options.B: To ensure practitioners keep their knowledge updated with current evidence-based care
options.C: To determine who qualifies for promotion to a government directorate position
options.D: To replace the original midwifery training certificate after ten years of service

explanation: CPD programs help practicing midwives stay current with evolving clinical guidelines and medical advancements to improve maternal and child health outcomes. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h4)

question: A midwife continues to manage patients in a rural maternity clinic even though her practicing license expired six months ago. What is the status of this practice?

options.A: It is valid provided she pays her renewal fees by the end of the year
options.B: It is permitted if the local community leaders approve her work
options.C: It is acceptable as long as she completed her initial training
options.D: It is illegal and constitutes professional malpractice

explanation: Practicing without a current, valid license violates the NMCN Act and renders the practice illegal, regardless of past qualifications. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following bodies holds the legal authority to try registered midwives accused of professional misconduct in Nigeria?

options.A: National Industrial Court of Nigeria
options.B: Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals
options.C: Local Government Health Service Commission
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Disciplinary Tribunal

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Disciplinary Tribunal is the statutory body empowered to investigate and judge cases of professional misconduct among practitioners. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following actions is classified as professional misconduct for a registered midwife?

options.A: Abandoning a woman in active labor to attend to personal business
options.B: Recording maternal vital signs every thirty minutes during first stage labor
options.C: Consulting an obstetrician regarding an abnormal fetal heart rate
options.D: Attending an accredited CPD workshop to earn license renewal points

explanation: Leaving a woman unattended during critical stages of labor constitutes severe negligence and professional misconduct. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T4#BMP211_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary philosophy behind midwife-led care models during normal pregnancy and birth?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on postpartum infant nutrition rather than maternal health
options.B: Treating all pregnancies as high-risk events requiring immediate surgical readiness
options.C: Ensuring a medical doctor is present at every single antenatal booking visit
options.D: Viewing childbirth as a normal physiological process needing little intervention

explanation: Midwife-led care assumes pregnancy is natural and healthy, stepping in with medical interventions only when clear complications develop. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is seeing a familiar midwife throughout pregnancy particularly beneficial for a mother?

options.A: It eliminates the need to ever perform routine blood pressure checks
options.B: It builds trust and helps the midwife notice subtle changes early
options.C: It legally transfers all hospital liability directly to the patient
options.D: It guarantees she will never experience any physical pain during labor

explanation: When a woman sees the same midwife regularly, trust grows, making her more comfortable sharing worries and allowing the midwife to spot warning signs faster. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following describes the principle of woman-centred care?

options.A: Following strict hospital routines regardless of individual patient wishes
options.B: Placing the mother's personal values and needs at the center of decisions
options.C: Allowing the obstetrician to make all final choices without patient input
options.D: Prioritizing hospital administrative efficiency over maternal comfort

explanation: Woman-centred care means respecting the unique background, beliefs, and choices of the mother rather than forcing a one-size-fits-all routine. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h2)

question: How does protecting physiological norms differ from immediate medical intervention in labor?

options.A: It focuses solely on managing postpartum hemorrhage after the placenta is out
options.B: It relies first on non-pharmacological comfort measures before artificial medical steps
options.C: It requires immediate surgical delivery for every primigravida mother
options.D: It bans the use of skilled birth attendants during the second stage of labor

explanation: Protecting physiological norms means supporting natural labor processes using positioning, movement, and support before jumping into drugs or surgery. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is a well-documented clinical benefit of midwife-led continuity of care for low-risk women?

options.A: Lower rates of regional analgesia and episiotomies
options.B: Total elimination of newborn resuscitation needs
options.C: Increased need for pharmaceutical pain relief
options.D: Higher rates of routine cesarean sections

explanation: Studies consistently show that women with continuous midwifery support experience fewer medical interventions like episiotomies and epidurals. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h3)

question: A first-time mother expresses deep fear of a traumatic hospital birth. Based on research findings, what emotional outcome is she more likely to experience under a continuous midwife-led model?

options.A: Total emotional detachment from her newborn
options.B: Reduced risk of birth trauma and anxiety
options.C: Severe chronic postnatal depression
options.D: Immediate rejection of breastfeeding support

explanation: Familiarity and continuous support significantly lower anxiety and reduce the psychological trauma often associated with fragmented hospital care. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is a key feature of the caseload midwifery model?

options.A: Midwives work strictly rotating eight-hour shifts with no on-call responsibilities
options.B: Care is handed over to a new doctor at every single antenatal appointment
options.C: A primary midwife follows a defined group of women across the entire maternity cycle
options.D: A large pool of fifty practitioners manages a single patient's antenatal card

explanation: Caseload midwifery pairs a primary midwife with a specific set of clients to provide end-to-end care throughout pregnancy, birth, and the postnatal period. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why might a healthcare facility choose team midwifery over individual caseload midwifery?

options.A: To completely eliminate antenatal booking visits for new mothers
options.B: To ensure that the mother never sees the same practitioner twice
options.C: To provide better work-life balance and protect midwives from burnout
options.D: To force all pregnant women to undergo scheduled surgical deliveries

explanation: Team models share the on-call burden among several midwives, reducing the exhaustion and burnout common in sole caseload arrangements. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system is considered the ideal grassroots setting for midwife-led care?

options.A: Private specialist eye clinics
options.B: Tertiary teaching hospitals
options.C: National medical research institutes
options.D: Primary health care centres

explanation: Primary health care centres are situated directly within communities, making them the frontline access point for grassroots midwifery services. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h5)

question: What common perception among many urban Nigerian women complicates the acceptance of midwife-led care?

options.A: Demanding home births without any skilled birth attendants present
options.B: Refusing to attend any form of antenatal care during the first trimester
options.C: Believing that high-technology obstetric care in big hospitals is always superior
options.D: Believing that traditional birth attendants are always safer than hospitals

explanation: Many urban clients equate heavy medical technology with safety, sometimes viewing physiological midwife-led care as inferior or outdated. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is a common professional barrier faced when introducing midwife-led care models?

options.A: Universal agreement among doctors to handle all normal births
options.B: Interprofessional friction and misunderstanding of midwifery scope
options.C: Mandatory retirement age of twenty-five for all practicing midwives
options.D: Complete lack of pregnant women willing to use maternity services

explanation: Resistance from medical colleagues who misunderstand midwifery autonomy is a frequent hurdle when establishing these care models. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is interprofessional education important for resolving conflicts between doctors and midwives?

options.A: It teaches midwives how to perform major caesarean sections independently
options.B: It trains them together to build mutual respect and collaborative teamwork
options.C: It forces midwives to give up their clinical license to medical boards
options.D: It replaces practical clinical training with online theoretical lectures

explanation: Learning alongside each other helps medical and midwifery students understand and value each other's distinct professional roles. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T5#BMP211_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of taking an obstetric history during an antenatal visit?

options.A: To diagnose all genetic disorders present in the family
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of the hospital delivery
options.C: To fulfill mandatory administrative paperwork for the hospital
options.D: To gather health information and guide clinical care

explanation: History taking systematically collects past and present health details so the midwife can provide safe, individualized care throughout pregnancy. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is a thorough obstetric history especially important in busy primary health clinics?

options.A: It prevents the need for referral to a tertiary hospital.
options.B: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations.
options.C: It guarantees that the mother will experience a completely pain-free labour.
options.D: It helps identify potential complications early when resources are limited.

explanation: When diagnostic equipment or advanced specialists are scarce, a detailed history acts as an essential early warning tool for risks. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which practice helps create a safe, welcoming space for a pregnant woman during the interview?

options.A: Insisting that she speaks only English during the interview
options.B: Maintaining strict confidentiality and treating her respectfully
options.C: Rushing through the questions to save time for other patients
options.D: Involving extended family members in every intimate detail

explanation: Respectful care and privacy build trust, encouraging the woman to share accurate and complete health information. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h2)

question: A pregnant teenager is quiet and hesitates to answer questions about her past health. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Scold her for being uncooperative to get faster results
options.B: Stop the interview entirely and send her home
options.C: Threaten to report her behavior to the hospital management
options.D: Reassure her of confidentiality and use a gentle, non-judgmental tone

explanation: Anxious or hesitant patients need reassurance and a warm, non-judgmental approach to feel safe enough to open up. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which past surgery is especially critical to note because it increases the risk of uterine rupture?

options.A: Tonsillectomy done five years ago
options.B: Appendectomy performed during childhood
options.C: Previous myomectomy or caesarean section
options.D: Repair of a simple hand laceration

explanation: Surgeries that cut into the muscular wall of the uterus weaken the tissue, raising the risk that the uterus could rupture during a future labour. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why do midwives ask pregnant women about taking traditional herbal remedies?

options.A: Traditional herbs are always provided free of charge by local healers.
options.B: Hospital regulations require patients to sell herbs on hospital grounds.
options.C: Some herbal mixtures can stimulate uterine contractions or harm the foetus.
options.D: Herbs have no chemical effects on the human body.

explanation: Many local herbs are pharmacologically active and can cause dangerous side effects, such as premature uterine contractions or toxicity. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h3)

question: What does the term 'Gravida' mean in maternity care?

options.A: The total number of living male children born
options.B: The number of children currently living at home
options.C: The total number of times a woman has been pregnant
options.D: The number of deliveries that reached 28 weeks

explanation: Gravidity counts every pregnancy a woman has experienced, regardless of how long it lasted or how it ended, including her current pregnancy. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h4)

question: A woman is pregnant for the third time. Her first pregnancy was a miscarriage at 10 weeks, and her second resulted in a healthy live birth at 39 weeks. What is her Gravida and Parity (using 28 weeks as the threshold)?

options.A: Gravida 3, Parity 2
options.B: Gravida 1, Parity 3
options.C: Gravida 2, Parity 2
options.D: Gravida 3, Parity 1

explanation: She has been pregnant three times total (Gravida 3). Only one pregnancy reached the threshold of 28 weeks (Parity 1), while the first was a miscarriage. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which detail is needed to calculate the Estimated Due Date using Naegele's rule?

options.A: The blood pressure reading taken at booking
options.B: The date when the woman first felt foetal movement
options.C: The date of the last normal menstrual period
options.D: The weight of the woman during her first trimester

explanation: Naegele's rule adds seven days to the first day of the last menstrual period and subtracts three months to estimate the delivery date. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is asking about the date of 'quickening' (first baby movements) helpful during an antenatal visit?

options.A: It is the only legal method allowed to confirm a viable pregnancy.
options.B: It provides a secondary way to cross-check and estimate gestational age.
options.C: It stops the mother from experiencing morning sickness in later months.
options.D: It accurately predicts the exact day labour will spontaneously begin.

explanation: Quickening usually occurs around 18 to 20 weeks in a first pregnancy (and slightly earlier in subsequent ones), helping confirm or question the LMP estimate. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which symptom during pregnancy is a major warning sign for severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Increased appetite during the second trimester
options.B: Mild swelling of the fingers in hot weather
options.C: Severe headache and blurred vision
options.D: Occasional mild heartburn after eating spicy food

explanation: Persistent severe headaches and visual disturbances are classic warning signs of central nervous system involvement in severe pre-eclampsia. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h6)

question: A pregnant woman at 32 weeks says she has not felt her baby kick all day. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Immediately assess foetal heart rate and investigate foetal well-being
options.B: Tell her not to worry and send her home to rest
options.C: Advise her to wait until the next scheduled antenatal clinic date
options.D: Prescribe local herbal teas to stimulate foetal activity

explanation: Reduced or absent foetal movements is a critical warning sign that requires urgent evaluation of foetal viability and well-being. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of keeping clear, accurate records in maternity care?

options.A: It prevents the woman from changing her mind about her birth plan.
options.B: It allows the hospital to charge higher fees for delivery services.
options.C: It ensures safe continuity of care across different healthcare providers.
options.D: It completely eliminates the need to talk to the pregnant woman.

explanation: Accurate records allow any midwife or doctor taking over care to instantly understand the woman's history, current status, and identified risks. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h7)

question: What does the communication tool SBAR help midwives do during a handover?

options.A: It measures the exact blood loss during a postpartum haemorrhage.
options.B: It replaces all physical medical files with digital voice recordings.
options.C: It provides a structured and concise way to relay critical patient information.
options.D: It forces the patient to diagnose her own medical condition.

explanation: SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation) organizes thoughts and data so important clinical details are never missed during staff handovers. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T1#BMP211_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the main reason for routine antenatal visits during pregnancy?

options.A: Treat chronic health conditions before birth
options.B: Prescribe routine antibiotics to prevent infections
options.C: Find out the exact day labor will start
options.D: Track normal body changes and catch problems early

explanation: Routine antenatal visits allow midwives to monitor normal body changes and spot warning signs before they become emergencies. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why do midwives take a patient history and do a physical check at every antenatal visit?

options.A: To check for genetic issues in the first trimester
options.B: To replace the need for lab tests
options.C: To fill out clinic paperwork
options.D: To get a complete picture of mother and baby health

explanation: Combining history and physical checks gives the midwife complete information to keep both mother and baby safe. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why should a pregnant woman empty her bladder right before an abdominal check?

options.A: It stops urinary tract infections during the exam
options.B: A full bladder causes discomfort and gets in the way of feeling the tummy
options.C: Urine samples are needed for every single physical check
options.D: An empty bladder makes the baby's heart beat faster

explanation: A full bladder pushes the uterus up and makes feeling the tummy difficult or painful. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h2)

question: A patient looks nervous and hesitates to lie down for her abdominal check. What should you do first?

options.A: Ask another midwife to take over
options.B: Tell her to lie down right away to save time
options.C: Explain the check simply and ask for her permission
options.D: Skip the tummy check and only check blood pressure

explanation: Clear communication and asking for consent help reduce fear and build trust between you and the mother. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h2)

question: When checking a pregnant woman's eyes and palms, what active sign is a midwife looking for?

options.A: Blue skin showing heart trouble
options.B: Yellow skin showing liver trouble
options.C: Pale skin showing low blood levels
options.D: Swelling showing fluid retention

explanation: The inner eyelids and palms are good places to spot pale areas linked to low blood levels, or anaemia. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why is checking vital signs like blood pressure so important at every visit?

options.A: It helps screen for dangerous blood pressure issues like pre-eclampsia
options.B: It shows how many weeks pregnant the woman is
options.C: It measures how fast the placenta is growing
options.D: It tracks what the mother eats every day

explanation: Rising blood pressure is often the earliest warning sign of hypertensive problems in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why do midwives place a small wedge under the right hip of a pregnant woman during an abdominal exam?

options.A: To keep her spine straight and comfortable
options.B: To push the baby's head deeper into the pelvis
options.C: To stop low blood pressure by moving the heavy uterus off major blood vessels
options.D: To make the dark belly line easier to see

explanation: Tilting the pelvis slightly to the left keeps the uterus off major blood vessels, keeping the mother's circulation steady. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h4)

question: What happens when a pregnant woman lies flat on her back for too long without a hip tilt?

options.A: Leg blood flow increases and causes cramps
options.B: The baby stops moving completely
options.C: The heavy uterus presses on major blood vessels and lowers blood pressure
options.D: Her breathing becomes very deep and easy

explanation: Pressure on the main blood vessels reduces blood return to the heart, making the mother dizzy and lowering blood flow to the baby. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the dark line that runs down the middle of a pregnant belly called?

options.A: Pregnancy mask
options.B: Linea nigra
options.C: White line
options.D: Stretch marks

explanation: Pregnancy hormones often cause the skin down the middle of the belly to darken, which is called linea nigra. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why does a midwife check the belly for old surgical scars before feeling the tummy?

options.A: To check for past operations like a previous caesarean section
options.B: To measure how thick the belly fat is
options.C: To guess how much weight the mother will gain
options.D: To find out the sex of the baby

explanation: Past scars warn the midwife about risks like uterine weakness or unusual placental attachment. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h5)

question: Around how many weeks of pregnancy are Leopold's maneuvers usually reliable for feeling the baby's position?

options.A: 24 weeks
options.B: 12 weeks
options.C: 16 weeks
options.D: 20 weeks

explanation: Before 24 weeks, the baby is too small compared to the amount of water around it, making it hard to feel positions clearly. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which maneuver is used to check if the baby's presenting part has moved down into the pelvic brim?

options.A: Lateral maneuver
options.B: First pelvic maneuver
options.C: Second pelvic maneuver
options.D: Fundal maneuver

explanation: The second pelvic maneuver involves facing the mother's feet to check how far the baby has moved down into the pelvis. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the normal resting range for a baby's heart rate?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 80 to 120 beats per minute
options.C: 140 to 180 beats per minute
options.D: 110 to 160 beats per minute

explanation: A healthy resting baby's heart rate normally falls between 110 and 160 beats per minute. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h7)

question: While listening to the baby's heart with a Pinard stethoscope, you notice the beats match the mother's pulse. What should you do?

options.A: Call for an emergency delivery right away
options.B: Move the stethoscope to find the baby's back and count again
options.C: Record it as a normal baby heart rate
options.D: Assume the baby is sleeping and try again tomorrow

explanation: Matching the mother's pulse means you are hearing her blood flow through the placenta, not the baby's actual heartbeat. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which measurement is essential to record when tracking baby growth during a tummy check?

options.A: Size around the mother's hips
options.B: Thickness of the belly skinfold
options.C: Total weight gain in pounds
options.D: Fundal height in centimeters

explanation: Measuring fundal height in centimeters matches up closely with weeks of pregnancy and helps track normal baby growth. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h8)

question: Why is it important to compare today's belly check with past antenatal records?

options.A: To figure out how many calories the mother needs to eat
options.B: To prove you finished all required clinic paperwork
options.C: To track steady baby growth and spot warning signs early
options.D: To calculate the exact date of conception

explanation: Checking measurements over time reveals growth trends and fluid levels much better than just a single check. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T2#BMP211_U2_T2_h8)

question: At approximately what gestational age do midwives routinely begin performing formal abdominal palpation maneuvers?

options.A: 24 weeks
options.B: 16 weeks
options.C: 36 weeks
options.D: 12 weeks

explanation: By 24 weeks of gestation, the uterus has grown well above the pelvis and fetal parts are large enough to be clearly distinguished through the abdominal wall. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why is it important for the pregnant woman to empty her bladder just before abdominal palpation?

options.A: An empty bladder prevents uterine contractions
options.B: A full bladder pushes the uterus upward and alters findings
options.C: A full bladder blocks the maternal pulse
options.D: An empty bladder lowers the maternal blood pressure

explanation: A distended bladder displaces the uterus superiorly, which can lead to false readings when measuring fundal height and assessing fetal position. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h1)

question: Where is the upper mark of the tape measure placed when measuring fundal height?

options.A: The center of the maternal umbilicus
options.B: The top of the pubic symphysis
options.C: The base of the xiphisternum
options.D: The highest point of the uterine fundus

explanation: Fundal height is measured by stretching a tape from the pubic symphysis up to the highest point of the uterine fundus. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h2)

question: A woman at 30 weeks gestation has a measured fundal height of 25 centimeters. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Advise her to increase her daily fluid intake
options.B: Schedule her immediately for a repeat delivery date
options.C: Investigate further for potential growth restriction
options.D: Reassure her that this is completely normal

explanation: A fundal height measurement that lags behind gestational age by more than two centimeters suggests slow fetal growth and requires clinical follow-up. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h2)

question: What term describes a fetal lie where the spine of the baby runs across the maternal abdomen at a right angle?

options.A: Oblique lie
options.B: Longitudinal lie
options.C: Transverse lie
options.D: Compound lie

explanation: In a transverse lie, the long axis of the fetus is perpendicular to the long axis of the mother. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is an oblique lie considered clinically significant during late pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents the mother from feeling fetal movements
options.B: It usually causes severe maternal hypertension
options.C: It is an unstable orientation that often shifts before labor
options.D: It guarantees that the infant will present feet first

explanation: An oblique lie is typically unstable and tends to convert into either a longitudinal or transverse lie once contractions begin. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which specific grip is used during the third Leopold's maneuver to check the presenting part above the pubic symphysis?

options.A: Lateral grip
options.B: Fundal grip
options.C: Pawlik's grip
options.D: Pelvic grip

explanation: Pawlik's grip involves using a single hand just above the symphysis pubis to grasp and evaluate the lower fetal pole. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h4)

question: How does a fetal head feel during abdominal palpation compared to the breech?

options.A: Softer and rounder
options.B: Harder and more distinct
options.C: Irregular with no clear borders
options.D: Larger and spongier

explanation: The fetal head feels hard, round, and movable, whereas the breech feels softer, broader, and less clearly defined. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which anatomical structure serves as the denominator when the fetus is in a vertex presentation?

options.A: The occiput
options.B: The mentum
options.C: The acromion
options.D: The sacrum

explanation: In a vertex presentation, the occiput is the reference point used to define the fetal position within the maternal pelvis. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing the second Leopold's maneuver?

options.A: To check if the amniotic fluid volume is normal
options.B: To measure the exact length of the uterine fundus
options.C: To locate the firm fetal back and small parts
options.D: To confirm that the head has entered the pelvic brim

explanation: The second maneuver involves palpating the lateral walls of the uterus to determine which side holds the fetal back and which holds the limbs, identifying the position. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which directional position does the midwife face when performing the fourth Leopold's maneuver?

options.A: Facing the mother's head
options.B: Standing at her right side
options.C: Standing at her left side
options.D: Facing the mother's feet

explanation: For the fourth maneuver, the midwife turns to face the pregnant woman's feet to assess the descent of the presenting part into the pelvis. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h6)

question: During abdominal palpation, a midwife feels four fifths of the fetal head above the pubic symphysis. What does this finding indicate?

options.A: The fetal head is unengaged and floating
options.B: The amniotic fluid is severely reduced
options.C: The fetal head is fully engaged
options.D: The fetus is lying in a transverse position

explanation: When four or five fifths of the head remain palpable above the brim, the head has not yet entered the pelvic inlet and remains floating. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT required when documenting routine abdominal palpation findings?

options.A: Fetal engagement status
options.B: Fetal lie and presentation
options.C: Fundal height in centimeters
options.D: Maternal blood glucose level

explanation: Routine palpation documents physical findings like fundal height, lie, presentation, position, and engagement, but not blood glucose levels. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is timely and clear documentation of palpation findings critical in midwifery practice?

options.A: It replaces the need for any ultrasound examinations
options.B: It ensures safe communication and continuity of care among staff
options.C: It prevents the mother from feeling anxious during labor
options.D: It guarantees that labor will progress without complications

explanation: Clear documentation allows all healthcare providers to track the ongoing well-being and growth of the fetus accurately. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T3#BMP211_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of fetal heart auscultation during labor?

options.A: To determine the exact gestational age
options.B: To confirm the presence of twin pregnancy
options.C: To measure the exact weight of the baby
options.D: To detect early signs of fetal distress

explanation: Listening to the fetal heart allows midwives to spot potential oxygen shortages early so they can act quickly. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why do basic auscultation tools remain vital in many Nigerian primary health clinics?

options.A: They are cost-effective and do not rely on electricity
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for antenatal visits
options.C: They provide more accurate readings than modern machines
options.D: They measure the exact blood pressure of the mother

explanation: Tools like the Pinard stethoscope work without batteries or grid power, making them dependable in low-resource settings. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h1)

question: Where is the fetal heart sound usually heard best when the baby is in a normal vertex position?

options.A: High up in the upper right abdominal quadrant
options.B: In the lower abdominal quadrant below the umbilicus
options.C: Exclusively on the right flank of the mother
options.D: Directly over the maternal xiphisternum

explanation: In a vertex presentation, the fetal back faces forward and downward, placing the maximum heart sound below the navel. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h2)

question: A midwife performs abdominal palpation and finds the fetal head in the fundus and the breech near the pelvis. Where should she place her stethoscope?

options.A: In the right or left lower quadrant
options.B: Deep in the right iliac fossa
options.C: Directly over the symphysis pubis
options.D: At or above the level of the umbilicus

explanation: When a baby is in a breech position, the chest and heart are positioned higher up in the maternal abdomen. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h2)

question: What critical action must a midwife take after placing the Pinard stethoscope on the mother's abdomen?

options.A: Secure the wide end tightly with adhesive tape
options.B: Remove their fingers from the bell of the stethoscope
options.C: Blow gently into the narrow end to clear dust
options.D: Apply warm ultrasound gel over the wide flared end

explanation: Holding the bell with fingers can pick up the maternal pulse or dampen the soft fetal heart sounds. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is it necessary to feel the mother's pulse while listening with a Pinard stethoscope?

options.A: To determine if the mother is experiencing uterine contractions
options.B: To calculate the exact body mass index of the pregnant woman
options.C: To make sure the midwife is not mistaking maternal pulse for the fetal heartbeat
options.D: To assess whether the mother has a normal blood pressure reading

explanation: The maternal pulse rate can sometimes match the rate heard through the abdomen, so simultaneous palpation rules out confusion. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of applying gel when using a Doppler ultrasound?

options.A: To cool down the warm surface of the electronic probe
options.B: To eliminate air pockets and help sound waves travel
options.C: To permanently stick the transducer to the skin
options.D: To disinfect the maternal abdominal skin surface

explanation: Ultrasound waves do not travel well through air, so gel creates a smooth pathway from the probe to the skin. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which factor distinguishes a Doppler monitor from a traditional Pinard stethoscope?

options.A: The Doppler converts sound wave frequency shifts into an audible electronic signal
options.B: The Doppler can only be used during the first trimester of pregnancy
options.C: The Doppler relies entirely on human bone conduction to work
options.D: The Doppler requires no power source or maintenance whatsoever

explanation: Dopplers use electronic sensors and speakers to amplify movement, whereas Pinards rely purely on acoustic physics. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which of the following is an advantage of the Pinard stethoscope over the Doppler device?

options.A: It detects fetal heart tones much earlier in pregnancy
options.B: It automatically calculates the numerical heart rate
options.C: It requires no special training or abdominal palpation
options.D: It never requires batteries or electrical power

explanation: The Pinard is completely mechanical, making it immune to power failures or dead batteries in low-resource settings. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of using a Doppler ultrasound?

options.A: It is helpful when the mother has a high BMI
options.B: It works without any source of electrical power
options.C: It produces an audible sound for the room to hear
options.D: It provides quick detection of fetal heart sounds

explanation: Doppler devices depend on batteries or electrical charging to operate. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the normal baseline range for a fetal heart rate in beats per minute?

options.A: 110 to 160 beats per minute
options.B: 140 to 180 beats per minute
options.C: 80 to 120 beats per minute
options.D: 60 to 100 beats per minute

explanation: A healthy resting fetal heart rate falls within the 110 to 160 beats per minute range. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h6)

question: When is the best time for a midwife to count the fetal heart rate during active labor?

options.A: Strictly while a contraction is peaking
options.B: Immediately after a contraction ends
options.C: Right before the membranes rupture
options.D: Only when the mother pushes to deliver

explanation: Counting right after a contraction helps the midwife identify late decelerations and recovery patterns safely. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h6)

question: What vital detail must be included when documenting fetal heart auscultation in a partograph?

options.A: The exact weight of the placenta
options.B: The exact baseline rate and rhythm
options.C: The color of the coupling gel used
options.D: The brand name of the Doppler device

explanation: Clear documentation requires precise numerical values and rhythm status to track fetal well-being over time. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why is writing vague statements like 'heart sound normal' discouraged in midwifery records?

options.A: It prevents the mother from reading her file
options.B: It causes the hospital to buy more stationery
options.C: It lacks specific, legally defensible clinical data
options.D: It takes too much time to write on paper

explanation: Specific numbers are required to prove that fetal surveillance was performed correctly and safely. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T4#BMP211_U2_T4_h7)

question: What part of the reproductive system does a midwife check during a vaginal exam to see how labor is progressing?

options.A: The cervix
options.B: The clitoris
options.C: The uterine fundus
options.D: The fallopian tubes

explanation: Measuring how much the cervix has opened helps midwives track how labor is advancing. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do midwives often prefer a vaginal exam over an ultrasound during active labor?

options.A: It provides a clear visual image of the internal pelvic organs on a screen
options.B: It completely eliminates the risk of introducing bacteria into the uterus
options.C: It gives immediate physical feel of cervical opening and baby descent
options.D: It is completely painless for every woman

explanation: Direct physical touch allows the midwife to quickly feel the cervix and the baby right at the bedside. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h1)

question: How often is a vaginal exam usually recommended during normal labor to help prevent infection?

options.A: Every 8 hours
options.B: Every 30 minutes
options.C: Every 4 hours
options.D: Only once at admission

explanation: Limiting exams to every four hours balances monitoring progress while keeping infection risks low. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h2)

question: A student wants to check a laboring woman's cervix every hour to see how fast it is opening. What is the best response?

options.A: Approve the plan because frequent checks ensure absolute safety
options.B: Replace all internal checks with abdominal palpation permanently
options.C: Suggest checking every 15 minutes for better accuracy
options.D: Modify the plan because unnecessary frequent checks increase infection risk

explanation: Too many internal exams introduce bacteria into the birth canal without offering extra medical benefit. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which situation requires an emergency vaginal exam during labor?

options.A: Suspected umbilical cord prolapse
options.B: General patient anxiety about labor pain
options.C: Routine documentation update at midnight
options.D: Routine shift change handover

explanation: A cord prolapse is an emergency that requires immediate internal assessment and action to protect the baby. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h3)

question: Why is a vaginal exam done right after the water breaks if the baby's head was high?

options.A: To artificially speed up contractions
options.B: To measure the remaining amniotic fluid
options.C: To close the cervical os tightly
options.D: To check for umbilical cord descent or prolapse

explanation: When amniotic fluid rushes out, the cord can slip down beside the baby's head and cut off oxygen. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which condition means a routine vaginal exam should NOT be performed?

options.A: Occiput posterior fetal position
options.B: Mild gestational hypertension
options.C: Placenta praevia
options.D: Premature rupture of membranes at term

explanation: Touching a low-lying placenta with examining fingers can cause severe, dangerous bleeding for the mother. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the main danger of doing a vaginal exam on a woman with unexplained late pregnancy bleeding?

options.A: It always causes immediate fetal demise within minutes
options.B: It permanently stops all future uterine contractions
options.C: It can trigger heavy bleeding by disturbing the placenta
options.D: It changes the baby's genetic presentation

explanation: Inserting fingers blindly when bleeding is present risks tearing placental tissue near the cervix. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h4)

question: In which direction should the vulva be cleaned with antiseptic before a vaginal exam?

options.A: In any random direction as long as soap is used
options.B: From front to back
options.C: In a circular outward motion starting from the anus
options.D: From back to front

explanation: Wiping from front to back prevents bacteria from the anal area from reaching the vaginal opening. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the most important action a midwife takes to prevent infection during a vaginal exam?

options.A: Using a bright overhead examination light
options.B: Using sterile gloves and proper hand hygiene
options.C: Asking the woman to empty her bladder fully
options.D: Warming the examination room to room temperature

explanation: Clean barrier protection and hand hygiene stop outside germs from entering the birth canal. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h5)

question: What must a midwife always secure before starting a vaginal exam?

options.A: Clearance from the hospital finance department
options.B: Informed consent from the patient
options.C: Written approval from the hospital director
options.D: Permission from the senior medical officer on duty

explanation: Every woman has the right to understand and agree to any physical procedure performed on her body. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is explaining each step of a vaginal exam out loud to the patient so important?

options.A: It legally protects the hospital from all future lawsuits
options.B: It helps reduce anxiety and builds trust between the midwife and the woman
options.C: It speeds up the rate at which the cervix opens up
options.D: It ensures that medical students outside the room can take notes

explanation: Talking the patient through the procedure removes the fear of the unknown and gives her a sense of control. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T5#BMP211_U2_T5_h6)

question: What type of energy does an ultrasound machine use to create images inside the uterus?

options.A: Sound waves
options.B: Ionizing radiation
options.C: Magnetic fields
options.D: Thermal infrared rays

explanation: Ultrasound technology uses high-frequency sound waves rather than harmful radiation, making it completely safe for regular use in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is ultrasound considered safer than X-rays for monitoring a pregnant woman?

options.A: It does not use ionizing radiation
options.B: It requires no electrical power source
options.C: It completely eliminates all false positive results
options.D: It provides color images of internal organs

explanation: Because ultrasound relies on harmless sound waves instead of ionizing radiation, it poses no known radiation risk to the developing fetus. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h1)

question: What specific measurement provides the most accurate estimation of gestational age during the first trimester?

options.A: Biparietal Diameter
options.B: Abdominal Circumference
options.C: Crown-Rump Length
options.D: Femur Length

explanation: Crown-Rump Length is the standard measurement used in early pregnancy to date the gestation accurately before natural variations in fetal growth become significant. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h2)

question: A woman comes to the clinic at 10 weeks gestation for her first scan. What is the primary clinical goal of this early ultrasound?

options.A: Confirm fetal viability and establish an accurate due date
options.B: Determine the exact sex of the baby
options.C: Check the maturity of the fetal lungs
options.D: Measure the exact birth weight of the baby

explanation: First-trimester scans focus heavily on checking for a heartbeat, confirming the location of the pregnancy, and dating the gestation precisely. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h2)

question: Around what gestational age is the detailed mid-pregnancy anomaly scan usually performed?

options.A: 18 to 22 weeks
options.B: 12 to 14 weeks
options.C: 6 to 8 weeks
options.D: 36 to 40 weeks

explanation: The structural anomaly scan is best performed between 18 and 22 weeks because internal organs are large enough to be clearly visualized. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why do midwives monitor fetal biometry measurements like femur length and abdominal circumference in the third trimester?

options.A: To detect chromosomal abnormalities like Down syndrome
options.B: To measure the strength of uterine contractions
options.C: To calculate the exact date of conception
options.D: To estimate fetal weight and check growth patterns

explanation: Biometric measurements taken later in pregnancy help healthcare providers determine if the baby is growing at a normal and healthy rate. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the medical term for an abnormally low volume of amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus?

options.A: Polyhydramnios
options.B: Placenta previa
options.C: Oligohydramnios
options.D: Hydrops fetalis

explanation: Oligohydramnios describes a reduced volume of amniotic fluid, which can indicate placental insufficiency or fetal urinary tract issues. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h4)

question: An ultrasound report shows that the placenta is covering the internal cervical os at 36 weeks. What management plan does this support?

options.A: Discharging the patient until term
options.B: Planning for a Caesarean section due to placenta previa
options.C: Prescribing iron supplements for anemia
options.D: Recommending immediate induction of labor

explanation: A low-lying placenta that covers the cervix at term prevents safe vaginal birth and requires a planned Caesarean section to avoid severe bleeding. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why is a full bladder often recommended for a transabdominal scan during early pregnancy?

options.A: It prevents the patient from feeling dizzy during the test
options.B: It stimulates active fetal movements for easier counting
options.C: It pushes the uterus upward for better visualization
options.D: It measures the exact renal function of the mother

explanation: A full urinary bladder acts as an acoustic window and elevates the early pregnant uterus out of the pelvic cavity so the sonographer can see it clearly. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h5)

question: What is an essential responsibility of the midwife when preparing a patient for an obstetric ultrasound?

options.A: Performing the complete anatomical scan independently
options.B: Diagnosing complex congenital heart diseases
options.C: Administering local anesthesia to the abdominal wall
options.D: Explaining the procedure and addressing any anxiety or questions

explanation: Midwives play a crucial counseling role by preparing women emotionally, clarifying why the test is done, and managing expectations. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h5)

question: What safety principle guides healthcare providers to use the lowest possible ultrasound exposure necessary to get a diagnosis?

options.A: EDD
options.B: ALARA
options.C: BMI
options.D: APGAR

explanation: The ALARA principle stands for As Low As Reasonably Achievable, ensuring patients are not exposed to unnecessary ultrasound energy. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h6)

question: What does it mean when medical professionals say that obstetric ultrasound is operator-dependent?

options.A: The equipment will only function if plugged into a specialized hospital generator
options.B: The machine requires a licensed electrical engineer to operate it during emergencies
options.C: The results can be interpreted automatically by the computer without human review
options.D: The accuracy of the results depends heavily on the skill and training of the person performing the scan

explanation: Because the operator manually guides the probe and interprets the live images, operator skill directly influences whether structures are correctly identified. [learn more](BMP211_U2_T6#BMP211_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which germ is commonly linked to postpartum infections and wound issues in maternity wards?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.B: Corynebacterium diphtheriae
options.C: Staphylococcus aureus
options.D: Plasmodium falciparum

explanation: Staphylococcus aureus is a frequent hospital germ that easily infects surgical cuts and reproductive organs after childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why are new mothers and babies so easily prone to infections in the hospital?

options.A: They spend less time sleeping compared to other hospital patients
options.B: Delivery creates open wounds and newborn immune systems are immature
options.C: Hospital rooms are kept at much colder temperatures than homes
options.D: They consume a specialized diet that increases bacterial growth

explanation: Open wounds from delivery and the baby's developing immune system give germs an easy way to enter and spread. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main rule behind standard infection control in the delivery room?

options.A: Healthy women from rural areas carry zero pathogenic bacteria
options.B: Infection risks disappear once the third stage of labour is completed
options.C: All patients and body fluids are treated as potentially infectious
options.D: Only patients with visible fevers require barrier nursing care

explanation: Standard precautions mean treating every patient's blood and fluids as infectious because screening tests do not catch every single germ. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h2)

question: How do infection control rules protect both the mother and baby at the same time?

options.A: By replacing physical examinations with remote digital monitoring
options.B: By ensuring all patients receive prophylactic broad-spectrum antibiotics
options.C: By isolating every mother in a private room for fourteen days
options.D: By breaking the chain of transmission between reservoirs and susceptible hosts

explanation: Stopping the chain of infection keeps germs from traveling from sources to vulnerable people on the ward. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is considered the single most important action to stop hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Wearing sterile boots
options.B: Proper hand hygiene
options.C: Routine floor mopping
options.D: Daily linen changes

explanation: Frequent and correct handwashing or using alcohol rub removes surface germs from the skin, greatly lowering cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why are midwives in the delivery suite told not to wear artificial nails or rings?

options.A: They can accidentally scratch the delicate skin of the newborn
options.B: They make it difficult to feel subtle changes in fetal heart rates
options.C: They trap microorganisms and prevent effective hand cleansing
options.D: They react negatively with harsh chlorine decontamination fluids

explanation: Gaps under fake nails and rings hide large numbers of bacteria that survive normal handwashing. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h3)

question: What type of gloves must a midwife wear when stitching a perineal tear?

options.A: Clean non-sterile gloves
options.B: Sterile surgical gloves
options.C: Double-layered household gloves
options.D: Heavy-duty utility gloves

explanation: Siring a tear touches deep open tissues, so sterile gloves are needed to stop outside bacteria from entering. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h4)

question: What must a midwife do immediately after taking off used protective gear like gloves and aprons?

options.A: Change into fresh scrubs
options.B: Document the exact time
options.C: Perform hand hygiene
options.D: Sanitize the clinical chart
