explanation: Hands can easily pick up germs while taking off protective gear, so washing hands right after is mandatory. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which maternity task requires strict sterile technique to stop a uterine or bladder infection?

options.A: Checking blood pressure readings
options.B: Assessing maternal weight gain
options.C: Catheterization of the bladder
options.D: Listening to fetal heart tones

explanation: Passing a catheter puts a tube directly into the sterile bladder, requiring full sterile technique to prevent infections. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h5)

question: A midwife is getting ready to repair a tear after birth. What is the main infection control goal?

options.A: Reducing the total volume of blood loss from the placental site
options.B: Ensuring the mother remains fully awake throughout the entire suturing process
options.C: Speeding up the uterine involution process in the immediate postpartum period
options.D: Preventing introduction of bacteria into the open perineal wound layers

explanation: Stitching creates a healing wound where introduced bacteria can multiply and cause localized infection or wound breakdown. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h5)

question: Where should used injection needles and surgical blades go right after a delivery procedure?

options.A: Open metal kidney dishes on instrument trays
options.B: Black plastic municipal waste bins
options.C: Soft red polythene infectious waste bags
options.D: Rigid puncture-resistant sharps containers

explanation: Sharps must go directly into puncture-proof boxes to stop accidental needle-prick injuries for staff and cleaners. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why must surgical instruments be decontaminated right after childbirth before sterilization?

options.A: To neutralize the chemical smell of previous anesthetic medications
options.B: To cool down instruments that were exposed to high ambient room temperatures
options.C: To ensure the metal instruments retain their shiny factory polish
options.D: To remove organic blood and tissue so the sterilization process works effectively

explanation: Leftover blood and tissue protect germs from heat or steam, which stops proper sterilization if the tools are not cleaned first. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the recommended standard practice for routine umbilical cord care to prevent infection?

options.A: Dressing the area with herbal pastes
options.B: Washing the base with saliva daily
options.C: Applying fresh palm oil twice daily
options.D: Keeping the cord stump clean and dry

explanation: Standard guidelines advise keeping the cord clean and dry without traditional substances, which can introduce bacteria and cause tetanus or sepsis. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is exclusive breastfeeding strongly encouraged to help prevent infections in newborns?

options.A: Breast milk completely sterilizes the newborn's gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Breastfeeding prevents the baby from coming into contact with hospital air
options.C: Breast milk keeps the infant's oral cavity at a constant low temperature
options.D: Breast milk contains protective maternal antibodies that boost neonatal immunity

explanation: Breast milk supplies vital antibodies that protect the baby's fragile gut and breathing system from germs. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T1#BMP211_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the most common way infections spread between patients in a maternity unit?

options.A: Shared linen and bedding
options.B: Hospital room walls and floors
options.C: Contaminated air conditioning systems
options.D: Healthcare workers' hands

explanation: Hands easily carry microorganisms from one patient to another when hygiene steps are missed. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why are newborn babies especially vulnerable to catching infections?

options.A: They are frequently handled by visiting family members
options.B: They spend most of their time sleeping in cots
options.C: They consume high volumes of breast milk
options.D: They have immature immune systems and healing navels

explanation: An infant's body has not yet developed strong natural defenses against common bacteria. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h1)

question: How long should routine handwashing with soap and water take?

options.A: Five full minutes
options.B: Five to ten seconds
options.C: Two to three minutes
options.D: Forty to sixty seconds

explanation: Taking nearly a minute ensures every part of the hand gets proper friction and rinsing. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h2)

question: What is the main difference between cleaning hands with soap and water versus using alcohol rubs?

options.A: Alcohol rubs remove heavy mud while soap only removes light dust
options.B: Soap and water sterilize the skin completely while alcohol only cleans the surface
options.C: Alcohol rubs require running water to activate their ingredients
options.D: Soap and water physically wash away dirt, while alcohol rubs kill germs chemically

explanation: Friction from washing lifts away dirt and microbes, while alcohol breaks down proteins inside germs. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h2)

question: When is it necessary to use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: Every time you enter a postnatal ward
options.B: Immediately after taking a patient's temperature
options.C: When hands are visibly soiled with blood or body fluids
options.D: Before performing an aseptic wound dressing

explanation: Visible dirt or fluid stops alcohol from reaching and killing microorganisms effectively. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h3)

question: A midwife finishes a delivery and removes her gloves safely without any tears. What should she do next?

options.A: Use an alcohol-based hand rub on gloved hands
options.B: Proceed immediately to the next patient without cleaning
options.C: Wipe hands with a dry sterile gauze pad
options.D: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water

explanation: After removing gloves following contact with body fluids, hand hygiene is always required. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of surgical asepsis compared to medical asepsis?

options.A: To make hospital linen smell fresh and clean
options.B: To reduce only the number of visible dirt particles
options.C: To eliminate all microorganisms completely from an area
options.D: To prevent airborne droplets from traveling across rooms

explanation: Surgical asepsis creates a sterile zone where no living germs are present. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h4)

question: Which of these maternity procedures requires strict surgical asepsis?

options.A: Giving a routine antenatal health talk
options.B: Weighing a healthy newborn baby
options.C: Assessing fundal height on the postnatal ward
options.D: Performing a cesarean section delivery

explanation: Procedures that open the abdominal cavity expose internal tissues, requiring complete sterility. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h4)

question: In what direction should water run off your arms during a surgical hand scrub?

options.A: From elbows down toward the clean fingertips
options.B: Directly sideways off the forearms
options.C: From fingertips down toward the elbows
options.D: It does not matter as long as the water is warm

explanation: Keeping hands higher than elbows ensures rinse water flows away from washed fingers. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h5)

question: A midwife preparing for a cesarean section notices a small cut on her knuckle. What should she do?

options.A: Ignore it since surgical gloves will cover the hand completely
options.B: Report it and avoid scrubbing for that surgery
options.C: Cover it with ordinary cloth plaster and proceed
options.D: Apply extra surgical soap over the cut while scrubbing

explanation: Open cuts can harbor bacteria that might leak through tiny glove punctures during surgery. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h5)

question: Where should scrubbed hands be positioned after rinsing to keep them sterile?

options.A: Clasped tightly together resting against the abdomen
options.B: Crossed over your chest near the shoulders
options.C: Elevated above the waist and away from the body
options.D: Relaxed downward hanging loosely by your sides

explanation: Keeping hands high and in front prevents accidental contact with unsterile scrubs or surroundings. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h6)

question: Why can scrubbed skin still contaminate a sterile field if a glove tears?

options.A: Airborne dust settles instantly on bare washed skin
options.B: Surgical soap leaves a sticky residue that attracts dirt
options.C: Skin continuously expels resident bacteria from deep glands
options.D: Water temperature during rinsing activates dormant spores

explanation: Washing reduces surface germs, but living bacteria remain in deeper skin layers and can multiply under gloves. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T2#BMP211_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of maintaining asepsis during obstetric procedures?

options.A: To make instruments look shiny and new
options.B: To prevent disease-causing microorganisms from entering the body
options.C: To remove all visible blood and dirt
options.D: To reduce the cost of hospital maintenance

explanation: Asepsis is specifically aimed at keeping harmful microbes away from vulnerable areas to stop infections before they start. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why are postpartum mothers and newborns especially vulnerable to infections?

options.A: They consume a special postpartum diet that attracts germs
options.B: They have open wounds and fresh mucosal sites after delivery
options.C: They spend too much time sleeping in the hospital ward
options.D: They refuse to take routine vaccinations after birth

explanation: The raw placental site and tears or episiotomies create easy entry points for bacteria into the mother's bloodstream. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why must used obstetric instruments be rinsed with cold water rather than hot water initially?

options.A: Cold water is required to sterilize the instruments instantly
options.B: Cold water makes the instruments smell better
options.C: Hot water causes blood proteins to bake and stick to the metal
options.D: Hot water is too expensive to use in the decontamination room

explanation: Heat cooks proteinaceous matter like blood and tissue, making it extremely difficult to clean off later in the process. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h2)

question: A midwife finishes repairing an episiotomy and places the bloody forceps directly onto a dry tray without wiping them. What is the main risk of this action?

options.A: The blood will dry and form a protective layer over trapped bacteria
options.B: The forceps will lose their metal temper from the air exposure
options.C: The instruments will rust before they reach the washing sink
options.D: The hospital will run out of clean trays too quickly

explanation: Dried blood hardens on surfaces, protecting underlying microorganisms from being reached by cleaning agents and sterilizing gases or steam. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which personal protective equipment is most appropriate when manually scrubbing bloody instruments?

options.A: Bare hands washed carefully with antiseptic soap
options.B: Sterile surgical gloves and a paper cap
options.C: Heavy-duty utility gloves, apron, and eye protection
options.D: A standard cotton lab coat and examination gloves

explanation: Utility gloves protect against punctures and chemical splashes, while face shields stop contaminated water droplets from hitting the eyes. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h3)

question: What is the main reason for drying instruments completely before putting them into a sterilization pack?

options.A: Wet instruments are too heavy to lift into the autoclave chamber
options.B: Dry instruments heat up faster during the drying cycle
options.C: Water left on metal causes the instruments to change color permanently
options.D: Residual moisture can dilute chemical sterilants or create wet packs that let in bacteria

explanation: Moisture can compromise paper wrappers, turning them into wicks that pull environmental bacteria inside after the cycle ends. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h3)

question: What should a midwife do when an instrument shows deep rust or a broken lock during inspection?

options.A: Wrap it in extra paper to hide the damage from view
options.B: Polish it with abrasive sandpaper until the rust disappears
options.C: Use it only for minor procedures where perfection is not required
options.D: Remove it from service immediately and report it

explanation: Damaged or rusted instruments cannot be properly cleaned or sterilized and pose a direct infection risk to patients. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is a chemical indicator strip placed inside an instrument pack before wrapping?

options.A: To show the patient that the hospital buys expensive supplies
options.B: To seal the wrapping paper securely shut during transit
options.C: To record the exact name of the midwife who packed the tray
options.D: To prove that the inside of the pack was exposed to sterilizing parameters

explanation: Internal indicators change color when exposed to specific temperatures and steam, confirming the sterilizing agent penetrated the pack. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is considered the most reliable and widely used method for sterilizing metal obstetric instruments?

options.A: Wiping thoroughly with bleach solution
options.B: Steam sterilization under pressure in an autoclave
options.C: Soaking in cold soapy water overnight
options.D: Boiling in water for ten minutes

explanation: Autoclaving uses moist heat under pressure to kill all microbial forms, including tough bacterial spores, faster and more thoroughly than other methods. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h5)

question: When is a midwife most likely to choose a chemical liquid soak instead of a steam autoclave?

options.A: When there is no electricity available in the entire facility
options.B: When the metal instruments need to be sharpened before use
options.C: When the instruments are made of heat-sensitive plastic or rubber
options.D: When the procedure is taking place in a busy delivery suite

explanation: High temperatures and moisture in autoclaves can warp or melt certain plastics, making chemical immersion necessary for those specific items. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h5)

question: Which type of monitoring indicator uses resistant bacterial spores to prove the autoclave kills microorganisms?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape
options.B: Visual inspection mirror
options.C: Mechanical gauge
options.D: Biological indicator

explanation: Biological indicators contain actual live bacterial spores that are extremely heat-resistant, providing the ultimate proof of sterilization success. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why do maternity units rely on multiple monitoring methods rather than just checking the pressure gauge on the autoclave?

options.A: Machine gauges can show pressure while failing to reach the temperature needed to kill spores
options.B: Hospital regulations require staff to fill out unnecessary paperwork daily
options.C: Biological tests take too long to run between emergency deliveries
options.D: Chemical tapes are the only legal requirement in modern healthcare

explanation: Mechanical dials only show physical machine output, whereas chemical and biological tests verify that sterilizing conditions actually penetrated the load. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h6)

question: Where is the best place to store newly sterilized obstetric instrument packs in a maternity clinic?

options.A: Inside a cardboard box on the delivery room floor
options.B: On top of the autoclave machine for easy reach
options.C: On open shelves right next to the washing sink
options.D: In clean, dry, closed cabinets away from moisture

explanation: Closed storage protects sterile packs from dust, splashes, humidity, and accidental physical damage from passing foot traffic. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h7)

question: What does 'event-related sterility' mean for wrapped surgical instrument packs?

options.A: Sterility depends on how many times the pack is opened during an emergency delivery
options.B: Packs are only considered sterile during daylight working hours
options.C: Packs stay sterile until the wrapper gets torn, wet, or contaminated, no matter the time
options.D: Packs automatically lose their sterility after exactly seven days

explanation: Sterility is maintained by the integrity of the packaging barrier, meaning an undamaged pack remains sterile indefinitely unless an event damages it. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T3#BMP211_U3_T3_h7)

question: What is the main idea behind universal precautions in the maternity ward?

options.A: Giving prophylactic antibiotics to every mother after delivery
options.B: Using gloves only when a patient is known to have HIV
options.C: Treating every patient's body fluids as potentially infectious
options.D: Testing all pregnant women for hidden infections before labor

explanation: Universal precautions assume every person might carry an infection, so safety rules apply to everyone equally to protect staff and patients. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why must midwives apply universal precautions even if a woman looks healthy and has a negative antenatal test?

options.A: Healthy women carry higher bacterial loads than sick patients
options.B: Hospital policy requires it only for statistical record keeping
options.C: Antenatal tests can miss very recent infections or window periods
options.D: Ministry of health laws punish midwives who skip documentation

explanation: A negative test at 36 weeks does not protect against an infection contracted just before labor during the window period. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h1)

question: When is the most critical time to perform hand hygiene during labor care?

options.A: Only when hands look visibly dirty with blood or meconium
options.B: Immediately after the placenta is completely delivered
options.C: At the beginning and end of an eight-hour shift only
options.D: Before touching the woman and after body fluid exposure

explanation: Hand hygiene must happen before contact to protect the patient, and after contact or fluid exposure to protect the midwife and next patient. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h2)

question: A midwife just finished delivering a baby and removing her gloves. What is the immediate next step she should take regarding her hands?

options.A: Apply powdered lotion to prevent skin dryness from the gloves
options.B: Perform hand hygiene with soap and water or alcohol rub
options.C: Proceed immediately to document the delivery in the case note
options.D: Wipe them with a dry towel kept in the pocket of her apron

explanation: Gloves can have tiny invisible holes or tears, making hand hygiene mandatory immediately after removing them. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which piece of protective gear specifically shields the midwife's eyes from sudden fluid spurts during delivery?

options.A: A standard surgical face mask
options.B: Face shields or protective goggles
options.C: Heavy rubber utility boots
options.D: A waterproof plastic apron

explanation: Masks cover the nose and mouth, but goggles or face shields are needed to protect the mucous membranes of the eyes from splashes. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why must a midwife wear a waterproof plastic apron over her uniform during the active second stage of labor?

options.A: To block amniotic fluid and blood from soaking through to her skin
options.B: To provide a soft cushion when holding the baby against her chest
options.C: To keep her personal clothes completely free from wrinkled creases
options.D: To identify her easily as the lead birth attendant in the room

explanation: The primary goal of waterproof aprons is creating a physical barrier against soaking body fluids that carry infectious pathogens. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h3)

question: What practice causes most accidental needlestick injuries among maternity staff and must be completely avoided?

options.A: Carrying a safety box with one hand down the corridor
options.B: Recapping used injection needles or suture needles
options.C: Placing suture scissors on a sterile instrument tray
options.D: Washing metal speculums in a cold decontamination basin

explanation: Trying to push a needle back into its cap often leads to missing the cap and stabbing one's own finger. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h4)

question: When should a used disposable needle or suture blade be placed into the puncture-resistant safety box?

options.A: After cleaning and drying the instruments
options.B: Immediately after use at the bedside
options.C: When the assistant brings the box closer
options.D: At the end of the entire delivery shift

explanation: Carrying loose sharps across the room or waiting to dispose of them later increases the chance of an accidental injury. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h4)

question: A midwife gets a sudden splash of amniotic fluid directly into her eyes while assisting an emergency breech delivery. What is her immediate first action?

options.A: Rub the eyes vigorously with a sterile gauze pad to dry them
options.B: Leave the delivery room immediately to find the head nurse
options.C: Apply antibiotic eye ointment prescribed for newborn prophylaxis
options.D: Rinse the eyes immediately with plenty of clean water or saline

explanation: Immediate flushing dilutes and washes away infectious agents before they can infect the mucous membranes of the eye. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h5)

question: What should a midwife do first after sustaining a deep needle-stick injury during episiotomy repair?

options.A: Swallow prophylactic antiretroviral drugs kept in the ward locker
options.B: Wash the wound with soap and running water after encouraging bleeding
options.C: Squeeze the puncture site tightly and apply a strong iodine tincture
options.D: Cover the bleeding finger with a plaster and finish the skin sutures

explanation: Washing under running water helps flush out pathogens introduced by the sharp object before starting official reporting and PEP protocols. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of soaking bloody delivery instruments in 0.5 percent chlorine solution immediately after use?

options.A: Softening the metal to make manual scrubbing much easier
options.B: Decontamination to neutralize dangerous blood-borne pathogens
options.C: Removal of grease and rust from aging surgical metal
options.D: Final sterilization so they are ready for the next patient

explanation: Decontamination is an initial step that makes handling safer for cleaning staff and kills fragile viruses before they dry. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why must a midwife wash instruments with soap and water AFTER soaking them in chlorine, rather than skipping the wash step?

options.A: Chlorine ruins the sterilizer machine if organic matter is absent
options.B: Washing removes the strong chemical smell of chlorine from hands
options.C: Chlorine does not remove dried blood, protein, and tissue debris
options.D: Soap gives the metal a shiny finish required by hospital inspectors

explanation: Organic matter protects microbes underneath it; if dirt and blood are not scrubbed off, later sterilization will fail. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T4#BMP211_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which major bloodborne virus is a primary concern when handling maternity waste?

options.A: Hepatitis B virus
options.B: Rotavirus
options.C: Influenza virus
options.D: Rhinovirus

explanation: Exposure to blood and body fluids in the labor ward carries a high risk of transmitting bloodborne pathogens like Hepatitis B and HIV. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h1)

question: Why must all delivery waste be treated using strict universal precautions?

options.A: Any item contaminated with body fluids can potentially transmit infections.
options.B: Government regulations require all maternity waste to be incinerated immediately.
options.C: Normal refuse collection bins cannot handle wet materials.
options.D: Most delivery waste contains hazardous chemical compounds.

explanation: Universal precautions assume all blood and body fluids are infectious, protecting staff from accidental pathogen exposure. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h1)

question: What official classification does placental tissue fall under?

options.A: Anatomical pathological waste
options.B: Non-hazardous chemical waste
options.C: General domestic refuse
options.D: Radioactive diagnostic material

explanation: Placentas and body parts are classified specifically as anatomical pathological waste requiring dedicated handling pathways. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h2)

question: A midwife finishes delivering a placenta. Where should she place it immediately if the mother is not taking it home?

options.A: A cardboard box meant for used medication packaging
options.B: An open metal basin sitting on the delivery trolley
options.C: A standard black plastic bag for ordinary ward rubbish
options.D: A leak-proof yellow bin designated for anatomical waste

explanation: Anatomical waste like the placenta must go directly into a dedicated, leak-proof yellow container to prevent fluid leakage and contamination. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary responsibility of a midwife when a family requests to take their placenta home?

options.A: Charge the family an extra disposal fee for releasing the tissue.
options.B: Refuse the request immediately because hospital policy forbids releasing human tissue.
options.C: Provide safe packaging and ensure proper consent while respecting cultural values.
options.D: Bury the placenta herself within the hospital compound.

explanation: Cultural requests can be safely accommodated through proper documentation and secure leak-proof packaging for transport. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a required step when releasing a placenta to a family?

options.A: Obtaining signed administrative consent
options.B: Providing basic safety advice for transport and burial
options.C: Placing the tissue in a secure, leak-proof container
options.D: Performing a mandatory laboratory biopsy on the tissue

explanation: A routine laboratory biopsy is not required simply because a family requests to take their placenta home. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h3)

question: What specific protective gear helps prevent splashes of amniotic fluid into a midwife's eyes during delivery?

options.A: Face shields or goggles
options.B: Sterile cotton gowns
options.C: Heavy rubber boots
options.D: Disposable paper caps

explanation: Goggles or face shields protect the eyes and mucous membranes from splashes of blood and amniotic fluid. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why might a midwife wear heavy-duty utility gloves over standard examination gloves during waste handling?

options.A: To provide extra protection against punctures and strong chemical disinfectants
options.B: To make her hands look more professional to patients
options.C: To save money on buying single-use gloves
options.D: To keep her hands warm in air-conditioned labor wards

explanation: Utility gloves are thick enough to resist punctures from hidden sharps and shield skin from harsh cleaning agents. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h4)

question: Where should placentas awaiting delayed disposal be temporarily stored?

options.A: In an open bucket under the delivery bed
options.B: Inside the general staff room kitchenette
options.C: In a dedicated refrigerator separate from food and vaccines
options.D: On top of the clean linen storage trolley

explanation: Temporary cold storage prevents putrefaction, but it must be completely isolated from food or medical vaccines to avoid cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h5)

question: What feature must all bins or trolleys used to transport placental waste possess?

options.A: Open tops for easy air circulation
options.B: Built-in weighing scales
options.C: Leak-proof and covered construction
options.D: Transparent glass walls

explanation: Transport containers must be covered and leak-proof to prevent spills and foul odors along hospital corridors. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of maintaining waste logbooks in a maternity unit?

options.A: To record the personal contact details of every mother
options.B: To track how many babies are born each day
options.C: To create a clear audit trail proving safe disposal and regulatory compliance
options.D: To calculate the exact financial cost of electricity used

explanation: Logbooks track waste volumes and disposal methods to satisfy health inspectors and environmental protection agencies. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why is adherence to environmental agency guidelines critical for Nigerian maternity facilities?

options.A: It lowers the electricity bills of the hospital.
options.B: It prevents illegal dumping and protects public health from contaminated waste.
options.C: It guarantees an increase in government funding.
options.D: It speeds up the process of registering new babies at birth.

explanation: Following agency rules ensures that infectious material does not enter local communities or water sources illegally. [learn more](BMP211_U3_T5#BMP211_U3_T5_h6)

question: Why do we keep patient records in the maternity unit?

options.A: Meeting personal journaling needs
options.B: Reducing the cost of medical supplies
options.C: Providing a permanent legal account of care
options.D: Fulfilling hospital administrative quotas

explanation: Records serve as a permanent history that protects both the patient and the midwife while guiding ongoing care. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h1)

question: What happens when documentation is poorly done during labour?

options.A: It breaks down continuity of care across shifts
options.B: It prevents her from receiving routine medications
options.C: It automatically increases her blood pressure
options.D: It shortens the duration of the second stage

explanation: When details are missing, incoming staff lack crucial context about how the labour is progressing and any potential problems. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h1)

question: Which book or register is used to record a newborn's birth weight and immediate Apgar scores?

options.A: Labour Ward Register
options.B: Postnatal Register
options.C: Antenatal Register
options.D: Family Planning Register

explanation: Immediate birth outcomes like weight and Apgar scores are documented right in the labour ward record as soon as delivery happens. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h2)

question: A midwife just helped a mother have a normal vaginal delivery. Where should she write the details of this birth first?

options.A: Family Planning Register
options.B: Labour Ward Register
options.C: Immunization Register
options.D: Antenatal Register

explanation: The labour ward register is the main book used to record delivery details right after a baby is born. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the correct way to fix a mistake when writing in an official hospital register?

options.A: Draw a single line through the error and initial it
options.B: Scratch it out completely until it is unreadable
options.C: Apply correction fluid generously over the mistake
options.D: Tear out the affected page and start a new one

explanation: Drawing a single line keeps the original entry visible beneath the correction for transparency, and adding your initials shows who made the fix. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h3)

question: Why is it a bad idea to wait until the end of a long shift to write your clinical notes?

options.A: The register pages will automatically close and lock
options.B: Hospital management will fine the nursing unit
options.C: Critical details and exact times are easily forgotten
options.D: The pen ink will dry up inside the storage cabinet

explanation: Memory fades quickly in a busy clinic, which leads to inaccurate entries if charting is left until later. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h3)

question: In a legal case about patient care, how do the courts view a client's medical chart?

options.A: The property of the attending doctor only
options.B: Merely an optional suggestion
options.C: Primary legal evidence of care
options.D: A temporary scrap paper document

explanation: Clinical records carry high legal weight and are reviewed by courts to see if proper midwifery care was given. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h4)

question: In healthcare law, what does the court assume happened if you performed a care task but forgot to document it?

options.A: The action was NOT performed
options.B: Another department handled it
options.C: The action was done perfectly
options.D: The policy was waived

explanation: In nursing and midwifery law, the golden rule is: if it was not documented, legally it was never done. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h4)

question: Where is the safest place to store physical maternity registers when the clinic is closed?

options.A: On top of the medicine trolley in the ward
options.B: Open on the main desk for easy morning access
options.C: Inside a public waiting area bookshelf
options.D: Inside a locked cabinet in a restricted room

explanation: Keeping books in a locked space stops unauthorized people from seeing private patient information. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h5)

question: Which of these actions breaks patient confidentiality in a maternity ward?

options.A: Discussing a patient's delivery complications in the public corridor
options.B: Writing vital signs in the official labour register
options.C: Asking the doctor to review a high-risk antenatal chart
options.D: Handing over patient notes to the incoming shift midwife

explanation: Talking about private health matters where visitors or other patients can overhear violates confidentiality rules. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h5)

question: How do hospital managers use information gathered from maternity registers?

options.A: To advertise private maternity services online
options.B: To decide which staff members receive promotions
options.C: To track health trends and plan resource allocation
options.D: To determine personal grocery allowances for doctors

explanation: Summary data from registers provides essential statistics that help plan public health needs and distribute hospital supplies. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h6)

question: The local health ministry wants to know the total number of postpartum haemorrhage cases treated last month. Where should the midwife look for this information?

options.A: Staff attendance sign-in sheets
options.B: The personal diary of the head of nursing
options.C: General hospital cafeteria purchase receipts
options.D: Maternity unit registers and delivery logs

explanation: Official ward registers track diagnoses and complications systematically, making them the correct source for hospital reports. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T1#BMP211_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during childbirth?

options.A: To monitor the progress of labor and maternal-fetal well-being
options.B: To calculate the exact date of delivery for pregnant women
options.C: To replace all manual physical examinations in the labor ward
options.D: To serve as a financial receipt for hospital bill payments

explanation: The partograph provides a clear visual record that helps midwives track how labor is advancing alongside the health of both mother and baby. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h1)

question: At what specific stage of labor should a midwife in a Nigerian primary health center start plotting on the partograph?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta has been completely delivered
options.B: During the first prenatal booking visit in the first trimester
options.C: Only when the baby's head is already crowning at the outlet
options.D: As soon as the woman enters the active phase of labor

explanation: Plotting officially begins when the cervix reaches four centimeters dilation, which marks the start of the active phase of labor. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which section occupies the topmost part of the standard WHO partograph sheet?

options.A: Neonatal immunization records
options.B: Postpartum family planning notes
options.C: Maternal blood pressure logs
options.D: Fetal condition monitoring

explanation: The top section of the chart is dedicated to tracking the baby's heart rate, liquor status, and head molding. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h2)

question: Why is the partograph designed to show all labor parameters on a single sheet?

options.A: To save printing costs for the hospital administration and the government
options.B: To provide a quick visual trend that highlights any developing complications
options.C: To eliminate the need for writing any narrative notes in the case file
options.D: To ensure patients can easily fill out their own medical records

explanation: Grouping all observations together lets the midwife spot warning signs immediately by looking at how the lines trend over time. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h2)

question: What letter is used on the partograph to record clear amniotic fluid after the membranes have ruptured?

options.A: I
options.B: M
options.C: B
options.D: C

explanation: The letter C stands for clear amniotic fluid, while M denotes meconium and I indicates membranes that are still intact. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h3)

question: What does a severe degree of skull bone molding (+3) typically suggest during a difficult labor?

options.A: Significant compression of the fetal head trying to pass through a tight pelvis
options.B: An unusually high volume of clear amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus
options.C: Early rupture of the amniotic membranes before the onset of contractions
options.D: Normal rapid descent of the baby without any mechanical obstruction

explanation: High molding scores show that the baby's skull bones are overlapping heavily to fit through a potentially narrow birth canal. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which symbol is conventionally used to plot cervical dilatation on the partograph grid?

options.A: A triangle
options.B: A circle
options.C: A square
options.D: An X

explanation: Midwives use an X mark to plot the cervical dilatation score against time, connecting successive marks with a solid line. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h4)

question: How does a midwife record the descent of the fetal head using abdominal palpation?

options.A: By checking the color of the amniotic fluid during a sterile speculum exam
options.B: By estimating the number of fifths of the head remaining above the pelvic brim
options.C: By counting the total number of strong contractions felt in one hour
options.D: By measuring the exact length of the baby using an obstetric tape measure

explanation: Head descent is gauged by feeling how many finger-widths or fifths of the fetal head can still be felt above the symphysis pubis. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h4)

question: How often should a midwife routinely check and record the maternal pulse rate on the partograph?

options.A: Once every shift
options.B: Every 2 hours
options.C: Every 30 minutes
options.D: Every 4 hours

explanation: Maternal pulse is monitored frequently every half hour to catch early signs of exhaustion, dehydration, or hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h5)

question: A laboring woman passes urine during a routine assessment. Which tests should the midwife perform on the urine sample for the partograph?

options.A: Fasting blood glucose test
options.B: Serum electrolyte balance
options.C: Protein and ketone levels
options.D: Complete blood cell count

explanation: Urinalysis on the partograph specifically tracks protein and ketones to monitor for pre-eclampsia and maternal starvation or dehydration. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is the standard recommended time interval between routine vaginal examinations for plotting cervical dilatation in active labor?

options.A: Every 1 hour
options.B: Every 6 hours
options.C: Every 4 hours
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: Routine vaginal examinations are spaced four hours apart to minimize infection risks while adequately tracking cervical progress. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main danger of delaying entries and attempting to fill out the partograph from memory hours later?

options.A: It forces the doctor to perform an immediate emergency cesarean section
options.B: It causes the paper chart to tear easily from excessive erasing
options.C: It leads to inaccurate records and missed warning signs of complications
options.D: It automatically invalidates the nursing license of the attending midwife

explanation: Real-time plotting is essential because delayed recording introduces memory errors and obscures fast-developing fetal distress or arrest of labor. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h6)

question: At what rate of cervical dilatation does the alert line progress upward and rightward on the partograph?

options.A: 2 centimeters per hour
options.B: 0.5 centimeters per hour
options.C: 1 centimeter per hour
options.D: 3 centimeters per hour

explanation: The alert line is constructed based on the minimum expected rate of cervical dilation in active labor, which is one centimeter per hour. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h7)

question: What immediate clinical action should be taken when a laboring woman's cervical dilatation line crosses over the action line?

options.A: Stop all monitoring procedures and advise the family to prepare for a home birth
options.B: Discharge the patient home immediately to walk around and return the next morning
options.C: Wait another four hours to see if the cervix dilates spontaneously on its own
options.D: Perform a thorough reassessment and initiate definitive management like augmentation or delivery

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is abnormally prolonged, requiring prompt medical intervention to prevent severe complications. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T2#BMP211_U4_T2_h7)

question: What is the main reason midwives keep clear, detailed patient records?

options.A: Satisfying government tax requirements for health facilities
options.B: Giving midwives personal protection against hospital queries
options.C: Providing material for nursing and medical school textbooks
options.D: Preventing dangerous gaps in communication between care providers

explanation: Clear records ensure that when different staff members take over care, they have immediate access to past findings and ongoing treatment plans. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why are midwifery records considered legally binding documents?

options.A: They are signed by the local government chairman before filing
options.B: They replace the need for verbal testimony from the patient
options.C: They provide a chronological account of care that can be used in court
options.D: They are kept inside locked steel cabinets in the hospital ward

explanation: Because they detail what was done and when, courts rely on these written notes to reconstruct clinical events during legal investigations. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h1)

question: What common saying highlights the importance of writing down every care action?

options.A: Always secure your files before closing the shift
options.B: If it was not documented, it was not done
options.C: Verbal orders override written hospital policies
options.D: Patient consent covers all missing treatment notes

explanation: Courts and professional tribunals operate on the standard that undocumented care is legally presumed not to have occurred. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the professional consequence if a midwife alters or backdates a patient chart?

options.A: Mandatory transfer to a rural primary health center
options.B: A minor warning letter without any further investigation
options.C: Severe legal penalties and possible license suspension
options.D: Immediate promotion to a senior ward management role

explanation: Falsifying records destroys professional trust and violates regulatory standards, leading to disciplinary actions up to losing the right to practice. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which ethical principle is broken when a midwife covers up a clinical error instead of recording it?

options.A: Paternalism
options.B: Beneficence
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Veracity

explanation: Veracity is the duty to tell the truth and be honest, which requires accurate documentation of both successes and clinical errors. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h3)

question: A midwife notices a colleague wrote a rude comment about a teenage mother in the case notes. What is the best action to take?

options.A: Add another insulting remark to support the original observation
options.B: Tear out the affected page so nobody else reads the comment
options.C: Advise the colleague to use professional, objective language instead
options.D: Ignore the note since it does not affect the baby's vital signs

explanation: Midwifery notes must remain professional and free of personal bias, requiring peer correction when inappropriate language is used. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT an acceptable way to handle patient records?

options.A: Leaving physical case notes open on a public desk for visitors to see
options.B: Keeping computer screens turned away from public view at the nursing station
options.C: Limiting chart access strictly to the healthcare team directly involved
options.D: Storing active patient files inside a securely locked ward cabinet

explanation: Leaving sensitive case files exposed to the public violates patient confidentiality and privacy rights. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why is discussing a patient's labor details in a hospital corridor an ethical breach?

options.A: It exposes private medical information to unauthorized people passing by
options.B: It prevents the doctor from hearing the diagnosis clearly
options.C: It automatically invalidates the official birth notification form
options.D: It wastes valuable time that should be spent writing charts

explanation: Public discussions break the confidential bond between midwife and patient by allowing others to overhear private health details. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h4)

question: What legal assumption is made by a court when a vital care step is left undocumented?

options.A: The care was omitted or never actually happened
options.B: The attending physician took personal responsibility for the task
options.C: The care was performed correctly but nobody bothered to write it down
options.D: The hospital policy overrode the need for that specific entry

explanation: Without written proof in the record, the legal system assumes the action was not carried out. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h5)

question: How do opposing lawyers typically use missing or messy entries during a malpractice lawsuit?

options.A: To prove the hospital has excellent administrative standards
options.B: To request a higher financial grant for the maternity unit
options.C: To argue negligence and lack of standard care by the midwife
options.D: To support the midwife's verbal testimony during cross-examination

explanation: Gaps and messy writing create doubt, allowing lawyers to convince the court that proper monitoring and interventions were neglected. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h5)

question: What is the correct way to fix a writing mistake in a paper clinical record?

options.A: Tear out the entire page and start the nursing notes fresh
options.B: Draw a single line through the error, correct it, then sign and date
options.C: Scrape the ink off the paper using a razor blade until it disappears
options.D: Apply thick liquid correction fluid over the error and write on top

explanation: A single line keeps the original entry legible underneath, ensuring transparency, while liquid paper hides information which looks suspicious in court. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h6)

question: A midwife realizes she forgot to record several medication doses given hours earlier. What should she do?

options.A: Backdate the entries to match the exact time the drugs were given
options.B: Write a late entry clearly labeled with the current time and the note details
options.C: Leave the spaces blank since too much time has already passed
options.D: Ask a junior student nurse to sign and document the medications instead

explanation: Late entries are legally acceptable if they are clearly marked as late entries with the current time and date, preserving honesty. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T3#BMP211_U4_T3_h6)

question: What is meant by a clinical risk in a maternity unit?

options.A: Any circumstance that could lead to unintended harm
options.B: A disciplinary action taken against a negligent midwife
options.C: An unavoidable complication of a normal delivery
options.D: The financial cost of managing a complicated birth

explanation: Clinical risk refers to any event or system gap that carries the potential for accidental harm to the mother or newborn. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h1)

question: According to safety principles, why do most errors happen in busy maternity units?

options.A: Medical equipment is always too modern for routine use
options.B: Patients refuse to follow instructions during the first stage of labor
options.C: Underlying system vulnerabilities create the conditions for mistakes
options.D: Midwives deliberately choose to ignore hospital guidelines

explanation: Safety science shows that errors stem mostly from flawed systems, equipment failures, or poor staffing rather than pure human negligence alone. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which term describes an event that had the potential to cause harm but missed the patient completely?

options.A: A near miss
options.B: An adverse event
options.C: A sentinel event
options.D: A no-harm incident

explanation: A near miss is an error or unsafe condition that is intercepted or avoids reaching the patient, preventing actual injury. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h2)

question: A midwife prepares the wrong dose of oxytocin, but a colleague checks the calculation and stops administration just in time. How should this be classified?

options.A: An adverse event
options.B: A near miss
options.C: A sentinel event
options.D: A normal variance

explanation: Since the medication was stopped before reaching the patient, no harm occurred, making it a classic near miss event. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the very first action a midwife must take when an adverse clinical event happens?

options.A: Notify the family members waiting outside the ward
options.B: Secure patient safety and stabilize clinical condition
options.C: Call the legal department to report the mistake
options.D: Fill out the official hospital incident reporting form

explanation: Preserving life and halting further harm takes absolute precedence over paperwork or administrative tasks during an emergency. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why is it necessary to preserve empty ampoules and broken equipment after an incident?

options.A: They must be returned to the manufacturer for a refund
options.B: Patient relatives will ask to inspect them during visiting hours
options.C: Hospital accountants require them to balance inventory stocks
options.D: They serve as vital physical evidence for the investigation

explanation: Retaining physical items prevents tampering and ensures that root cause analysis teams can inspect faulty tools or medication vials accurately. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h3)

question: Where should an official hospital incident report be submitted after completion?

options.A: The personal office of the state commissioner for health
options.B: The public notice board outside the antenatal clinic
options.C: The hospital quality improvement or risk management department
options.D: The patient's personal home address for transparency

explanation: Incident reports are internal administrative documents routed to safety officers to analyze system trends rather than kept in clinical files. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h4)

question: What kind of language must a midwife use when documenting an adverse event in a clinical case note?

options.A: Speculative theories about which coworker caused the delay
options.B: Vague summaries to protect the hospital from legal liability
options.C: Emotional expressions of deep regret and personal guilt
options.D: Objective, factual descriptions of care and observations

explanation: Clinical documentation must remain strictly factual, avoiding blame, speculation, or emotional language to ensure accurate legal and medical records. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary question asked during a Root Cause Analysis investigation?

options.A: What disciplinary committee will handle this case?
options.B: How much financial compensation will the family demand?
options.C: Why did the system allow this mistake to happen?
options.D: Which specific staff member should be dismissed immediately?

explanation: Root cause analysis focuses on uncovering systemic flaws and workflow failures rather than assigning individual blame. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why are near misses considered valuable subjects for clinical safety investigations?

options.A: They require no paperwork or administrative committee review
options.B: They prove that current maternity guidelines are completely flawless
options.C: They reveal hidden system flaws before actual harm occurs
options.D: They guarantee that no patient will ever complain later

explanation: Studying near misses allows hospitals to fix broken processes proactively before an identical scenario results in severe injury or death. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h5)

question: What does the practice of open disclosure primarily involve?

options.A: Handing over all personal staff files to the patient's relatives
options.B: Refusing to speak with relatives until an official lawyer arrives
options.C: Transparent and honest communication with families after an adverse event
options.D: Publicly posting hospital error statistics on social media networks

explanation: Open disclosure ensures families receive truthful, empathetic information regarding unexpected complications during maternity care. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h6)

question: A patient experiences a severe postpartum hemorrhage due to a delayed drug administration. Which approach represents proper open disclosure?

options.A: Sitting with the family in a quiet room, explaining the facts honestly, and expressing regret
options.B: Blaming the hospital pharmacy department loudly in front of the distraught mother
options.C: Telling the husband that heavy bleeding is entirely normal and refusing further questions
options.D: Avoiding the patient's bedside completely until she is discharged from the ward

explanation: Proper disclosure requires private, compassionate, and factual communication acknowledging the complication without shifting blame defensively. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h6)

question: What characterizes a punitive hospital culture regarding clinical errors?

options.A: Colleagues work together to investigate system failures
options.B: Training drills are conducted weekly for all staff members
options.C: Staff hide mistakes out of fear of harsh punishment
options.D: Management rewards midwives who report near misses openly

explanation: A punitive culture creates fear, driving errors underground and preventing the facility from learning or improving patient safety. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why are structured handover tools like SBAR introduced into maternity units after adverse event investigations?

options.A: To eliminate the need for keeping written clinical case notes
options.B: To increase the cost of maternal healthcare services for patients
options.C: To reduce the number of hours midwives spend working each week
options.D: To improve team communication and prevent information gaps between shifts

explanation: Standardized handovers ensure critical patient details are transmitted clearly, reducing miscommunication errors during staff rotations. [learn more](BMP211_U4_T4#BMP211_U4_T4_h7)

question: How are presumptive signs of pregnancy best described?

options.A: Definitive proof of a single intrauterine fetus
options.B: Objective findings discovered during a physical exam
options.C: Subjective changes reported by the pregnant woman
options.D: They can only be detected using laboratory blood tests

explanation: Presumptive signs are based on what the woman feels and reports herself rather than objective clinical findings. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why should a midwife avoid diagnosing pregnancy using only presumptive signs?

options.A: They are completely invisible to the healthcare provider
options.B: They only appear during the final trimester of gestation
options.C: These symptoms can be caused by other medical conditions or stress
options.D: Only laboratory technicians are legally allowed to use them

explanation: Many early pregnancy symptoms also occur in non-pregnant states due to hormonal shifts or illness. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which hormone primarily maintains the uterine lining and prevents menstruation during early pregnancy?

options.A: Insulin
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Progesterone keeps the endometrium thick and prevents it from shedding, which stops menstrual bleeding. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why is a missed period (amenorrhea) alone not a guaranteed sign of pregnancy?

options.A: Menstruation always stops abruptly during menopause
options.B: Stress and hormone imbalances can also stop menstrual periods
options.C: Implantation bleeding replaces a normal period entirely
options.D: Every pregnant woman continues to bleed monthly

explanation: Many non-pregnancy factors like emotional stress, weight changes, and illness can cause a missed period. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which hormone surge is linked to early pregnancy nausea and vomiting?

options.A: Follicle stimulating hormone
options.B: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.C: Adrenocorticotropic hormone
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Rapidly rising human chorionic gonadotropin levels in the first trimester strongly correlate with nausea and vomiting. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h3)

question: A pregnant woman attending antenatal clinic reports a strong craving to eat dry soil. What is the correct term for this behavior?

options.A: Pica
options.B: Hyperemesis
options.C: Quickening
options.D: Amenorrhea

explanation: Pica is the craving and consumption of non-nutritive, non-food substances during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary cause of increased urinary frequency during the first trimester?

options.A: Pressure from the enlarging uterus and increased blood flow
options.B: A urinary tract infection caused by bacteria
options.C: Sudden shrinkage of the kidney size
options.D: Complete blockage of the ureters by the placenta

explanation: The growing uterus presses against the bladder while increased renal circulation produces more urine. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h4)

question: How does urinary frequency differ between the first and third trimesters?

options.A: First trimester frequency is due to hormonal changes and uterine positioning, while third trimester is due to fetal head descent
options.B: There is no difference in the physiological cause of urinary frequency across pregnancy
options.C: First trimester frequency is caused by urinary infections, while third trimester is caused by kidney failure
options.D: Third trimester frequency only happens at night, whereas first trimester happens exclusively in the afternoon

explanation: Early frequency stems from pelvic organ positioning and increased blood volume, while late frequency results from the baby moving down. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the term for the first perception of fetal movement felt by the mother?

options.A: Ballotement
options.B: Lightening
options.C: Quickening
options.D: Engagement

explanation: Quickening refers to the initial fluttering sensations of fetal movement perceived by the pregnant woman. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is quickening classified as a presumptive sign rather than a positive sign?

options.A: Intestinal gas can mimic the fluttering feeling of movement
options.B: Midwives can easily feel the baby kick through the abdomen
options.C: It occurs too early for any fetal activity to exist
options.D: It can only be seen using an ultrasound machine

explanation: Because gastrointestinal sensations can feel similar, quickening is subjective and not definitive proof on its own. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a category used to classify signs of pregnancy?

options.A: Theoretical signs
options.B: Positive signs
options.C: Presumptive signs
options.D: Probable signs

explanation: Pregnancy signs are strictly classified into presumptive, probable, and positive categories. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main clinical risk of relying only on presumptive signs to confirm pregnancy?

options.A: It causes immediate harm to the growing embryonic tissue
options.B: It prevents the placenta from developing properly in the uterus
options.C: It can lead to misdiagnosis because other conditions share identical symptoms
options.D: It automatically triggers high-risk obstetric complications

explanation: Mistaking hormonal or digestive disorders for pregnancy can delay proper medical treatment for the actual underlying condition. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T1#BMP212_U1_T1_h6)

question: Around which weeks of pregnancy does morning sickness typically begin?

options.A: Twentieth to twenty-second week
options.B: Fourteenth to sixteenth week
options.C: Fourth to sixth week
options.D: Tenth to twelfth week

explanation: Morning sickness usually starts in the early first trimester, commonly showing up between the fourth and sixth week of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h1)

question: What does experiencing normal morning sickness generally indicate to a midwife about the pregnancy?

options.A: Severe lack of maternal vitamins
options.B: An unusually large fetus size
options.C: An impending miscarriage risk
options.D: Healthy placental development

explanation: Mild nausea and vomiting are linked to rising pregnancy hormones, which reflect a strong, progressing placenta and a healthy pregnancy environment. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which hormone relaxes the stomach muscles and slows down digestion during early pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles throughout the body, including the gastrointestinal tract, which slows digestion and contributes to nausea. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why do women carrying twins often experience worse morning sickness?

options.A: Faster movement of the bowels
options.B: Lower amounts of blood sugar
options.C: Reduced levels of body water
options.D: Higher levels of hCG hormones

explanation: Multiple pregnancies produce much higher amounts of human chorionic gonadotropin, which directly increases the severity of nausea and vomiting. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h2)

question: What percentage of pre-pregnancy weight loss is considered a warning sign in early pregnancy nausea?

options.A: Five percent
options.B: Fifteen percent
options.C: Twenty percent
options.D: Ten percent

explanation: Losing more than five percent of body weight signals that vomiting is becoming severe enough to impact maternal health and nutritional status. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h3)

question: A pregnant woman at eight weeks comes to the clinic reporting she has not kept any water down all day and her urine is very dark. What is the best assessment conclusion?

options.A: She is experiencing normal symptoms that require only reassurance
options.B: She has a typical mild digestive upset common in twin pregnancies
options.C: She needs advice on eating spicy foods to stimulate her appetite
options.D: She is showing red flags for dehydration that need urgent care

explanation: Inability to keep fluids down and dark urine point directly to dehydration, which moves far beyond normal, manageable morning sickness. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which laboratory finding is specifically associated with hyperemesis gravidarum rather than normal morning sickness?

options.A: Ketosis and electrolyte imbalance
options.B: High levels of red blood cells
options.C: Elevated blood glucose levels
options.D: Low amounts of white blood cells

explanation: Severe and constant vomiting in hyperemesis gravidarum breaks down body fats, producing ketones and disturbing essential body electrolytes. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h4)

question: How does the vomiting pattern in hyperemesis gravidarum differ from normal morning sickness?

options.A: It only happens immediately after drinking cold water
options.B: It stops completely by the tenth week of pregnancy
options.C: It occurs strictly during the early morning hours
options.D: It happens all day and night without relief

explanation: Unlike morning sickness which comes and goes, hyperemesis gravidarum involves unrelenting vomiting that persists throughout the entire day. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h4)

question: A newly pregnant mother complains of waking up every morning feeling very nauseous. What practical tip should the midwife give her first?

options.A: Take heavy prescription anti-nausea drugs every morning
options.B: Avoid eating anything at all until the afternoon hours
options.C: Keep dry crackers by the bed and eat a small piece before standing up
options.D: Drink a large glass of warm milk immediately upon waking up

explanation: Eating bland carbohydrates like crackers before rising helps absorb stomach acid and prevents the sudden drop in blood sugar that triggers morning nausea. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why is eating small, frequent meals recommended for managing pregnancy nausea?

options.A: It speeds up the digestion of fatty foods completely
options.B: It stops the liver from producing extra bile acids
options.C: It prevents the stomach from becoming completely empty
options.D: It increases the total amount of daily calorie intake

explanation: An empty stomach allows gastric acids to irritate the lining, making nausea worse; grazing on small snacks keeps acid levels balanced. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h5)

question: Why is it important for midwives to address the emotional side of morning sickness?

options.A: Emotional stress directly stops the placenta from making hormones
options.B: Counseling replaces the need for any dietary changes at home
options.C: Prolonged nausea can lead to anxiety, guilt, and emotional distress
options.D: Mental upset is the single leading cause of hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: Feeling sick constantly drains a mother emotionally, making empathetic counseling essential to help her cope with the psychological burden. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a helpful way for a midwife to support a woman suffering from morning sickness?

options.A: Explaining that the symptoms usually fade by the second trimester
options.B: Telling her that the nausea is all in her head and she should ignore it
options.C: Validating her feelings and offering gentle reassurance
options.D: Involving her partner or family to help with home chores

explanation: Dismissing a mother's physical experience damages trust and ignores real physiological symptoms; all other options represent supportive, compassionate midwifery care. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T10#BMP212_U1_T10_h6)

question: What is the medical term used for pregnancy heartburn?

options.A: Preeclampsia
options.B: Polyhydramnios
options.C: Pruritus
options.D: Pyrosis

explanation: Pyrosis is the medical term for the burning feeling caused by acid reflux. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h1)

question: During which stage of pregnancy does heartburn most commonly happen?

options.A: First trimester only
options.B: Immediately during conception
options.C: Second and third trimesters
options.D: The first two weeks postpartum

explanation: As the uterus grows larger and hormone levels peak, reflux symptoms usually worsen in the later stages of pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h1)

question: Which hormone relaxes the valve at the bottom of the esophagus during pregnancy?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscles in the body, which softens the valve keeping stomach acid down. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h2)

question: How does the growing uterus contribute to heartburn late in pregnancy?

options.A: It twists the esophagus around the trachea
options.B: It shrinks the size of the small intestine
options.C: It blocks the production of digestive enzymes completely
options.D: It pushes the stomach upward and increases pressure in the abdomen

explanation: Mechanical crowding forces stomach acids upward against the relaxed valve into the chest area. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h2)

question: When do women usually notice their heartburn symptoms become worse?

options.A: During heavy physical leg exercise
options.B: When drinking plain cold water
options.C: After eating or when lying down
options.D: Immediately upon waking up fasting

explanation: Food intake and lying down make it easier for stomach contents to flow backward into the esophagus. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h3)

question: An antenatal client complains of a burning chest and a sour taste after meals. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Early stage labor contractions
options.B: Normal fetal movement kicking ribs
options.C: Physiological gastric reflux
options.D: Urinary tract infection

explanation: A burning chest combined with a sour taste points toward standard pregnancy heartburn. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h3)

question: What eating pattern helps prevent heartburn during pregnancy?

options.A: Skipping lunch and breakfast
options.B: Eating right before sleeping
options.C: One large meal per day
options.D: Small, frequent meals

explanation: Eating smaller amounts prevents the stomach from becoming overly full, reducing the chance of acid overflow. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Why should a pregnant woman avoid lying down immediately after eating?

options.A: It causes immediate gestational diabetes
options.B: It slows down kidney filtration rates
options.C: It stops the baby from breathing properly
options.D: It removes the help of gravity in keeping stomach acid down

explanation: Staying upright uses gravity to keep stomach contents at the bottom of the stomach. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h4)

question: Which medication is usually recommended first for quick heartburn relief in pregnancy?

options.A: Strong sleeping pills
options.B: Strong narcotic pain relievers
options.C: High-dose herbal laxatives
options.D: Antacids containing calcium or magnesium

explanation: Calcium and magnesium antacids work fast to neutralize stomach acid safely during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why do midwives advise pregnant women to avoid using sodium bicarbonate for routine heartburn?

options.A: It instantly stops all uterine blood flow
options.B: It turns stomach acid into dangerous poison
options.C: It contains high levels of sodium that can cause fluid retention
options.D: It causes permanent damage to the throat

explanation: Excess sodium intake can worsen swelling and fluid overload during pregnancy. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h5)

question: Which sign is NOT normal for pregnancy heartburn and requires medical attention?

options.A: Burning chest discomfort
options.B: Sour taste in mouth
options.C: Mild burping
options.D: Vomiting blood

explanation: Vomiting blood indicates injury or bleeding in the upper gastrointestinal tract and requires urgent medical review. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h6)

question: A woman at 32 weeks gestation complains of severe upper abdominal pain under her ribs that is not heartburn. What condition must the midwife suspect?

options.A: Pre-eclampsia
options.B: Normal morning sickness
options.C: Postpartum depression
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Upper abdominal pain in the third trimester is a warning sign of severe pre-eclampsia and liver involvement. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T11#BMP212_U1_T11_h6)

question: Which pregnancy hormone relaxes smooth muscles and slows down bowel movements?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Estrogen
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone relaxes the smooth muscles of the digestive tract, slowing down peristalsis and causing food and waste to move more slowly. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h1)

question: How does the growing uterus contribute to constipation in late pregnancy?

options.A: It secretes extra enzymes that dry out fecal matter
options.B: It blocks blood flow to the stomach lining
options.C: It absorbs all the water before it can reach the large intestine
options.D: It presses directly against the bowels and restricts normal waste movement

explanation: As the uterus grows larger, it takes up more space in the abdomen, pushing against the intestines and slowing down transit time. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h1)

question: What is the standard definition of infrequent bowel movements used when assessing constipation?

options.A: Going more than twenty-four hours without passing gas
options.B: Only opening the bowels once every morning
options.C: Skipping a bowel movement every single weekend
options.D: Fewer than three bowel movements a week

explanation: Passing fewer than three stools per week is a primary clinical indicator of constipation. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h2)

question: Why do pregnant women often develop painful hemorrhoids along with constipation?

options.A: Straining against hard stool increases pressure on pelvic blood vessels
options.B: The baby's head kicks against the lower rectum constantly
options.C: Iron tablets chemically burn the lining of the anal canal
options.D: Progesterone directly causes veins in the rectum to burst open

explanation: Passing hard, dry stools requires straining, which forces blood to pool in the pelvic veins and leads to swollen hemorrhoids. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h2)

question: A pregnant woman has hard stools at 20 weeks. What is the best initial recommendation?

options.A: Purchase strong prescription enemas from the local chemist
options.B: Stop taking all antenatal vitamins and iron tablets immediately
options.C: Increase her daily water intake and eat more local high-fiber foods
options.D: Stay completely on bed rest until her bowel habits return to normal

explanation: Diet and lifestyle changes, such as boosting fiber and fluids, are always the safest first-line approach for managing minor pregnancy discomforts. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which local Nigerian food item is a good source of dietary fiber to help prevent constipation?

options.A: Polished white garri without soup
options.B: Condensed milk
options.C: Beans and brown rice
options.D: White refined flour bread

explanation: Beans and whole grains like brown rice are rich in fiber, which adds bulk to the stool and stimulates regular bowel movements. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h3)

question: Which category of laxatives is generally considered safest as a first choice because it draws water into the stool?

options.A: Heavy metal blockers
options.B: Harsh chemical stimulants
options.C: Osmotic laxatives
options.D: Strong purgative herbs

explanation: Osmotic laxatives pull water into the bowel to soften stools without harming the pregnancy or causing sudden cramping. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h4)

question: Why must midwives be cautious about recommending stimulant laxatives to pregnant women?

options.A: They can cause strong bowel contractions that might irritate the uterus
options.B: They neutralize all the calcium stored in maternal bones
options.C: They instantly cause permanent kidney failure in the unborn baby
options.D: They permanently stop the stomach from producing digestive acid

explanation: Because the bowels and uterus share nearby pelvic space, strong stimulants can provoke cramping that risks uterine irritability. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h4)

question: Which symptom combined with constipation requires immediate medical referral for a possible bowel obstruction?

options.A: Mild fatigue and slight lower back heaviness
options.B: Swollen ankles after standing for a long time
options.C: Inability to pass gas and persistent vomiting
options.D: Occasional heartburn after eating spicy food

explanation: Stopping the passage of gas along with vomiting points to a blocked bowel, which is a surgical emergency needing hospital care. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a routine sign of simple pregnancy constipation?

options.A: Feeling bloated and uncomfortably full
options.B: Passing hard lumpy stool three times a week
options.C: High fever and severe continuous abdominal rigidity
options.D: Needing to strain during bowel movements

explanation: High fever and a rigid abdomen are red flags pointing away from simple constipation and toward infection or surgical complications. [learn more](BMP212_U1_T12#BMP212_U1_T12_h5)
