options.D: Ovulation can occur before your first period, so family planning should start now

explanation: The body releases an egg before the bleeding starts, meaning a woman can get pregnant before her period returns. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T3#BMP212_U4_T3_h7)

question: What primary physical process causes the postpartum uterus to shrink back to its normal size?

options.A: Complete shedding of the pelvic floor
options.B: Continuous myometrial contractions
options.C: Rapid increase in estrogen levels
options.D: Immediate closure of the cervix

explanation: Strong uterine muscle contractions actively reduce the size of the organ and seal off open blood vessels at the placental site during involution. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why does postpartum lochia change color from bright red to brownish and finally white over several weeks?

options.A: The gradual return of normal monthly menstrual periods
options.B: Reactions to the various types of soap used during bathing
options.C: A dangerous infection developing inside the uterine cavity
options.D: The healing of the placental site and changing types of discharge

explanation: As the internal wound where the placenta attached heals, the discharge transitions from mostly blood to old blood and tissue fluid, and finally to white blood cells and mucus. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h1)

question: In which direction should a postpartum mother wipe her perineum to prevent introducing harmful bacteria?

options.A: Using a circular motion
options.B: From front to back
options.C: Strictly side to side
options.D: From back to front

explanation: Wiping from front to back prevents fecal bacteria from the anal region from spreading to the vaginal and urethral openings. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h2)

question: A new mother chooses not to bathe for ten days due to local custom. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Ignore the practice entirely since cultural habits cannot be changed
options.B: Educate her gently on how daily bathing and warm water prevent infection
options.C: Report her immediately to the senior nurse for breaking hospital rules
options.D: Force her to take a shower to meet modern hygiene standards

explanation: Respectful midwifery combines cultural understanding with clear, supportive health education explaining the reasons for daily hygiene. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h2)

question: When can a mother with an uncomplicated vaginal birth generally start gentle walking and breathing exercises?

options.A: Immediately upon arrival at home from the labor ward
options.B: At least three months after the baby is born
options.C: Within the first twenty-four hours
options.D: Only after the six-week postnatal clinic visit

explanation: Early ambulation is safe and encouraged for normal vaginal births to prevent blood clots and promote recovery. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why must women who had a cesarean section wait longer before starting strenuous abdominal exercises?

options.A: Because stitches prevent them from moving their legs at all
options.B: To ensure breast milk production is not permanently stopped
options.C: To allow the surgical abdominal wall incisions time to heal properly
options.D: So that fat deposits around the abdomen can harden first

explanation: Strenuous core workouts put high pressure on healing abdominal tissues and risk opening the wound if started too early after surgery. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of performing regular postpartum pelvic floor exercises?

options.A: Increasing the total volume of breast milk
options.B: Preventing urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse
options.C: Stopping postpartum lochia bleeding immediately
options.D: Accelerating the loss of stubborn hip fat

explanation: Strengthening the pelvic floor supports the bladder, uterus, and bowels, reducing the risk of urine leakage and structural sagging. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h4)

question: How should a midwife instruct a mother to perform a basic pelvic floor muscle contraction?

options.A: Flex her abdominal wall forward until she holds her breath completely
options.B: Squeeze and lift the muscles as if trying to stop passing gas or urine
options.C: Rotate her hips in a wide circle while standing up straight
options.D: Push down hard as if she is having a difficult bowel movement

explanation: The correct action involves lifting and squeezing inward around the vagina and anus rather than pushing downward. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h4)

question: What does a sudden return of bright red, heavy lochia during physical activity indicate?

options.A: The mother is eating too much protein after her delivery
options.B: The baby is feeding too frequently during the day
options.C: The body is being pushed too hard and requires immediate rest
options.D: The normal involution process is finally completed successfully

explanation: Increased or bright red bleeding during exertion is a warning sign that physical activity is interfering with uterine healing and must be reduced. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a safe sign during postpartum recovery and requires stopping exercise?

options.A: Mild tiredness after a short walk
options.B: Gradual tightening of core muscles
options.C: Slow improvement in mood and energy
options.D: Sudden heavy vaginal bleeding

explanation: Heavy bleeding is a dangerous warning sign of potential hemorrhage or delayed involution, whereas mild tiredness or normal muscle improvement is expected. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is adequate fluid intake especially important for women during the puerperium?

options.A: To cause the uterine muscle to shrink instantly
options.B: To prevent constipation and urinary tract infections
options.C: To prevent the development of postpartum depression
options.D: To completely stop all postpartum lochia discharge

explanation: Good hydration keeps urine diluted and prevents hard stools, addressing two common postpartum discomforts. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h6)

question: How does chronic lack of sleep negatively impact a woman's physical recovery after childbirth?

options.A: It impairs immune function and slows down tissue healing
options.B: It accelerates the natural loss of red blood cells
options.C: It causes the breast milk supply to turn into colostrum
options.D: It permanently prevents the uterus from contracting at all

explanation: Rest is essential for cellular repair; continuous sleep deprivation weakens the body's defense mechanisms and delays recovery from delivery wounds. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T4#BMP212_U4_T4_h6)

question: What main health problem happens when pregnancies are spaced too close together?

options.A: Elevated risk of adult-onset diabetes mellitus
options.B: Permanent loss of primary visual acuity
options.C: Premature fusion of cranial sutures in infants
options.D: Severe maternal iron deficiency anemia

explanation: Pregnancies that happen too close together do not give the mother's body enough time to rebuild her nutrient stores, which frequently leads to severe anemia. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h1)

question: Why does leaving enough time between pregnancies protect the uterus?

options.A: It gives the uterine muscle and lining time to regain complete structural integrity
options.B: It permanently thickens the outer peritoneal layer of the pelvic cavity
options.C: It lowers overall systemic blood pressure in the pelvic blood vessels
options.D: It prevents the ovaries from releasing eggs during lactation

explanation: Giving the reproductive organs time to heal ensures the uterine tissue is strong enough to handle the demands of another pregnancy and labor. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h1)

question: When can a mother who is NOT breastfeeding start releasing eggs again after childbirth?

options.A: Exactly six months after placental delivery
options.B: As early as four to six weeks postpartum
options.C: Only after complete involution of the uterus
options.D: Only after three consecutive menstrual cycles

explanation: Without breastfeeding to suppress hormones, the monthly cycle often restarts within a month or two after birth, well before most women expect it. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why is it risky to wait for your first monthly period to return before using contraception?

options.A: Ovulation consistently happens before the first period returns
options.B: The first period is always too light to indicate fertility
options.C: Menstrual blood quality changes significantly after childbirth
options.D: Hormonal contraceptives prevent the return of menstruation permanently

explanation: An egg is released before the bleeding starts, meaning a woman can become pregnant before she even realizes her fertility has returned. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h2)

question: When is the best time for midwives to start talking about family planning with pregnant women?

options.A: Immediately after the placenta is delivered
options.B: When the child is weaned from the breast
options.C: Only at the six-week postnatal check
options.D: During routine antenatal care visits

explanation: Bringing up family planning early during antenatal visits gives couples plenty of time to discuss and choose their postpartum options before the baby arrives. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h3)

question: A new mother is worried that a certain contraceptive will cause heavy bleeding and make her husband unhappy. How should the midwife respond?

options.A: Delay all contraception counseling until her husband can attend the clinic
options.B: Tell her that cultural beliefs about bleeding are completely outdated
options.C: Listen actively to her concerns and discuss side effect management options
options.D: Insist that she choose an intrauterine device because it has no hormones

explanation: Listening to a client's personal and marital worries builds trust and helps her find a method she feels comfortable using. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the strict rules required for the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM) to work?

options.A: The infant must sleep through the night without feeding
options.B: The mother must remain completely without postpartum menses
options.C: The infant must nurse frequently throughout day and night
options.D: The baby must be exclusively or nearly exclusively breastfed

explanation: Long gaps in feeding at night cause prolactin hormones to drop, which allows fertility to return and breaks the rules of LAM. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why does giving an infant regular solid foods lower the birth control effectiveness of breastfeeding?

options.A: It directly stimulates the mother's ovaries to release an egg
options.B: It decreases the frequency and intensity of suckling at the breast
options.C: It neutralizes the hormonal feedback loop in the infant's digestive tract
options.D: It permanently stops the production of breastmilk within forty-eight hours

explanation: When a baby fills up on other foods, they breastfeed less often, which changes the mother's hormone levels and can bring back ovulation. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h4)

question: Why are combined estrogen-progestogen birth control methods generally avoided during the first three weeks after birth?

options.A: They increase the risk of blood clots and can reduce milk supply
options.B: They accelerate the natural involution of the uterine muscle
options.C: They cause immediate permanent cessation of lochia flow
options.D: They make the infant hypersensitive to synthetic hormones

explanation: Postpartum women already have a higher chance of developing blood clots, and estrogen adds to this risk while also slowing down milk production. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h5)

question: A breastfeeding mother who gave birth two weeks ago wants a safe hormonal contraceptive that won't hurt her milk supply. What is the best choice?

options.A: Progestogen-only pill or implant
options.B: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Combined monthly injectable estrogen
options.D: High-dose emergency contraceptive pill

explanation: Progestogen-only methods do not interfere with breastmilk production and are completely safe to use during the early weeks after delivery. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h5)

question: What is the main drawback of putting in an intrauterine device (IUD) right after childbirth compared to waiting later?

options.A: A complete suppression of lochial drainage
options.B: Permanent scarring of the internal cervical os
options.C: A higher rate of spontaneous device expulsion
options.D: An increased risk of postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: Because the uterus and cervix are still large and relaxed right after birth, the body is more likely to push the device out on its own. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h6)

question: What happens to a woman's ability to have children right after an IUD is removed?

options.A: She remains temporarily sterile for one year
options.B: It takes at least six months for eggs to mature
options.C: Fertility returns right away with no delay
options.D: Her ovulation cycle is permanently suppressed

explanation: IUDs work locally and do not use hormones to block ovulation, meaning normal fertility comes back instantly when the device is taken out. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h6)

question: What is a common myth about modern family planning methods in many Nigerian communities?

options.A: They make breastmilk turn sweet and spoil quickly
options.B: They instantly cure all forms of postpartum depression
options.C: They cause permanent sterility or accumulate inside the stomach
options.D: They guarantee that every future baby will be a male child

explanation: A widespread misunderstanding is that modern contraceptives stay trapped inside the body or permanently ruin a woman's ability to get pregnant. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h7)

question: A patient wants an implant but is scared because her mother-in-law says contraceptives rot inside the womb. How should the midwife reply?

options.A: Tell the client to ignore her mother-in-law completely and get the implant in secret
options.B: Refuse to provide any family planning until the entire extended family attends clinic
options.C: Agree with the mother-in-law's warning and suggest traditional herbs instead
options.D: Provide clear, respectful education that debunks the myth and offer to speak with the family if desired

explanation: Respectful conversation bridges the gap between traditional fears and medical facts without disrespecting the patient's family support system. [learn more](BMP212_U4_T5#BMP212_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of antenatal assessment?

options.A: Monitor maternal well-being and track foetal growth
options.B: Treat long-standing chronic illnesses
options.C: Prescribe routine prophylactic antibiotics
options.D: Determine the exact day of delivery

explanation: Antenatal care focuses mainly on keeping both mother and baby healthy through continuous tracking. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is establishing a baseline at the first booking visit important?

options.A: It completely prevents all future pregnancy complications
options.B: It helps compare future changes during later visits
options.C: It replaces the need for any laboratory investigations
options.D: It determines the final financial cost of delivery

explanation: Having initial baseline records allows midwives to spot abnormal changes quickly as the pregnancy progresses. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which condition is routinely screened for using a blood sample to prevent severe neonatal jaundice?

options.A: Asymptomatic bacteriuria
options.B: Rhesus incompatibility
options.C: Gestational diabetes
options.D: Iron deficiency anaemia

explanation: Checking the rhesus factor helps identify mothers who may need anti-D immunoglobulin to protect the baby. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h2)

question: What does routine urinalysis primarily check for during an antenatal visit?

options.A: Electrolyte balance and liver enzymes
options.B: Red blood cell shape and size
options.C: Protein, glucose, and infection
options.D: Hormone levels and ovulation

explanation: Urine dipsticks quickly reveal protein for pre-eclampsia, glucose for diabetes, and white cells for infection. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why must a pregnant woman empty her bladder before abdominal palpation?

options.A: It is required to collect a midstream urine sample
options.B: It prevents the spread of urinary tract infections
options.C: A full bladder displaces the uterus and causes discomfort
options.D: A full bladder makes the foetal heart rate too fast

explanation: An overfull bladder pushes the uterus upward and makes feeling foetal parts difficult and painful for the mother. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h3)

question: What is the correct physical position for a woman undergoing routine abdominal palpation?

options.A: Left lateral position with knees drawn up
options.B: Lithotomy position with stirrups
options.C: High Fowler position sitting upright
options.D: Dorsal position with a small head pillow

explanation: Lying flat on the back with slight head support relaxes the abdominal wall muscles for easier palpation. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which grip is used to determine what is occupying the upper part of the uterus?

options.A: Fundal grip
options.B: Lateral grip
options.C: Pawlik's grip
options.D: Pelvic grip

explanation: The fundal grip is performed at the top of the abdomen to feel whether the head or breech is sitting in the fundus. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h4)

question: A midwife feels a hard, smooth, and ballotable mass in the lower uterine pole during the Pawlik's grip. What is the most likely presentation?

options.A: Transverse lie
options.B: Cephalic presentation
options.C: Compound presentation
options.D: Breech presentation

explanation: A hard, round, ballotable mass in the lower pole indicates the foetal head is presenting. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the normal baseline range for a foetal heart rate?

options.A: 60 to 100 beats per minute
options.B: 140 to 180 beats per minute
options.C: 110 to 160 beats per minute
options.D: 80 to 120 beats per minute

explanation: A healthy resting foetal heart beats between 110 and 160 times every minute. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why must the midwife feel the mother's pulse while listening to the foetal heart with a Pinard stethoscope?

options.A: To assess whether the mother is experiencing anxiety
options.B: To make sure maternal and foetal heart rates are not confused
options.C: To calculate the exact maternal blood pressure
options.D: To determine if the mother is having uterine contractions

explanation: Palpating the maternal pulse confirms that the sound heard through the stethoscope belongs to the baby, not the mother's aorta. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h5)

question: After 24 weeks of pregnancy, what should the symphysis-fundal height measurement in centimeters roughly correspond to?

options.A: Gestational age in months
options.B: Total maternal weight gain
options.C: Total foetal birth weight
options.D: Gestational age in weeks

explanation: Fundal height in centimeters usually matches the weeks of pregnancy within a two-centimeter margin after 24 weeks. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main reason for documenting all antenatal findings immediately after the examination?

options.A: It satisfies hospital administrative filing quotas
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for verbal handovers
options.C: It proves the midwife worked a full shift
options.D: It prevents errors and ensures continuity of care

explanation: Immediate documentation ensures that any healthcare worker reading the notes later gets accurate, up-to-date patient information. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a danger sign that midwives should teach pregnant women to watch for?

options.A: Vaginal bleeding at any stage
options.B: Mild swelling of the fingers in the morning
options.C: Noticeable reduction in foetal movement
options.D: Severe headache and blurred vision

explanation: Mild dependent oedema can be a normal physiological finding in late pregnancy, unlike bleeding, severe headaches, or decreased movement. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why should midwives avoid heavy medical jargon when explaining examination results to a pregnant woman?

options.A: It prevents unnecessary anxiety and improves understanding
options.B: It makes the consultation take much longer than needed
options.C: Medical terms are legally forbidden in antenatal clinics
options.D: Patients prefer guessing what their health status is

explanation: Clear, simple language helps the mother understand her health status and follow advice without getting frightened by unfamiliar terms. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T1#BMP218_U1_T1_h7)

question: What defines a high-risk pregnancy in clinical practice?

options.A: A pregnancy with a greater chance of health problems for mother or baby
options.B: A pregnancy where the mother is under twenty years of age
options.C: Any gestation complicated by severe morning sickness in the first trimester
options.D: Any pregnancy that requires delivery exclusively by elective caesarean section

explanation: High-risk status simply means the baseline probability of adverse outcomes is elevated, demanding closer observation. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which pregnant woman attending an antenatal clinic needs the closest observation and is classified as high-risk?

options.A: A thirty-two-year-old woman in her first pregnancy with normal blood pressure
options.B: A twenty-eight-year-old woman carrying a single healthy fetus at twenty weeks
options.C: A twenty-two-year-old woman experiencing mild ankle swelling at thirty-four weeks
options.D: A twenty-five-year-old woman with a history of three previous spontaneous miscarriages

explanation: A history of recurrent pregnancy loss is a major risk factor that places a woman in a high-risk category requiring extra care. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the main goal of antenatal triage when women arrive at the clinic?

options.A: To distribute routine blood-building supplements to all pregnant women
options.B: To calculate the exact expected date of delivery for new clients
options.C: To rapidly sort women based on the urgency of their condition
options.D: To register women for their routine health insurance scheme

explanation: Triage is designed to prioritize care so that the most critically ill patients receive immediate attention. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is a complaint of sudden blurred vision in a pregnant woman treated as an emergency?

options.A: It confirms the presence of a severe iron deficiency anaemia
options.B: It shows the baby has dropped into the pelvis too early
options.C: It is a classic warning sign of severe pre-eclampsia and impending seizures
options.D: It indicates that the woman has developed gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Visual changes like blurring or flashing lights occur due to blood vessel spasms in severe pre-eclampsia, which can precede eclamptic fits. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h2)

question: Who usually acts as the main coordinator of care for pregnant women in a busy antenatal clinic?

options.A: The hospital accountant
options.B: The pharmacy technician
options.C: The midwife
options.D: The laboratory scientist

explanation: Midwives maintain continuous contact with pregnant women, making them pivotal in coordinating ongoing assessments and team communication. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h3)

question: What action should a midwife take before transferring an unstable high-risk patient from a primary clinic to a larger hospital?

options.A: Wait for family members to deposit money for fuel
options.B: Discharge her home so she can prepare her own transport
options.C: Stabilize her vital signs and prepare a clear referral note
options.D: Discontinue all intravenous fluids to prevent fluid overload

explanation: Emergency stabilization and proper documentation are vital safety measures before embarking on medical transport. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which simple tool do mothers use at home to monitor the daily well-being of their unborn baby?

options.A: Cardiotocograph machine
options.B: Sphygmomanometer
options.C: Fetal kick chart
options.D: Pinard stethoscope

explanation: Kick charts empower pregnant women to track daily fetal activity and report any sudden decrease immediately. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of performing ultrasound scans with Doppler studies in a high-risk pregnancy?

options.A: To determine the exact genetic makeup and blood group of the fetus
options.B: To induce labor when the pregnancy reaches thirty-seven weeks
options.C: To prevent the onset of gestational diabetes mellitus in the mother
options.D: To evaluate fetal growth, amniotic fluid, and placental blood flow

explanation: Doppler studies assess blood flow in umbilical vessels, helping to identify fetuses experiencing oxygen shortages or growth restriction. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which medication is standardly used to prevent and treat convulsions in severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Magnesium sulphate
options.B: Methylergometrine
options.C: Oxytocin infusion
options.D: Nifedipine capsule

explanation: Magnesium sulphate is the proven medication of choice for managing eclampsia and preventing seizures in severe pre-eclampsia. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why are corticosteroids given to a pregnant woman at thirty-one weeks who is at risk of early preterm delivery?

options.A: To prevent heavy bleeding after the baby is born
options.B: To lower the mother's elevated blood pressure levels safely
options.C: To stop uterine contractions and prolong the pregnancy to term
options.D: To accelerate fetal lung maturity and reduce breathing complications

explanation: Antenatal corticosteroids stimulate surfactant production in the fetal lungs, significantly lowering breathing difficulties in premature newborns. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h5)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the SBAR communication tool used during clinical handovers?

options.A: Birth weight
options.B: Blood pressure
options.C: Background
options.D: Bedside nurse

explanation: In the SBAR framework, 'B' represents Background, providing the relevant clinical history leading up to the current situation. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is careful and detailed record-keeping especially critical in the management of high-risk antenatal patients?

options.A: It ensures continuity of care and provides a clear record of clinical actions
options.B: It replaces the need for verbal communication during clinical handovers
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital will receive prompt financial insurance payouts
options.D: It prevents the patient from asking questions about her medical condition

explanation: Detailed records allow every member of the healthcare team to track changes and support safe clinical decisions. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T2#BMP218_U1_T2_h6)

question: During routine antenatal visits in Nigeria, what are two core preventative care interventions given to mothers?

options.A: Hypertension monitoring and weight management
options.B: Blood transfusion and iron therapy administration
options.C: Tetanus immunization and malaria chemoprevention
options.D: Gestational diabetes screening and ultrasound scans

explanation: Tetanus toxoid vaccination and intermittent preventive treatment for malaria are the two primary routine interventions used to protect mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why are preventative interventions like tetanus toxoid and IPTp so important in Nigerian healthcare settings?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for any further laboratory investigations
options.B: They actively protect vulnerable mothers and babies from deadly, preventable infections
options.C: They serve strictly as administrative records for the federal health ministry
options.D: They replace the requirement for general nutritional counseling during pregnancy

explanation: These interventions are designed as active barriers against conditions that historically drive up maternal and neonatal mortality rates. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which organism is responsible for causing neonatal tetanus?

options.A: Streptococcus pyogenes
options.B: Plasmodium falciparum
options.C: Clostridium tetani
options.D: Escherichia coli

explanation: Spores of the bacterium Clostridium tetani enter the body through breaks in the skin or unsterile cord care, producing the toxin that causes tetanus. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h2)

question: How does giving the tetanus vaccine to a pregnant woman protect her newborn baby?

options.A: It permanently prevents the infant from ever cutting their skin later in life
options.B: It kills all bacteria living inside the delivery room environment instantly
options.C: Maternal antibodies cross the placenta to provide early protection after birth
options.D: The vaccine travels directly into the baby's bloodstream through amniotic fluid

explanation: Vaccinating the mother prompts her immune system to create protective antibodies which cross the placental barrier to shield the newborn. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the standard single dose volume for tetanus toxoid injection during antenatal care?

options.A: 2.0 ml
options.B: 0.5 ml
options.C: 0.1 ml
options.D: 1.0 ml

explanation: The standard adult booster dose for tetanus toxoid during pregnancy is strictly measured at 0.5 millilitres. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the correct minimum time interval between the first and second dose of tetanus toxoid?

options.A: Exactly 1 week apart
options.B: At least 6 months apart
options.C: At least 4 weeks apart
options.D: Exactly 24 hours apart

explanation: TT2 must be administered a minimum of four weeks following the initial TT1 dose to properly build up maternal immunity. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which specific medication is used for Intermittent Preventive Treatment for Malaria (IPTp) during pregnancy in Nigeria?

options.A: Quinine intravenous infusion
options.B: Chloroquine phosphate
options.C: Artemether-Lumefantrine
options.D: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine

explanation: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine, commonly abbreviated as SP, is the designated drug for IPTp in routine antenatal care guidelines. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is IPTp-SP given to pregnant women even if they feel healthy and show no malaria symptoms?

options.A: To replace routine iron and folic acid supplementation completely
options.B: To clear hidden parasites in the placenta and prevent hidden complications
options.C: To cure severe chronic hypertension before it leads to eclampsia
options.D: To permanently immunize the unborn child against all viral infections

explanation: Malaria in pregnancy often hides in the placenta without obvious fever, making preventative treatment necessary for all women in endemic zones. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h4)

question: At what stage of pregnancy should a midwife typically give the first dose of IPTp-SP?

options.A: The very first week of pregnancy
options.B: Beginning of the second trimester
options.C: Immediately postpartum
options.D: At 38 weeks gestation

explanation: IPTp-SP is safely started in the second trimester, once quickening occurs and organogenesis is complete. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at 28 weeks gestation received her first dose of IPTp-SP four weeks ago. What is the correct clinical action for today's visit?

options.A: Withhold SP until she reaches 36 weeks of pregnancy
options.B: Refer her to the laboratory for a rapid diagnostic malaria test first
options.C: Administer her second dose of IPTp-SP under direct observation
options.D: Prescribe a double dose to make up for missed weeks in the first trimester

explanation: Doses of SP are given at least one month apart throughout the second and third trimesters until delivery, so she is due for her next dose. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h5)

question: What simple advice can a midwife share with a pregnant woman to help reduce mild nausea after taking SP tablets?

options.A: Lie flat on the back for two hours immediately after
options.B: Crush the tablets into palm oil and swallow quickly
options.C: Avoid drinking any fluids for the rest of the day
options.D: Take the medication with water after eating a meal

explanation: Taking SP after food helps soothe the stomach lining and decreases the likelihood of drug-induced nausea. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is counseling mothers about minor side effects an essential part of giving antenatal medicines?

options.A: It guarantees that the clinic will never run out of essential drug supplies
options.B: It prevents mothers from panicking and abandoning future clinic visits
options.C: It replaces the need to document treatments in the patient record
options.D: It eliminates all possible drug reactions inside the human body

explanation: When women know what mild symptoms to expect, they remain confident and continue attending their scheduled antenatal visits. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT an appropriate place to document a woman's tetanus and IPTp doses?

options.A: The pregnant woman's antenatal card
options.B: The daily market attendance sheet
options.C: The facility maternal health register
options.D: The client personal immunization card

explanation: Medical treatments must be documented in official health records like antenatal cards and clinic registers, not unrelated community logs. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the main risk of failing to properly record vaccine and IPTp doses in clinic registers?

options.A: It automatically changes the gestational age of the unborn baby
options.B: It can lead to missed doses or unnecessary repeat administrations
options.C: It stops the laboratory from running routine blood hemoglobin tests
options.D: It causes the expiration date of the remaining drug stock to shorten

explanation: Without clear records, subsequent healthcare providers cannot tell which protective doses the woman has already received. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T3#BMP218_U1_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of keeping antenatal records in a clinic?

options.A: To calculate the monthly financial revenue of the hospital
options.B: To replace verbal communication entirely among staff
options.C: To provide a continuous medical history for safe care
options.D: To fulfill government tax obligations for health workers

explanation: Antenatal records track the progress of pregnancy over time so any healthcare provider can review past findings and make safe clinical decisions. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does a breakdown in documentation pose a serious risk to a pregnant woman?

options.A: It prevents the client from buying prescribed drugs at the pharmacy
options.B: It automatically increases the financial cost of hospital admission
options.C: It makes spotting developing complications like pre-eclampsia difficult
options.D: It causes the expected date of delivery to change every week

explanation: When previous clinical signs are not properly recorded, healthcare workers miss warning trends that point toward dangerous conditions like high blood pressure or poor fetal growth. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h1)

question: Who primarily holds and carries the antenatal card during the pregnancy period?

options.A: The head midwife of the clinic
options.B: The attending doctor on duty
options.C: The pregnant woman herself
options.D: The local government health office

explanation: The antenatal card is given to the client to keep and bring along to every clinic visit and emergencies so her medical details are always accessible. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h2)

question: Name the section of the antenatal card that tracks the ongoing progress of the index pregnancy at each visit.

options.A: National census data sheet
options.B: Current pregnancy details
options.C: Staff attendance register
options.D: The hospital financial ledger

explanation: The current pregnancy section records serial measurements like fundal height, blood pressure, and fetal heart rate during every follow-up visit. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h2)

question: Where are facility antenatal registers kept after clinic sessions are completed?

options.A: Inside the client's handbag at home
options.B: Discarded daily in the waste incinerator
options.C: At the local market stall for safekeeping
options.D: Securely inside the health facility

explanation: Facility registers are permanent institutional books that stay within the clinic to maintain official records and generate health data reports. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h3)

question: Why are clinic registers important for public health planning beyond individual patient care?

options.A: They dictate the exact salary scale of midwives in the unit
options.B: They serve as advertising pamphlets for private maternity homes
options.C: They determine the retail price of drugs in the pharmacy
options.D: They help compile data for health management information systems

explanation: Data from facility registers is aggregated to create HMIS reports, which government agencies use to plan health interventions and track health indicators. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which antenatal visit requires the most comprehensive baseline clinical assessment and history taking?

options.A: The postpartum follow-up visit
options.B: The thirty-six week visit
options.C: The final visit before delivery
options.D: The booking visit

explanation: The booking visit establishes the baseline health status, complete medical history, and early laboratory investigations for the entire pregnancy. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h4)

question: A client comes for a routine follow-up visit at 28 weeks. Which set of assessments must the midwife record on her card?

options.A: Detailed surgical history from her childhood years
options.B: Only her current home address and next of kin details
options.C: Weight, blood pressure, urinalysis, and fundal height
options.D: Only her church denomination and occupation history

explanation: Routine return visits focus on active monitoring parameters such as maternal weight, blood pressure, urine constituents, and fetal growth measurements. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h4)

question: What legal status do clinical antenatal records hold in the event of a malpractice investigation?

options.A: They belong exclusively to the midwife who wrote them
options.B: They can be used as legal evidence in a court of law
options.C: They become invalid the moment the baby is delivered
options.D: They are considered casual notes with no legal weight

explanation: Antenatal records are legal documents that protect both the client and the health worker by providing an objective account of care given. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the correct professional action to take when a midwife makes a writing error inside an antenatal record?

options.A: Leave the error uncorrected since crossing out looks untidy
options.B: Tear out the affected page and rewrite the entire record cleanly
options.C: Apply correction fluid generously and write the new text over it
options.D: Draw a single neat line through the error, write the correction, and sign

explanation: Standard documentation rules require crossing out mistakes with a single line so the original entry remains legible, followed by the correct entry and signature. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common documentation error in busy antenatal clinics?

options.A: Leaving vital spaces blank in the physical antenatal card
options.B: Using handwriting that is completely illegible to other staff
options.C: Recording every clinical finding immediately with a clear signature
options.D: Omitting the exact date and time of clinical interventions

explanation: Recording findings immediately with a signature is good practice, not an error. The other options describe common documentation mistakes. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h6)

question: How do routine clinic audits help improve midwifery documentation standards?

options.A: By punishing midwives publicly for every minor spelling mistake made
options.B: By replacing physical paper registers with expensive computer software
options.C: By reducing the total number of pregnant women visiting the clinic daily
options.D: By identifying gaps through file reviews and providing constructive feedback

explanation: Audits review records against set standards to find recurring weaknesses, allowing facility managers to guide staff toward better documentation practices. [learn more](BMP218_U1_T4#BMP218_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main benefit of greeting an arriving laboring woman warmly and respectfully?

options.A: It helps lower her anxiety and reduces stress hormones that can slow labor.
options.B: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any medical complications.
options.C: It replaces the need to perform a complete abdominal and vaginal examination.
options.D: It shortens the first stage of labor by exactly two hours.

explanation: A calm environment and a welcoming attitude reduce stress, preventing excess adrenaline from interfering with normal uterine contractions. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why is allowing a chosen birth companion to stay with the laboring woman encouraged?

options.A: It speeds up the paperwork required during the hospital admission process.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for nurses to monitor contractions.
options.C: It provides continuous emotional support and helps ease her fear.
options.D: It allows family members to administer prescribed pain relief medications.

explanation: Familiar support figures offer reassurance, which significantly lowers maternal anxiety during the birthing process. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h1)

question: What does greenish or brownish amniotic fluid typically indicate when membranes rupture?

options.A: An infection of the maternal urinary bladder during labor.
options.B: A normal sign that labor is progressing very rapidly.
options.C: Normal fetal urine output mixed with standard amniotic fluid.
options.D: Presence of meconium, which signals possible fetal stress.

explanation: Meconium staining means the baby has passed stool in utero, pointing to hypoxia or fetal distress that requires close monitoring. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h2)

question: A woman arrives in labor reporting her water broke four hours ago, and the fluid is clear. What should the midwife do next?

options.A: Administer broad-spectrum antibiotics intravenously to prevent immediate sepsis.
options.B: Prepare the operating theater immediately for an emergency caesarean section.
options.C: Document the time and clear color while proceeding with the physical assessment.
options.D: Send the patient home to wait until contractions become much stronger.

explanation: Clear fluid means no immediate meconium hazard, but documenting the rupture time is vital for tracking infection risks over the next 24 hours. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which part of the fetus is typically identified during the second Leopold's maneuver?

options.A: The fundal height measurement
options.B: The pelvic floor muscle tone
options.C: The exact cervical dilatation
options.D: The fetal back and limbs

explanation: The lateral grip allows the midwife to feel the smooth, resistant curve of the fetal back and smaller moving parts like hands and feet. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why must the midwife ask the laboring woman to empty her bladder before performing abdominal palpation?

options.A: It is a hospital formality that has no actual clinical importance.
options.B: An empty bladder instantly causes the cervix to dilate by two centimeters.
options.C: A full bladder makes it difficult to clearly feel the fetus and causes discomfort.
options.D: It prevents the mother from accidentally urinating during the vaginal exam.

explanation: A distended bladder pushes the uterus upward and forward, masking fetal parts and making palpation painful for the mother. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h3)

question: What three characteristics must a midwife record when assessing uterine contractions?

options.A: Color, odor, and total volume
options.B: Frequency, duration, and intensity
options.C: Height, weight, and blood pressure
options.D: Speed, depth, and temperature

explanation: Evaluating how often contractions occur, how long they last, and how strong they feel gives a complete picture of labor progress. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h4)

question: When is the best time to count the fetal heart rate using a Pinard stethoscope to catch potential distress signs?

options.A: Right at the peak of a strong contraction
options.B: Immediately after a contraction ends
options.C: While the mother is standing up walking
options.D: Before performing the abdominal palpation

explanation: Listening right after a contraction helps identify slow fetal heart rates that recover slowly, which are warning signs of oxygen shortage. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary infection-control practice when performing a vaginal examination in labor?

options.A: Changing the examination table paper between patients
options.B: Wiping the perineum from back to front afterward
options.C: Applying warm water and perfumed soap beforehand
options.D: Using sterile gloves and clean antiseptic technique

explanation: Strict asepsis prevents introducing bacteria into the birth canal, which can lead to severe uterine infections. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why should unnecessary vaginal examinations be avoided after the amniotic membranes have ruptured?

options.A: It makes the cervix thicken up instead of continuing to dilate.
options.B: It automatically stops all uterine contractions and delays labor progress.
options.C: It causes the baby to change its head position to a breech presentation.
options.D: It increases the risk of introducing bacteria and causing uterine infection.

explanation: Once membranes rupture, the natural barrier against infection is lost, making every internal touch a potential infection pathway. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the name of the specialized chart used to monitor the progress of active labor and maternal-fetal well-being?

options.A: Partograph
options.B: Temperature sheet
options.C: Prescription chart
options.D: Antenatal card

explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview of labor progress, helping clinicians spot prolonged labor or distress early. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is timely and accurate handover communication vital during labor ward shift changes?

options.A: It is only done to satisfy hospital administrative filing rules.
options.B: It prevents the need for any further clinical assessments for hours.
options.C: It ensures the incoming team knows about any developing risks and can act fast.
options.D: It allows the doctors to take a longer break without checking patients.

explanation: Clear communication bridges the gap between shifts, ensuring no critical warning sign goes unnoticed during staff handovers. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T1#BMP218_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of using a partograph during labor?

options.A: To replace the need for physical abdominal examinations
options.B: To monitor labor progress and detect complications early
options.C: To calculate the exact date and time of conception
options.D: To record the financial cost of hospital admission

explanation: The partograph gives midwives a clear visual guide of how labor is moving, helping spot warning signs before they become dangerous emergencies. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is the partograph considered especially useful in busy Nigerian maternity units?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any documentation by doctors
options.B: It guarantees that every birth will be completely painless
options.C: It allows women to discharge themselves from the ward
options.D: It acts as an early warning system to guide prompt referrals

explanation: By tracking labor visually, midwives can quickly see when a patient needs higher-level care long before severe distress sets in. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h1)

question: At what minimum cervical dilation should a routine partograph be started?

options.A: 1 centimeter
options.B: 4 centimeters
options.C: 10 centimeters
options.D: 8 centimeters

explanation: Starting the partograph at four centimeters marks the official entry into the active phase of first-stage labor. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h2)

question: A primigravida arrives at the labor ward with a 2 cm dilated cervix and mild irregular contractions. What is the correct immediate action?

options.A: Open a partograph immediately and prepare for emergency delivery
options.B: Wait and monitor her in the first stage area until active labor begins
options.C: Transfer her straight to the operating theater for a cesarean section
options.D: Administer oxytocin drip to speed up her cervical dilation

explanation: Because she is still in the latent phase with a cervix less than four centimeters, starting a partograph now is incorrect and could lead to false alarms. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h2)

question: How often should the fetal heart rate be checked and recorded on the partograph during the active phase?

options.A: Only after delivery
options.B: Once every shift
options.C: Every 30 minutes
options.D: Every 4 hours

explanation: Checking the fetal heart rate every half hour allows the midwife to spot signs of fetal distress quickly. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does a moulding score of plus-plus (++) signify during a vaginal examination?

options.A: Fetal skull bones are overlapping but can still be separated
options.B: Fetal skull bones are widely separated with wide sutures
options.C: There is severe, irreducible overlap indicating disproportion
options.D: The membranes are intact and bulging with clear fluid

explanation: Double plus moulding means the bones are touching and overlapping, but pressure can still push them back into place, showing moderate adaptation. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h3)

question: How often should a vaginal examination be performed to assess cervical dilation during normal active labor?

options.A: Every 4 hours
options.B: Every 12 hours
options.C: Every 30 minutes
options.D: Every hour

explanation: A four-hourly vaginal examination balances tracking progress with minimizing the risk of introducing infection into the birth canal. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following vital signs is monitored more frequently than the others on the partograph?

options.A: Pulse rate
options.B: Temperature
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Respiratory rate

explanation: Pulse rate is checked every 30 minutes to catch early signs of maternal exhaustion, dehydration, or hemorrhage, while temperature and blood pressure are checked every four hours. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h4)

question: At what rate does the alert line on the partograph progress upward?

options.A: 1 centimeter per hour
options.B: 3 centimeters per hour
options.C: 2 centimeters per hour
options.D: 0.5 centimeters per hour

explanation: The alert line is drawn assuming normal cervical dilation proceeds at a steady pace of one centimeter every hour during the active phase. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h5)

question: What clinical action is required when a laboring woman's cervical dilation graph crosses over the action line?

options.A: Immediate intervention and definitive management for prolonged labor
options.B: Discharge the patient home because labor has slowed down
options.C: Wait another four hours to see if labor picks up on its own
options.D: Stop all fetal monitoring and encourage the mother to sleep

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is dangerously prolonged, requiring prompt medical review, such as augmentation or cesarean delivery. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why must a midwife evaluate all parameters on the partograph together rather than looking at cervical dilation alone?

options.A: Fetal condition and maternal status greatly influence the safety of ongoing labor
options.B: Doctors will refuse to read the chart if any section is blank
options.C: Cervical dilation is never an accurate indicator of labor progress
options.D: Hospital policy requires every single box on the paper to contain ink

explanation: Progress in dilation means little if the baby is showing signs of severe distress or the mother is developing signs of infection or exhaustion. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h6)

question: A midwife notes that a patient at a primary health clinic has crossed the alert line. What is the appropriate next step?

options.A: Tear up the partograph and start a fresh page the next morning
options.B: Advise the woman to walk around the compound for two hours
options.C: Arrange prompt transfer to a facility with emergency obstetric care
options.D: Perform an immediate vacuum extraction in the primary clinic

explanation: Crossing the alert line at a primary center serves as a warning sign requiring referral before the situation deteriorates to the action line. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T2#BMP218_U2_T2_h6)

question: Which tool on the delivery tray is used to cut the perineum if an episiotomy is needed?

options.A: Needle holder
options.B: Episiotomy scissors
options.C: Tissue forceps
options.D: Artery forceps

explanation: Episiotomy scissors are specially designed with blunt or angled blades to make a safe, controlled cut on the perineal tissues during delivery. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why are warm receiving towels kept ready at the delivery table?

options.A: To clean off thick meconium
options.B: To stimulate the baby's first breath
options.C: To dry amniotic fluid for accurate weighing
options.D: To prevent rapid heat loss and cold stress

explanation: Newborns move from a warm womb to a cooler room and lose heat very fast through evaporation, making immediate drying essential. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h1)

question: In the active second stage of labor, how often should you check the fetal heart rate for a low-risk woman?

options.A: Only when she feels like pushing
options.B: After every single contraction
options.C: Twice during the entire stage
options.D: Once every hour

explanation: Checking the fetal heart rate right after contractions helps spot any distress caused by the pressure of pushing. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h2)

question: A laboring woman in the second stage is exhausted and struggling to push. What is the best first step?

options.A: Prepare her for an emergency CS
options.B: Scold her gently for not pushing hard
options.C: Give her strong IV pain relief
options.D: Encourage brief rest periods and sips of water

explanation: Maternal exhaustion calls for supportive care like hydration and pacing rather than rushing to surgery unless fetal distress appears. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main responsibility of the delivery assistant rather than the primary birth attendant?

options.A: Performing the internal pelvic exam
options.B: Delivering the baby's shoulders
options.C: Keeping the sterile field organized and handing instruments
options.D: Deciding on an episiotomy

explanation: The assistant manages equipment, sterility, and comfort so the primary clinician can focus entirely on the delivery. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is keeping a calm environment during the second stage so important for the mother?

options.A: It lowers her body temperature
options.B: It helps her focus energy and reduces panic during pushing
options.C: It stops contractions from hurting
options.D: It speeds up cervical dilation

explanation: Psychological support lowers anxiety, helping the mother follow breathing and pushing instructions more easily. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h3)

question: What does 'crowning' mean during the second stage of labor?

options.A: The baby's shoulders have passed through the pelvis
options.B: The placenta has separated from the uterine wall
options.C: The cervix is fully dilated to ten centimeters
options.D: The baby's head is visible at the vaginal opening and stays there between contractions

explanation: Crowning happens when the widest part of the baby's head stays visible at the introitus, meaning birth is very close. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is it important to control the speed of the baby's head as it emerges through the perineum?

options.A: To ensure the placenta delivers at the same time
options.B: To give the midwife time to put on gloves
options.C: To prevent severe tearing of the perineal tissues
options.D: To keep the baby from crying too loudly

explanation: A controlled delivery allows the perineum to stretch slowly, greatly lowering the risk of severe tears. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h4)

question: At what specific times should you assess the Apgar score for a newborn?

options.A: At one minute and five minutes after birth
options.B: At thirty minutes and sixty minutes of life
options.C: Upon crowning and at delivery
options.D: At five minutes and ten minutes after birth

explanation: Standard newborn checks require Apgar scoring at one minute to check transition and at five minutes to check ongoing stability. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is a major benefit of immediate skin-to-skin contact between mother and newborn?

options.A: It forces the placenta to deliver within two minutes
options.B: It guarantees the baby won't get jaundice
options.C: It eliminates the need for Apgar scoring
options.D: It helps stabilize the baby's body temperature and blood sugar

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact uses maternal body heat to regulate the baby's temperature and encourages early feeding for stable blood glucose. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main goal of active management in the third stage of labor?

options.A: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage by promoting strong uterine contraction
options.B: To speed up episiotomy healing
options.C: To encourage immediate breastfeeding
options.D: To check the baby's reflexes and muscle tone

explanation: Active management uses uterotonics and controlled cord traction to shorten the third stage and keep blood loss to a minimum. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why must a midwife inspect the placenta and membranes very carefully after delivery?

options.A: To measure amniotic fluid loss
options.B: To confirm that no retained tissue remains inside the uterus
options.C: To check for congenital birth defects
options.D: To determine the baby's gestational age

explanation: Missing bits of placenta or torn membranes left inside can lead to severe bleeding and infection. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h6)

question: How often should you check the tone of the uterus during the first hour after delivery?

options.A: Every two hours
options.B: Only once at thirty minutes
options.C: Every fifteen minutes
options.D: Every thirty seconds

explanation: Checking every fifteen minutes during the first hour is critical because postpartum hemorrhage most commonly happens in this window. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h7)

question: During a routine check in the first hour, you find the uterus feels soft and boggy. What should you do first?

options.A: Perform gentle uterine massage to stimulate contractions
options.B: Leave the room so the mother can rest
options.C: Check the mother's temperature
options.D: Give oral antibiotics for infection

explanation: A soft or boggy uterus points to uterine atony, and prompt massage stimulates the muscle to contract and stop the bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T3#BMP218_U2_T3_h7)

question: What exact event marks the beginning of the third stage of labor?

options.A: Rupture of the fetal membranes
options.B: Complete delivery of the baby
options.C: Expulsion of the placenta
options.D: Full dilation of the cervix

explanation: The third stage starts right after the newborn is fully born and ends when the placenta is delivered. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is the immediate postpartum period considered a dangerous time for the mother?

options.A: The open placental site can bleed heavily
options.B: The cervix suddenly swells up with fluid
options.C: The pelvic bones separate to release pressure
options.D: The maternal blood pressure rises too fast

explanation: When the placenta detaches, it leaves open blood vessels that rely on strong uterine contractions to close off and stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the primary goal of performing AMTSL on a postpartum mother?

options.A: To speed up cervical repair
options.B: To encourage early breast milk letdown
options.C: To test the placenta for infections
options.D: To prevent postpartum hemorrhage

explanation: AMTSL is specifically bundled together to cut down the amount of blood lost after delivery and stop heavy bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h2)

question: How does active management differ from the natural delivery of the placenta?

options.A: Natural delivery relies heavily on high doses of intravenous antibiotics
options.B: Active management requires surgical removal of the placenta every time
options.C: Natural delivery takes less than two minutes to complete safely
options.D: Active management uses medications and traction to speed up separation

explanation: Instead of waiting for nature to take its course, the midwife intervenes promptly with uterotonics and controlled cord traction to control bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h2)

question: Within what timeframe should the uterotonic drug be given after the baby is born?

options.A: Within one hour
options.B: Within one minute
options.C: After exactly ten minutes
options.D: Only after the placenta comes out

explanation: Giving the uterotonic quickly is essential to stimulate the uterine muscle fibers before significant bleeding can occur. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following conditions makes ergometrine a dangerous choice for managing the third stage?

options.A: High blood pressure
options.B: Mild gestational diabetes
options.C: History of malaria
options.D: Severe postpartum fatigue

explanation: Ergometrine constricts blood vessels throughout the body, which can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure for hypertensive women. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h3)

question: What dangerous complication can happen if you pull on the umbilical cord without pushing the uterus upward?

options.A: Cervical laceration
options.B: Eclamptic seizure
options.C: Amniotic fluid embolism
options.D: Uterine inversion

explanation: Pulling the cord without providing counter-pressure to hold the uterus in place can pull the organ inside out. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h4)

question: When is the correct time to apply gentle traction to the umbilical cord during AMTSL?

options.A: When the uterus feels contracted and hard
options.B: Only after the placenta drops out on its own
options.C: Immediately as the baby's head crowns
options.D: While the mother is pushing out the infant

explanation: You must wait for a uterine contraction and palpable firmness before pulling, to ensure the placenta has separated safely. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of massaging the uterus right after the placenta is delivered?

options.A: To check if the bladder is completely empty
options.B: To push out remaining amniotic fluid
options.C: To speed up the healing of abdominal skin
options.D: To keep the uterine muscle contracted

explanation: Massaging stimulates the myometrium to stay firmly clamped down so that bleeding is controlled. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h5)

question: How often should a midwife check the tone of the uterus during the first two hours postpartum?

options.A: Only if the mother complains of pain
options.B: Once before the mother leaves the labor ward
options.C: Every fifteen minutes
options.D: Every hour on the hour

explanation: Frequent checks in the immediate postpartum window help catch early uterine relaxation before heavy blood loss occurs. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h5)

question: At what point is a placenta considered retained if it has not yet delivered?

options.A: After two hours
options.B: After one hour
options.C: After ten minutes
options.D: After thirty minutes

explanation: If the placenta fails to deliver within thirty minutes despite active management, it is classified as a retained placenta requiring medical action. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h6)

question: Why is it important to inspect the delivered placenta and membranes thoroughly?

options.A: To ensure no tissue was left inside the uterus
options.B: To measure the exact birth weight of the baby
options.C: To check if the umbilical cord was knotted
options.D: To prepare the tissue for laboratory testing

explanation: Missing a small piece of the placenta can cause persistent bleeding and postpartum infection later on. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T4#BMP218_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main change that must happen in a newborn's lungs during the Golden Minute?

options.A: The diaphragm must relax into a dome shape
options.B: Surfactant production must permanently cease
options.C: Pulmonary arteries must completely constrict
options.D: Alveoli must clear fluid and fill with air

explanation: At birth, lung fluid is absorbed or pushed out so the tiny air sacs (alveoli) can fill with air and start exchanging oxygen. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do midwives call the first minute of life the Golden Minute?

options.A: It is the exact duration required to administer routine Vitamin K prophylaxis
options.B: It is the critical window to establish independent breathing and prevent severe complications
options.C: It marks the time limit for placenta expulsion before postpartum hemorrhage begins
options.D: It represents the period when maternal blood pressure naturally stabilizes

explanation: Acting within this sixty-second window helps prevent prolonged lack of oxygen in newborns who struggle to breathe on their own. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT part of the standard initial steps of newborn care?

options.A: Immediate high-flow oxygen administration
options.B: Drying the skin thoroughly with warm towels
options.C: Positioning the head in a neutral sniffing posture
options.D: Providing a warm surface to prevent heat loss

explanation: Routine oxygen is not a standard first step unless simply drying and stimulating the baby fails to start spontaneous breathing. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h2)

question: A midwife receives a newborn who is limp and wet. What action should be performed first?

options.A: Dry the baby thoroughly with warm towels
options.B: Administer intravenous sodium bicarbonate
options.C: Perform external chest compressions
options.D: Insert an endotracheal tube immediately

explanation: Drying removes heat-robbing moisture and provides the gentle touch needed to stimulate the baby to breathe. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h2)

question: What heart rate means a newborn needs immediate positive pressure ventilation?

options.A: Below 60 beats per minute
options.B: Between 120 and 140 beats per minute
options.C: Below 100 beats per minute
options.D: Above 160 beats per minute

explanation: A heart rate under 100 beats per minute, combined with gasping or not breathing, shows the baby needs help with ventilation. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h3)

question: How can a midwife quickly check a newborn's heart rate in a busy labor ward?

options.A: Measure the blood pressure using an adult cuff
options.B: Listen with a stethoscope over the chest or feel the umbilical cord base
options.C: Check the radial pulse at the tiny wrist
options.D: Count respirations for a full sixty seconds

explanation: Listening to the chest or feeling the base of the umbilical cord lets you assess the heart rate quickly and accurately. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the correct ratio of chest compressions to breaths during newborn resuscitation?

options.A: Fifteen compressions to two breaths
options.B: Thirty compressions to two breaths
options.C: Five compressions to one breath
options.D: Three compressions to one breath

explanation: Newborn resuscitation uses a 3:1 ratio to balance getting oxygen into the lungs with supporting circulation. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h4)

question: A newborn gets effective bag-valve-mask ventilation for 30 seconds, but the heart rate stays at 40 beats per minute. What is next?

options.A: Stop all interventions and wrap the baby warmly
options.B: Start chest compressions combined with PPV
options.C: Administer oral glucose drops immediately
options.D: Wait another two minutes for spontaneous recovery

explanation: If the heart rate stays below 60 beats per minute even with good ventilation, chest compressions must be started. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h4)

question: Where should a pulse oximeter probe be placed on a newborn to measure pre-ductal oxygen saturation?

options.A: Right earlobe
options.B: Right hand or wrist
options.C: Abdominal wall
options.D: Left foot or ankle

explanation: The right hand receives blood before it passes through the ductus arteriosus, giving an accurate reading of pre-ductal oxygen levels. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why is continued monitoring needed after a newborn recovers from initial resuscitation?

options.A: To fulfill legal requirements before issuing a birth certificate
options.B: To ensure the baby does not cry too loudly in the ward
options.C: To prevent the mother from experiencing postpartum depression
options.D: To catch and manage secondary deterioration or metabolic complications early

explanation: Babies who needed resuscitation are still at risk for issues like low blood sugar, low body temperature, and trouble breathing again. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the main reason for giving Vitamin K by injection to a newborn?

options.A: Protecting against bacterial eye infections
options.B: Preventing hemorrhagic disease of the newborn
options.C: Stimulating early meconium passage
options.D: Boosting long-term immune system development

explanation: Newborns have low vitamin K levels and sterile guts at birth, which puts them at risk for bleeding unless given a supplement. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is eye ointment applied routinely to newborns shortly after birth?

options.A: To prevent gonococcal and chlamydial eye infections acquired during passage through the birth canal
options.B: To lubricate dry corneas caused by bright delivery room lighting
options.C: To prevent congenital cataracts from developing later in childhood
options.D: To improve visual acuity and focus in the first week of life

explanation: Eye ointment protects newborns from dangerous infections picked up during birth that could otherwise harm their sight. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the name of the first thick, yellowish breast milk that is packed with antibodies?

options.A: Meconium
options.B: Surfactant
options.C: Colostrum
options.D: Foremilk

explanation: Colostrum is the first milk made after birth, full of immune protection and nutrients designed for a newborn. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h7)

question: A healthy newborn is skin-to-skin with the mother. After 30 minutes, the baby starts licking its lips and sucking. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Wait two hours before allowing any feeding attempts
options.B: Swaddle the baby tightly and place in a separate cot
options.C: Take the baby to the nursery for a bottle of sterile water
options.D: Assist the mother to initiate early breastfeeding while skin-to-skin

explanation: Lip licking and sucking motions are clear feeding cues showing the baby is ready to latch during the golden hour. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T5#BMP218_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the surgical cut made in the perineum during childbirth called?

options.A: Episiotomy
options.B: Laparotomy
options.C: Hysterectomy
options.D: Amniotomy

explanation: An episiotomy is a surgical cut made in the perineum during the second stage of labor to widen the vaginal opening. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which degree of perineal tear involves the anal sphincter muscle?

options.A: First-degree tear
options.B: Third-degree tear
options.C: Perineal graze
options.D: Second-degree tear

explanation: Third-degree tears involve the perineal muscles and the anal sphincter complex, which requires careful surgical repair. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h1)

question: In which position is a mother usually placed for a perineal repair?

options.A: Supine flat position
options.B: Lithotomy position
options.C: Sims position
options.D: Trendelenburg position

explanation: The lithotomy position gives the healthcare provider clear visibility and access to the perineal structures during the repair. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why must perineal cleaning before a repair always be done from front to back?

options.A: To prevent introducing bacteria from the anal area into the vagina
options.B: To make the local anesthetic work much faster on the skin
options.C: To push the remaining lochia outward before the stitches go in
options.D: To keep the surrounding drapes completely dry during the process

explanation: Wiping from front to back stops fecal bacteria from contaminating the surgical site and causing wound infections. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is a key duty of the assistant midwife during a perineal repair?

options.A: Performing the actual suturing of the deep muscle layers
options.B: Keeping an accurate count of all needles and swabs used
options.C: Injecting the oxytocin directly into the perineal wound
options.D: Deciding the total dosage of local anesthetic for the mother

explanation: Tracking instruments, swabs, and needles prevents accidental retention of foreign objects in the birth canal. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h3)

question: How can the assisting midwife best support a nervous mother during a repair?

options.A: Administer extra pain medication without checking the doctor's orders
options.B: Ask her to close her eyes and ignore the procedure entirely
options.C: Talk to her gently, explain what is happening, and offer reassurance
options.D: Tell her that the pain will stop immediately within two minutes

explanation: Continuous communication helps reduce anxiety and builds trust between the mother and the clinical team. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h3)

question: How often should a postpartum mother ideally change her maternity pads?

options.A: Every four hours or when soaked
options.B: Twice a day during morning and night
options.C: Whenever she feels completely dry
options.D: Only once every twenty-four hours

explanation: Frequent pad changes prevent moisture buildup and bacterial growth around the healing perineal wound. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the main risk of applying unprescribed traditional mixtures to a fresh episiotomy wound?

options.A: Making the synthetic suture materials dissolve much too quickly
options.B: Stopping the local blood supply to the entire pelvic floor
options.C: Introducing harmful bacteria and causing severe wound infection
options.D: Permanently changing the natural pigmentation of the skin

explanation: Unsterile local mixtures often contain germs and irritants that contaminate the surgical cut and lead to wound breakdown. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of applying a cold pack to the perineum within the first 24 hours?

options.A: Preventing the lochia flow completely
options.B: Stimulating early breast milk production
options.C: Speeding up the dissolving of stitches
options.D: Reducing swelling and numbing pain

explanation: Cold therapy narrows blood vessels, which helps decrease swelling and provides a mild numbing effect on nerve endings. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which clinical sign strongly suggests a perineal hematoma?

options.A: Severe, disproportionate perineal pain and a tight, shiny swelling
options.B: Complete absence of any discomfort when walking around the ward
options.C: A mild itching sensation around the outer edges of the suture line
options.D: Clear watery fluid draining steadily from the vaginal opening

explanation: A collection of blood beneath the repaired tissue causes intense pain and visible swelling that feels firm to the touch. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h5)

question: What details must be included in the formal documentation of a perineal repair?

options.A: The mother's detailed family medical history and ancestry
options.B: The baby's exact Apgar score at five minutes after birth
options.C: The exact cost of the suture materials used in the theater
options.D: Type of repair, suture material, and practitioner's name

explanation: Recording the specifics of the tear, materials used, and the practitioner ensures clear communication for future clinical care. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why are pelvic floor exercises recommended to women after a perineal repair?

options.A: To restore muscle strength and improve long-term pelvic support
