options.B: To stop postpartum bleeding from the uterus within one hour
options.C: To prevent the baby from developing neonatal jaundice
options.D: To make the skin of the perineum heal with a lighter color

explanation: Targeted pelvic floor exercises improve blood circulation to the area and help regain muscle tone after childbirth. [learn more](BMP218_U2_T6#BMP218_U2_T6_h6)

question: How long does the postnatal period typically last?

options.A: Six weeks
options.B: Three months
options.C: Six months
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: The puerperium spans the first six weeks following childbirth, during which the maternal body returns to its non-pregnant state. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the main reason midwives do routine checks on mothers in the postnatal ward?

options.A: To complete the formal birth registration paperwork
options.B: To keep the hospital bed occupancy rates stable
options.C: To teach the mother advanced neonatal nursing skills
options.D: To catch early signs of problems in mother and baby

explanation: Regular checks allow midwives to spot physical or emotional issues early before they become serious emergencies. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why should a mother empty her bladder before a routine postnatal physical exam?

options.A: A full bladder pushes the uterus out of place and causes discomfort
options.B: Emptying the bladder helps the baby latch on much faster
options.C: Urine samples are mandatory for every single shift check
options.D: It prevents the mother from feeling sleepy during the talk

explanation: A full bladder pushes the uterus upward and to the side, making it harder to feel properly and causing unnecessary pain. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h2)

question: A midwife walks in to check a tired mother on the ward. What is the best first step?

options.A: Greet the mother warmly, introduce yourself, and explain what you will do
options.B: Undress the newborn baby quickly while the mother is resting
options.C: Immediately check the perineal pad without asking for permission
options.D: Record vital signs on the chart before speaking to anyone in the room

explanation: Building trust and asking permission helps the mother feel relaxed and comfortable with your care. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h2)

question: In the BUBBLE-EE postnatal check system, what does the letter 'L' stand for?

options.A: Lochia
options.B: Lactation
options.C: Labor
options.D: Ligaments

explanation: In the BUBBLE-EE acronym, L stands for lochia, which is the normal vaginal discharge after childbirth. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h3)

question: When checking the uterus in the early days after birth, what normal finding should the midwife expect?

options.A: A hard, immobile mass pushing sharply out of the pelvis
options.B: A firm, contracted mass at or below the belly button
options.C: A soft, spongy mass located high up near the right ribs
options.D: A completely hidden uterus on the very first postpartum day

explanation: A firm uterus shows that the muscles are contracting well, which helps prevent heavy bleeding. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h3)

question: Within how many hours should a healthy newborn normally pass their first urine and stool (meconium)?

options.A: 72 to 96 hours
options.B: 6 to 12 hours
options.C: 24 to 48 hours
options.D: After one full week

explanation: Most healthy newborns pass urine and their first dark stool within the first day or two of life. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why do newborn babies often lose a small amount of weight in their first few days of life?

options.A: Due to normal fluid shifts and passing meconium
options.B: Due to rapid dehydration caused by ward lighting
options.C: Because breast milk has no calories at all initially
options.D: Because the baby is burning excess fat from cold stress

explanation: It is normal for babies to lose a little weight at first as their bodies shed extra fluid and waste products. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which sign shows that a baby is latching on correctly for breastfeeding?

options.A: The baby's mouth takes in a large portion of the lower areola
options.B: The baby's lips are tucked inward tightly against the gums
options.C: Only the tip of the nipple is placed inside the baby's mouth
options.D: The mother feels sharp pinching pain throughout the feed

explanation: A deep latch protects the nipple from pain and helps the baby get enough milk easily. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a clear sign that a mother is bonding well with her newborn?

options.A: She asks the nurses to care for the baby in the nursery all night
options.B: She focuses entirely on her own phone while feeding
options.C: She avoids speaking to the infant until the umbilical cord falls off
options.D: She makes eye contact, holds the baby close, and responds to cries

explanation: Holding the baby close and responding to their cries are wonderful signs of a growing mother-baby bond. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT normal and should be treated as a warning sign in a postnatal mother?

options.A: Mild tummy cramps while breastfeeding in a mother who has given birth before
options.B: Moderate lochia changing to a lighter color by day four
options.C: Passing small lochia clots on the second postpartum day
options.D: Soaking a sanitary pad in less than one hour

explanation: Heavy bleeding that soaks a pad in under an hour points to postpartum hemorrhage and needs quick action. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h6)

question: A mother on the ward complains of a severe headache and blurred vision on her second day after delivery. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Document the complaint as a normal minor discomfort of childbirth
options.B: Report these symptoms to the doctor immediately to check for postpartum pre-eclampsia
options.C: Advise her to drink a hot cup of tea and wait until morning rounds
options.D: Tell her to turn off the ward lights and sleep off the stress

explanation: Severe headaches and vision changes are critical warning signs of postpartum pre-eclampsia that need urgent medical review. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T1#BMP218_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which hormone is mainly responsible for making breast milk after delivery?

options.A: Estrogen
options.B: Oxytocin
options.C: Progesterone
options.D: Prolactin

explanation: Prolactin is released from the pituitary gland to signal the breast tissue to produce milk. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h1)

question: What causes the sudden rise in prolactin that brings in milk after childbirth?

options.A: The closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus
options.B: The sudden increase in maternal body temperature
options.C: The first bath given to the newborn baby
options.D: The delivery of the placenta and drop in progesterone

explanation: During pregnancy, progesterone blocks milk production. Once the placenta is delivered, progesterone drops, allowing prolactin to do its job. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h1)

question: When should skin-to-skin contact ideally start after a normal vaginal birth?

options.A: After the baby has received a bath
options.B: Only after the mother has slept for six hours
options.C: When the mother's mature milk comes in
options.D: Within the first hour of life

explanation: Placing the baby skin-to-skin right after birth helps them find the breast and keeps their temperature and blood sugar stable. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h2)

question: A new mother looks stressed and says her baby is crying because she has no milk. What is the best first step for a midwife?

options.A: Observe a full breastfeeding session to check latch and positioning
options.B: Advise the mother to wait four hours between feeds to let milk accumulate
options.C: Prescribe oral galactagogue medications to stimulate immediate supply
options.D: Immediately prepare a bottle of infant formula to calm the baby

explanation: Watching a feed helps spot any small issues with latch or milk transfer before jumping to extra feeds or supplements. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which sign shows that a baby has a correct, deep latch on the breast?

options.A: The mother feels a sharp pinching sensation with every suck
options.B: The baby's nose is pressed flat against the breast tissue
options.C: More areola is visible above the baby's top lip than below
options.D: The baby's cheeks are pulled inward and dimpling during sucks

explanation: With a deep latch, the baby takes in more of the lower areola, leaving more of the upper areola showing. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h3)

question: Why is pushing a baby's head directly toward the breast a bad idea?

options.A: It often causes the baby to resist and pull away in defense
options.B: It helps align the infant's ears with the maternal shoulders
options.C: It prevents the let-down reflex from occurring too quickly
options.D: It increases the amount of milk produced by the pituitary gland

explanation: Babies naturally pull back when pressure is put on their head, which makes latching much harder. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) for small or vulnerable babies?

options.A: To allow the mother to sleep uninterrupted through the night
options.B: To completely replace the need for expressed breast milk feeds
options.C: To speed up the infant's discharge from the hospital within 24 hours
options.D: To stabilize temperature, heart rate, and encourage feeding readiness

explanation: KMC uses skin-to-skin contact to keep tiny newborns warm and stable while helping them grow and get ready to breastfeed. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h4)

question: A 32-week preterm baby is stable but not yet strong enough to suck and breathe easily at the breast. What is the safest way to feed them?

options.A: Feeding expressed breast milk with a small cup and spoon
options.B: Offering undiluted cow's milk via a standard baby bottle
options.C: Delaying all nutrition until the infant reaches term age
options.D: Forcing the baby to latch onto the breast until they figure it out

explanation: Cup feeding is a safe, clean method that avoids nipple confusion and lets preterms take milk at a safe pace. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the most common cause of sore and cracked nipples while breastfeeding?

options.A: Drinking too much warm fluid during feeds
options.B: Washing the breasts with mild soap and water
options.C: Letting the baby feed more than eight times a day
options.D: Incorrect infant positioning and latching

explanation: A shallow latch puts friction right on the sensitive nipple tip instead of deep in the mouth, leading to pain and cracks. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which breast condition comes with body symptoms like fever and chills, plus a red, painful area on the breast?

options.A: Mastitis
options.B: Engorgement
options.C: Blocked duct
options.D: Colostrum surge

explanation: Mastitis is an inflammation that often brings flu-like body symptoms, unlike a simple blocked duct. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why should you never microwave expressed breast milk?

options.A: It creates dangerous hot spots and destroys immune properties
options.B: It removes all the natural water content from the milk
options.C: It turns the milk completely solid and impossible to feed
options.D: It causes the milk to ferment and turn sour within minutes

explanation: Microwaves heat unevenly, which can burn the baby's mouth, and they destroy important proteins and antibodies in the milk. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h6)

question: How long can freshly expressed breast milk safely sit at room temperature before it needs to be used or put in the fridge?

options.A: Maximum 30 minutes
options.B: Up to 24 hours
options.C: Exactly 12 hours
options.D: Up to 4 hours

explanation: Breast milk has natural antibacterial properties that keep it safe at room temperature for up to four hours. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h6)

question: How can high anxiety in a mother negatively affect breastfeeding?

options.A: It releases adrenaline, which can inhibit the oxytocin-driven let-down reflex
options.B: It changes the chemical composition of colostrum into toxic fluid
options.C: It immediately stops the anterior pituitary gland from producing prolactin forever
options.D: It causes the infant to permanently lose its rooting and sucking reflexes

explanation: Stress triggers adrenaline, which gets in the way of oxytocin and makes it harder for milk to flow out. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a helpful counseling technique when talking to an anxious breastfeeding mother?

options.A: Celebrating small milestones like a successful single feed
options.B: Involving supportive family members in the care plan
options.C: Using active listening and validating her emotional experiences
options.D: Criticizing her technique harshly to force immediate behavioral change

explanation: Harsh criticism only hurts confidence and increases stress; mothers need empathy and gentle guidance. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T2#BMP218_U3_T2_h7)

question: What main body function changes in a newborn that affects how medications leave their body?

options.A: Increased gastric acidity
options.B: Decreased total body fat
options.C: Elevated liver enzyme production
options.D: Changes in how the kidneys clear substances

explanation: Kidney function develops quickly after birth, which changes how the newborn filters and clears medications from the body. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why do midwives check if a drug is safe for the baby before a breastfeeding mother takes it?

options.A: Maternal medications alter the nutritional value of milk
options.B: Newborns metabolize all drugs faster than adults
options.C: Breastfeeding stops completely if drugs are given
options.D: Many drugs can pass through breastmilk to the baby

explanation: Substances in the mother's bloodstream can pass into breastmilk and expose the nursing infant to the drug's effects. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h1)

question: Which medicine used to prevent bleeding after birth should be avoided in a mother with severe high blood pressure?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Ergometrine
options.D: Syntocinon

explanation: Ergometrine causes blood vessels to narrow, which can raise blood pressure to dangerous levels in women with hypertension. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h2)

question: A rural clinic does not have a reliable refrigerator to store oxytocin. Which medicine is the best alternative to prevent heavy bleeding after birth?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Intravenous syntocinon
options.D: Ergometrine

explanation: Misoprostol stays stable at room temperature, making it very useful in clinics without cold storage facilities. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of managing perineal or surgical pain soon after delivery?

options.A: It encourages the mother to walk early and bond with her baby
options.B: It stops normal uterine involution
options.C: It increases breastmilk production volume
options.D: It completely prevents postpartum infection

explanation: When pain is well controlled, the mother can move around easily, care for her newborn, and practice skin-to-skin contact. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h3)

question: Which group of medications is used first for routine pain relief after childbirth?

options.A: Strong narcotic infusions
options.B: Non-opioid analgesics
options.C: Skeletal muscle relaxants
options.D: Broad-spectrum antibiotics

explanation: Medicines like paracetamol safely manage most common postnatal aches and pains without causing heavy sedation. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h3)

question: Within how many hours after delivery should anti-D immunisation be given to an Rh-negative mother to work best?

options.A: 2 weeks
options.B: 1 week
options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 72 hours

explanation: Giving the injection within 72 hours helps clear any fetal blood cells before the mother's immune system reacts to them. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is anti-D immunoglobulin given to an Rh-negative mother after she gives birth?

options.A: To prevent her body from forming antibodies that could harm future pregnancies
options.B: To boost the infant's natural immunity against tetanus
options.C: To treat an active postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: To speed up the shrinking of the postpartum uterus

explanation: The medication stops the mother's immune system from reacting to fetal red blood cells, protecting future babies from blood complications. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h4)

question: After receiving which postnatal vaccine is a mother advised to avoid getting pregnant for at least one month?

options.A: Rubella vaccine
options.B: Hepatitis B vaccine
options.C: Oral polio vaccine
options.D: Tetanus toxoid booster

explanation: Rubella is a live vaccine, so healthcare providers recommend waiting a short period to prevent any risk to an early pregnancy. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h5)

question: Why are women sometimes given a tetanus booster shot right after giving birth?

options.A: To reduce postpartum pain from perineal stitches
options.B: To pass passive immunity directly into breastmilk
options.C: To protect against spores entering through the reproductive tract
options.D: To treat an active postpartum uterine infection

explanation: Postpartum wounds and the open healing uterus can let in tetanus spores, especially in environments where exposure is common. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h5)

question: What specific detail must a midwife always record in the patient chart when giving vaccines or immune globulins?

options.A: Brand of syringe used
options.B: Batch numbers
options.C: Pharmacy room temperature
options.D: Midwife home address

explanation: Batch numbers must be logged for all biological products to ensure they can be traced if any issues arise later. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to teach a mother about normal side effects before she leaves the postnatal ward?

options.A: It prevents unnecessary worry over normal body reactions
options.B: It guarantees she will never experience side effects
options.C: It replaces the need for any professional follow-up
options.D: It stops infants from reacting to maternal medicines

explanation: Knowing what to expect, such as mild soreness or a low fever, helps the mother stay calm and understand what is normal. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T3#BMP218_U3_T3_h6)

question: How long does the postnatal period officially last after childbirth?

options.A: Six weeks
options.B: Six months
options.C: Two weeks
options.D: One year

explanation: The postnatal period is universally defined as the first six weeks following delivery, during which maternal anatomical changes revert to their pre-pregnant state. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is the immediate postnatal transition a critical time for monitoring by midwives?

options.A: Newborns require no further thermal regulation after birth
options.B: Mothers usually regain their full pre-pregnancy weight immediately
options.C: Rapid physiological adjustments occur in both mother and baby
options.D: Uterine involution is fully complete within twenty-four hours

explanation: Both mother and newborn experience intense, rapid biological changes right after birth, making careful observation essential to catch early complications. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h1)

question: What is an effective way to support discharge counseling for mothers with low literacy levels?

options.A: Skipping the counseling session entirely
options.B: Giving them only dense medical textbooks
options.C: Communicating solely through text messages
options.D: Using illustrated educational materials

explanation: Pictures and diagrams help bridge gaps in written literacy, ensuring the mother fully grasps her care instructions. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h2)

question: A midwife is preparing a mother for discharge. Who should ideally be included in the counseling session to enhance home support?

options.A: No one else to maintain strict privacy
options.B: A partner or trusted family member
options.C: Only the hospital security personnel
options.D: An unfamiliar neighbor waiting outside

explanation: Involving family members helps share the responsibility of post-discharge care and ensures reinforcement of advice at home. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is a key maternal danger sign taught during discharge?

options.A: Slight abdominal cramping during breastfeeding
options.B: Mild fatigue after caring for the baby
options.C: Heavy vaginal bleeding soaking two pads per hour
options.D: Gradual lightening of lochia color to pink

explanation: Soaking more than two pads per hour for two hours indicates potential postpartum hemorrhage and requires urgent care. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a danger sign in a newborn?

options.A: Convulsions or abnormal shaking
options.B: Passing regular yellow-brown stools
options.C: Inability to suck or feed at all
options.D: Chest indrawing when breathing

explanation: Yellow-brown stools are normal for a feeding newborn, whereas poor feeding, seizures, and respiratory distress are serious danger signs. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why is adequate fluid intake especially important for a breastfeeding mother?

options.A: It supports adequate milk production
options.B: It stops uterine involution from occurring
options.C: It eliminates the need for perineal care
options.D: It completely prevents postpartum depression

explanation: Breast milk is largely composed of water, so nursing mothers must drink enough fluids to maintain their supply. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h4)

question: How does proper personal hygiene and frequent perineal care help a postpartum woman?

options.A: It prevents puerperal sepsis and wound infection
options.B: It accelerates the return of menstruation
options.C: It guarantees immediate weight loss
options.D: It stops normal lochial discharge completely

explanation: Keeping the perineal area clean reduces the risk of bacteria entering the reproductive tract and causing postpartum infections. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h4)

question: When is the comprehensive postnatal check traditionally scheduled for mother and baby?

options.A: At one year postpartum
options.B: At six weeks postpartum
options.C: At twenty-four hours postpartum
options.D: At six months postpartum

explanation: The six-week visit is the milestone check where the midwife assesses complete physical recovery and reviews family planning. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h5)

question: A mother is being discharged from the postnatal ward. What is the best way to ensure she remembers her follow-up appointment?

options.A: Telling her to come back whenever she feels like it
options.B: Relying entirely on her remembering the verbal date
options.C: Asking her to guess when she should return
options.D: Writing the exact date and time in her maternal record

explanation: Documenting appointments in the patient's personal health card provides a permanent reminder and reduces missed visits. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h5)

question: How should a midwife handle traditional postpartum practices encountered in the community?

options.A: Encourage every cultural practice regardless of the health risk
options.B: Condemn all traditional beliefs immediately without listening
options.C: Ignore them completely and pretend they do not exist
options.D: Respect harmless practices while discouraging harmful ones

explanation: Cultural sensitivity is essential; midwives should validate safe traditions while educating families on practices that cause harm, like cord infections from native applications. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is a harmful cultural practice applied to newborns that midwives must discourage?

options.A: Exclusively breastfeeding on demand
options.B: Applying native concoctions or cow dung to the umbilical cord
options.C: Bathing the baby daily with clean warm water
options.D: Swaddling the baby comfortably for sleep

explanation: Unsterile substances placed on the cord stump introduce bacteria and greatly increase the risk of neonatal tetanus and sepsis. [learn more](BMP218_U3_T4#BMP218_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of admitting a patient to the high-risk antenatal ward?

options.A: Ensuring immediate delivery within twenty-four hours
options.B: Providing intensive surveillance and timely intervention
options.C: Conducting routine screening for low-risk women
options.D: Preparing the patient for permanent family planning

explanation: High-risk wards focus heavily on close monitoring and quick action to catch complications early before they harm mother or baby. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must midwives view a high-risk pregnancy condition as dynamic rather than fixed?

options.A: Patients usually fake their symptoms to stay longer in the ward
options.B: Laboratory values change strictly according to the time of day
options.C: A stable condition can rapidly deteriorate into an emergency
options.D: Hospital policies require daily reassessment of room assignments

explanation: Conditions like gestational diabetes or pre-eclampsia can worsen suddenly, meaning constant vigilance is required from the midwifery team. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which laboratory test is most essential for immediate baseline assessment of a pre-eclamptic patient on admission?

options.A: Thyroid stimulating hormone
options.B: Serum lipid profile
options.C: Urinalysis for protein
options.D: Stool microscopy for ova

explanation: Checking urine protein is a fundamental step to confirm or assess the severity of hypertensive disorders like pre-eclampsia upon arrival. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h2)

question: A newly admitted high-risk pregnant woman has her baseline history taken. Which specific area requires the most urgent attention from the midwife?

options.A: Her personal preference for postnatal infant feeding
options.B: Previous severe obstetric complications or losses
options.C: The distance of her residence from the market square
options.D: Her occupation before the start of the pregnancy

explanation: Past history of severe issues like postpartum haemorrhage or stillbirth directly guides current risk stratification and monitoring plans. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h2)

question: Who serves as the central coordinator of care between the patient and other medical specialists in the ward?

options.A: The hospital pharmacist
options.B: The senior hospital administrator
options.C: The visiting relative
options.D: The midwife

explanation: Midwives spend the most time at the bedside, making them the vital link who coordinates information and care across the whole medical team. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is the midwife's daily report during ward rounds so crucial for high-risk patients?

options.A: Hospital management requires proof of daily staff attendance
options.B: Doctors are not legally allowed to touch the patient without a nurse present
options.C: It replaces the need to keep written bedside medical charts
options.D: Midwives observe subtle trends and changes over twenty-four hours

explanation: Continuous bedside presence allows midwives to notice gradual changes in mood, vitals, or symptoms that a brief doctor visit might miss. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which assessment is a direct measure of fetal well-being that the mother can track herself in the ward?

options.A: Symphysis-fundal height
options.B: Maternal blood pressure
options.C: Daily fetal kick counts
options.D: Urine protein dipstick

explanation: Tracking fetal movements gives the mother an active, direct way to help monitor her baby's daily well-being in the ward. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h4)

question: When is strict fluid intake and output charting most critical in the high-risk antenatal ward?

options.A: When managing a patient with severe pre-eclampsia
options.B: When preparing a patient for a routine ultrasound scan
options.C: During routine antenatal booking for a healthy primigravida
options.D: Before administering routine routine tetanus toxoid vaccination

explanation: Pre-eclampsia affects kidney function and fluid balance, making careful monitoring of urine output essential to prevent renal failure or pulmonary oedema. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of administering corticosteroids to a high-risk mother at risk of preterm birth?

options.A: To stop active uterine contractions
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure
options.C: To accelerate fetal lung maturity
options.D: To prevent maternal eclamptic fits

explanation: Corticosteroids help the baby's lungs develop faster, reducing breathing difficulties if born prematurely. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h5)

question: A midwife is caring for a patient receiving an intravenous infusion of magnesium sulphate. Which clinical check is most critical to perform regularly?

options.A: Testing fasting blood glucose levels every hour
options.B: Assessing deep tendon reflexes and respiration
options.C: Measuring visual acuity and pupillary light response
options.D: Checking for active bowel sounds and abdominal pain

explanation: Magnesium toxicity depresses the central nervous system, so checking reflexes and breathing rates helps catch dangerous overdose early. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is placing a seizing or unstable pregnant patient in the left lateral position a standard emergency action?

options.A: It relieves pressure on the major blood vessels and prevents aspiration
options.B: It is the only comfortable sleeping position allowed in the hospital
options.C: It stops uterine contractions permanently without needing drugs
options.D: It allows the doctor to perform an immediate vaginal examination

explanation: The left lateral position stops the uterus from pressing on the inferior vena cava, keeping blood flowing to the heart and stopping vomit from entering the lungs. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of emergency preparedness in an antenatal ward?

options.A: Conducting regular team emergency drills for staff
options.B: Having working suction machines available at the bedside
options.C: Ensuring oxygen delivery systems are fully functional
options.D: Keeping all emergency drug trays locked away in the pharmacy

explanation: Emergency drugs must be immediately accessible right on the ward, not locked away in a distant pharmacy, during a crisis. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h6)

question: How does providing clear explanations of medical procedures directly help a high-risk antenatal patient?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any pain relief medications
options.B: It reduces anxiety and builds trust with the healthcare team
options.C: It shortens the total length of hospital stay by half
options.D: It prevents the onset of gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Fear of the unknown fuels stress; explaining things clearly helps calm the patient and fosters a cooperative, trusting relationship. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is a common psychological challenge experienced by women admitted for long periods in high-risk wards?

options.A: Sudden loss of all long-term memory function
options.B: Anxiety, depression, and emotional fatigue
options.C: Complete indifference to their own health status
options.D: Aggressive hostility toward all newborn babies

explanation: Being away from home, family, and normal routines while worrying about pregnancy outcomes takes a heavy emotional toll. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h7)

question: When should discharge planning ideally begin for a high-risk pregnant woman?

options.A: During the postnatal check-up
options.B: Twenty-four hours before leaving
options.C: When labor pains officially start
options.D: On the day of admission

explanation: Planning early ensures that education, warning signs, and follow-up arrangements are properly addressed well before the patient leaves the hospital. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h8)

question: Why is a comprehensive written and verbal handover necessary when transferring a patient to the labor ward?

options.A: It allows the labor ward staff to cancel previous treatment plans
options.B: It ensures continuity of care and prevents critical details from being missed
options.C: It proves that the antenatal ward staff finished their shift on time
options.D: It is simply a legal formality required for billing purposes

explanation: A thorough handover communicates vital clinical facts, risks, and active treatments so the receiving team can manage the patient safely without delays. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T1#BMP315_U1_T1_h8)

question: What is the main reason for using an advanced partograph in high-risk labor?

options.A: To document routine postpartum contraceptive choices
options.B: To replace the need for physical pelvic examinations
options.C: To calculate the exact financial cost of delivery
options.D: To act as an early warning system for complications

explanation: An advanced partograph provides detailed monitoring to help clinicians spot deviations from normal labor progress early. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why might a standard partograph not be enough for a high-risk laboring woman?

options.A: It only measures maternal temperature and pulse rate
options.B: It is illegal to use for patients with high blood pressure
options.C: It lacks specific parameters needed for complicated scenarios
options.D: It requires a computer to function properly in the ward

explanation: High-risk cases involve complex factors like severe pre-eclampsia that need more detailed tracking than a basic chart provides. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h1)

question: What does a severe degree of skull bone molding on the partograph mean?

options.A: Intense compression of the fetal head in a tight pelvis
options.B: An immature gestational age of the unborn baby
options.C: Rapid dilation of the cervix without any obstruction
options.D: Normal descent of the fetus through a wide birth canal

explanation: Severe molding shows the fetal skull bones overlapping significantly as they struggle to fit through a contracted pelvis. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h2)

question: A laboring woman's cervical dilation graph moves to the right of the action line with severe caput and molding. What is the best interpretation?

options.A: Labor is obstructed and requires immediate senior review
options.B: Normal progress is occurring and staff should wait four hours
options.C: Contractions are too weak and require immediate oxytocin
options.D: The patient is ready to push and deliver spontaneously

explanation: Crossing the action line with signs of mechanical stress points directly to obstructed labor, demanding urgent intervention. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h2)

question: What does thick meconium-stained amniotic fluid usually suggest during labor?

options.A: Advanced maternal age during pregnancy
options.B: Inadequate fluid intake by the mother
options.C: Fetal hypoxia and potential distress
options.D: A normal and expected digestive process

explanation: Thick meconium release is often triggered by oxygen shortage, signaling that the baby is under stress. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is it important to test a laboring woman's urine for acetone during a long, complicated labor?

options.A: To detect dehydration and starvation from lack of energy
options.B: To confirm the presence of a urinary tract infection
options.C: To check if the kidneys are filtering excess protein
options.D: To measure the exact fetal heart rate through metabolites

explanation: When a mother goes without food and water during prolonged labor, her body burns fat stores, producing acetone in the urine. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h3)

question: How many hours to the right of the alert line is the action line usually placed?

options.A: Four hours
options.B: Six hours
options.C: Two hours
options.D: Twelve hours

explanation: The action line is drawn parallel to the alert line, shifted four hours to the right to mark the limit for safe delay. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h4)

question: What must be done right away when a patient's cervical dilation crosses the action line?

options.A: Stop all fetal heart monitoring to reduce maternal stress
options.B: Definitive management and senior medical review
options.C: Discharge the patient home for rest and re-evaluation
options.D: Wait another four hours to see if progress resumes

explanation: Crossing the action line means labor is abnormally slow, requiring a formal assessment and intervention plan from senior staff. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h4)

question: Who has the main responsibility for starting the chain of survival when a problem is found?

options.A: The attending midwife
options.B: The hospital accountant
options.C: The pharmaceutical supplier
options.D: The incoming pregnant patient

explanation: Midwives monitor labor continuously and are the first to identify warning signs, making their prompt escalation vital. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is preparation across multiple departments necessary during a severe labor complication?

options.A: It minimizes dangerous delays in executing emergency delivery
options.B: It prevents the need for any blood transfusions later
options.C: It allows the medical team to avoid documenting the event
options.D: It ensures all paperwork is completed before surgery starts

explanation: Time is critical in obstructed labor; preparing IV lines, blood, and theater at the same time saves precious minutes. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T2#BMP315_U1_T2_h5)

question: What must be confirmed about the cervix before a vacuum extraction can begin?

options.A: Cervical status does not affect vacuum use
options.B: It must be at least 8cm dilated
options.C: It only needs to be soft and effaced
options.D: It must be fully dilated to 10cm

explanation: Full cervical dilatation is required to prevent tearing the cervix when the baby's head passes through. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h1)

question: A woman has been pushing for two hours with no progress, and her bladder is full. What should the midwife do before considering a vacuum delivery?

options.A: Instruct her to keep pushing harder
options.B: Administer oxytocin immediately
options.C: Drain the bladder with a catheter
options.D: Prepare the operating room for a cesarean section

explanation: An empty bladder is necessary because a full bladder can block the baby's descent and cause injury during the procedure. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h1)

question: How does the midwife test the suction before applying the vacuum cup to the baby's head?

options.A: By blocking the cup with the palm of the hand
options.B: By placing the cup directly onto the maternal abdomen
options.C: By testing the pressure against a sterile gauze pad
options.D: By listening for air leaks near the mechanical pump

explanation: Placing the palm over the cup seals the opening so the midwife can verify that the pump builds and holds proper negative pressure. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h2)

question: Why is testing the vacuum equipment beforehand an important responsibility for the midwife?

options.A: It ensures the fetal heart rate remains completely steady
options.B: It numbs the birth canal to reduce maternal pain
options.C: It prevents sudden equipment failure during the delivery
options.D: It automatically calculates the weight of the baby

explanation: Checking the pump, tubing, and cup ensures that suction works properly before pulling the baby's head. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h2)

question: Where should the vacuum cup be placed on the baby's head to encourage proper flexion?

options.A: As close to the fetal face and forehead as possible
options.B: Randomly anywhere on the parietal bones
options.C: Over the flexion point near the posterior fontanelle
options.D: Directly on top of the anterior fontanelle

explanation: Placing the cup over the flexion point helps the head tilt forward during pulls, reducing the diameter passing through the pelvis. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is a key check the midwife must perform immediately after placing the vacuum cup on the scalp?

options.A: Confirm that the baby is crying inside the womb
options.B: Measure the exact depth of the vaginal vault
options.C: Check that no maternal tissues are trapped under the rim
options.D: Ensure the mother's blood pressure has dropped

explanation: Sweeping a finger around the rim ensures the vaginal wall or cervix is not caught, preventing pain and tearing when suction is applied. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h3)

question: When should pulling traction be applied during a vacuum-assisted delivery?

options.A: Only during maternal pushing and uterine contractions
options.B: Whenever the fetal heart rate begins to accelerate
options.C: Continuously throughout the entire labor process
options.D: Only in the resting phase between contractions

explanation: Pulling during contractions works with the mother's natural pushing reflex to guide the baby down the birth canal safely. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why must the midwife avoid twisting or rotating the vacuum cup while pulling?

options.A: It reverses the baby's heartbeat during labor
options.B: It will immediately rupture the mother's uterus
options.C: It can cause severe scalp damage and cup detachment
options.D: It pushes the baby back up into the abdominal cavity

explanation: Vacuum cups are designed only for straight traction; twisting motions tear the scalp skin and break the vacuum seal. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended number of cup detachments or pull failures before stopping a vacuum procedure?

options.A: Three
options.B: Five
options.C: One
options.D: Ten

explanation: Exceeding three pop-offs or failed pulls indicates that the vacuum method is not working and risks fetal injury if continued. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h5)

question: What should the clinical team do immediately after deciding to stop a failed vacuum extraction?

options.A: Leave the vacuum cup attached while resting
options.B: Wait another two hours for spontaneous birth
options.C: Prepare for an emergency cesarean section
options.D: Administer a high dose of oral pain relievers

explanation: If a vacuum delivery cannot be completed safely, the baby is delivered via alternative means, usually a cesarean section, without delay. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the normal, harmless swelling that typically appears on the newborn's scalp right after a vacuum delivery called?

options.A: Subgaleal hematoma
options.B: Caput succedaneum
options.C: Chignon
options.D: Hydrocephalus

explanation: The chignon is a temporary, localized swelling on the scalp caused by the negative pressure of the vacuum cup, which resolves within days. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why must the midwife inspect the mother's birth canal after a vacuum delivery?

options.A: To confirm the bladder has completely refilled
options.B: To measure the exact weight of the placenta
options.C: To check for hidden lacerations and perineal trauma
options.D: To ensure the uterus contracts into a firm ball

explanation: Instrumental deliveries place extra mechanical stress on maternal soft tissues, making tears and hematomas more likely. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T3#BMP315_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the main reason a midwife performs an MROP?

options.A: To measure the volume of amniotic fluid
options.B: To remove a retained placenta
options.C: To speed up the second stage of labor
options.D: To repair a severe perineal tear

explanation: MROP is done when the placenta stays inside the uterus instead of coming out naturally after birth. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why is a delayed third stage of labor dangerous for a new mother?

options.A: It leads to permanent high blood pressure
options.B: It causes immediate infection of the fallopian tubes
options.C: It prevents the baby from breastfeeding successfully
options.D: It greatly increases the risk of severe bleeding

explanation: When the placenta does not come out, the uterus cannot clamp down tightly, which can lead to heavy and dangerous bleeding. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h1)

question: When active management is used, at what time is the third stage usually considered prolonged?

options.A: 60 minutes
options.B: 10 minutes
options.C: 5 minutes
options.D: 30 minutes

explanation: Standard guidelines state that if the placenta is not delivered by 30 minutes after birth, it needs manual removal. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h2)

question: A mother gives birth, and 15 minutes later she starts passing large blood clots with heavy bleeding while the placenta is still inside. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Prepare for immediate manual removal due to hemorrhage
options.B: Wait another 15 minutes to reach the standard 30-minute mark
options.C: Send the patient home since the baby is already born safely
options.D: Encourage the mother to walk around the ward to aid delivery

explanation: Heavy bleeding means you cannot wait for the 30-minute mark; urgent action is needed to stop the bleeding and protect the mother. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why must a midwife wear sterile gloves that reach past the elbows during an MROP?

options.A: To keep the entire forearm entering the birth canal sterile
options.B: To make it easier to push the baby out of the uterus
options.C: To prevent the midwife from feeling any cold instruments
options.D: To protect the mother's abdomen from cold air in the room

explanation: Since the hand and forearm go deep inside the uterus, wearing gloves past the elbow prevents bacteria from entering. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which preparation is vital to manage potential shock during an MROP?

options.A: Placing a heavy sandbag directly on the patient's chest
options.B: Turning off all lights in the labor ward to calm the patient
options.C: Giving the patient a heavy meal to keep her energy high
options.D: Securing a large-bore intravenous line for fluids and drugs

explanation: Retained placental tissue combined with open blood vessels carries a high risk of shock, so having an IV line ready is essential. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the job of the hand placed on the mother's lower abdomen during an MROP?

options.A: To massage the mother's hips and relieve her back pain
options.B: To check the mother's pulse rate from the abdominal wall
options.C: To help push the placenta down faster by pressing hard
options.D: To support the uterus and prevent uterine inversion

explanation: Pressing gently on the abdomen stabilizes the uterus so it does not turn inside out when the placenta is pulled out. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h4)

question: How should the midwife's hand be shaped when first entering the cervix during an MROP?

options.A: Cone-shaped with fingers held close together
options.B: Clenched tightly into a hard fist
options.C: Open flat with fingers spread wide apart
options.D: Pointing only with the index finger extended

explanation: A cone shape helps the hand pass smoothly through the cervix into the uterus with minimal discomfort. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a known complication of an MROP?

options.A: Severe intrauterine infection
options.B: Persistent postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Perforation of the uterine wall
options.D: Development of gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Gestational diabetes is related to pregnancy hormones, not a surgical complication of removing a placenta. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h5)

question: Why do leftover placental pieces cause ongoing bleeding after an MROP?

options.A: Leftover fragments actively produce new red blood cells
options.B: The cervix closes completely and traps the blood inside
options.C: Retained tissue prevents the uterine muscle fibers from clamping down
options.D: Retained pieces cause the mother's blood pressure to rise too high

explanation: The uterus must contract tightly to stop bleeding. Any leftover tissue acts like a wedge, keeping the blood vessels open. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h5)

question: How often should vital signs be checked immediately after a stable patient undergoes an MROP?

options.A: Every 15 minutes for the first hour
options.B: Once a day before discharge
options.C: Only when the patient complains of dizziness
options.D: Once every six hours

explanation: Frequent monitoring during the first hour helps catch hidden bleeding or a dropping blood pressure early. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h6)

question: A mother who just had an MROP has a soft, boggy uterus and moderate vaginal bleeding. What is the immediate midwifery action?

options.A: Tell the mother to rest and check her again tomorrow morning
options.B: Encourage the mother to drink plenty of cold water
options.C: Remove the intravenous line to let the patient relax
options.D: Massage the uterine fundus and administer prescribed uterotonics

explanation: A soft uterus needs physical massage and medications like uterotonics to contract properly and stop the bleeding. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T4#BMP315_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main goal of performing a perineal repair after childbirth?

options.A: Speeding up the return of normal menstrual cycles
options.B: Preventing future occurrences of gestational diabetes
options.C: Halting postpartum lochia flow completely
options.D: Restoring normal anatomical alignment of pelvic tissues

explanation: Suturing brings torn muscle and skin back to their original positions so proper healing and function can happen. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which type of perineal trauma is most likely to be left to heal without sutures?

options.A: A deep third-degree tear involving the anal sphincter
options.B: A small, superficial first-degree tear without active bleeding
options.C: A gaping second-degree tear with heavy bleeding
options.D: A midline episiotomy extending toward the rectum

explanation: Minor surface tears that do not bleed much often heal very well on their own without requiring stitches. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which tissue layer of the birth canal is typically closed first during a perineal repair?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat
options.B: Vaginal mucosa
options.C: Perineal skin
options.D: Levator ani muscle

explanation: Repair starts at the apex of the vaginal wound inside the canal, closing the mucosa first before moving outward. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is it clinically important to properly stitch the deep perineal muscle layer?

options.A: To stop the uterus from undergoing normal postpartum involution
options.B: To ensure the lochia discharge changes from red to white
options.C: To restore pelvic floor support and prevent future incontinence
options.D: To prevent the baby from experiencing shoulder dystocia later

explanation: Reconnecting the muscles ensures the pelvic floor regains its strength, which protects against long-term problems like prolapse and urine leakage. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h2)

question: What structure is involved in a second-degree perineal tear that is NOT involved in a first-degree tear?

options.A: Vaginal skin
options.B: Anal sphincter
options.C: Perineal muscle
options.D: Rectal mucosa

explanation: A second-degree tear extends deeper to include the perineal muscles, whereas a first-degree tear only affects skin and mucosa. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h3)

question: A postpartum woman has a tear that extends through the anal sphincter and exposes the rectal lumen. What classification does this represent?

options.A: Fourth-degree tear
options.B: Second-degree tear
options.C: Third-degree tear
options.D: First-degree tear

explanation: When the tear involves both the anal sphincter complex and the inner lining of the rectum, it is classified as a fourth-degree tear. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h3)

question: What safety step must a midwife always perform immediately before injecting local anesthetic into the perineum?

options.A: Dilute the medication with equal parts sterile water
options.B: Apply a cold pack directly over the injection site
options.C: Warm the solution to match normal body temperature
options.D: Aspirate the plunger to check for blood vessel entry

explanation: Aspiration ensures the needle is not inside a blood vessel, preventing accidental intravenous injection of the anesthetic drug. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is it necessary to wait a few minutes after injecting local anesthesia before starting the repair?

options.A: To give the placenta time to separate from the uterine wall
options.B: To allow the vaginal tissues time to swell up for easier grasping
options.C: To give the drug time to numb the nerve endings effectively
options.D: To let the local bleeding stop completely on its own

explanation: Local anesthetics require a brief latency period to block nerve transmission so the patient does not feel pain during suturing. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h4)

question: Where should the midwife place the first stitch when repairing a vaginal mucosal tear?

options.A: At the lower edge near the anal sphincter
options.B: Directly at the midpoint of the hymenal ring
options.C: About 1 centimeter above the apex of the wound
options.D: Right on the skin of the perineal body

explanation: Starting slightly above the apex ensures that any bleeding vessels hidden at the very top of the tear are securely tied off. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why is a final rectal examination performed routinely at the end of a perineal repair?

options.A: To stimulate normal bowel movements after the delivery
options.B: To check that no suture has accidentally pierced the rectal mucosa
options.C: To measure the exact depth of the perineal body
options.D: To clear out any retained lochia in the vaginal vault

explanation: Feeling the rectal wall ensures a stitch has not mistakenly passed through into the rectum, which would cause infection or fistula formation. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the primary benefit of applying an ice pack to the perineum during the first 24 hours after repair?

options.A: Speeding up the closure of the cervix
options.B: Preventing the onset of postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Reducing local swelling and discomfort
options.D: Stopping postpartum uterine contractions

explanation: Cold therapy constricts local blood vessels, which helps bring down tissue edema and dulls pain receptors in the perineum. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why is encouraging high-fiber food and fluids an important part of post-repair management?

options.A: To prevent constipation and reduce straining on the sutures
options.B: To help the uterus return to its pre-pregnant size faster
options.C: To prevent postpartum depression and fatigue
options.D: To increase the production of breast milk for the baby

explanation: Soft stools prevent the mother from straining during bowel movements, protecting the newly repaired perineal muscles and wound edges. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T5#BMP315_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the target time frame for delivering a baby via a Category 1 emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: Within 4 hours
options.B: Within 30 minutes
options.C: Within 1 hour
options.D: Within 2 hours

explanation: Category 1 caesareans are done for immediate threats to life, needing surgical delivery within thirty minutes to protect the mother and baby. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why do midwives need to accurately classify the urgency of an emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: It helps prioritize theatre workflow and mobilization of the emergency team
options.B: It dictates whether general anesthesia must be avoided entirely
options.C: It removes the need to obtain formal written consent from the patient
options.D: It determines the exact type of skin incision the surgeon will use

explanation: Knowing the category lets the surgical and nursing teams prepare the operating room and patient with the right level of urgency. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h1)

question: What size of intravenous cannula is usually secured during emergency pre-operative prep?

options.A: Midline butterfly needle
options.B: Central venous line only
options.C: Large-bore cannula
options.D: Small paediatric cannula

explanation: A large-bore intravenous cannula allows for rapid fluid replacement and blood transfusion if heavy bleeding happens during surgery. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h2)

question: A frightened laboring woman needs an emergency Caesarean section but refuses to sign the consent form out of panic. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Ask a relative to sign the form without informing the patient
options.B: Cancel the procedure and allow her to attempt a spontaneous vaginal birth
options.C: Provide calm reassurance and briefly explain the life-saving reason for the surgery
options.D: Proceed with the surgery immediately without any form of consent

explanation: Calm communication helps ease panic, allowing the patient to understand the emergency and give informed consent. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why is a catheter used to empty the urinary bladder right before an emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: To stimulate regular uterine contractions during the surgery
options.B: To measure the exact volume of amniotic fluid produced
options.C: To eliminate the need for any post-operative urine monitoring
options.D: To prevent accidental surgical injury to the bladder

explanation: An empty bladder moves away from the lower uterine segment, lowering the chance of it being accidentally cut during the surgery. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h3)

question: Which of these items is usually NOT removed from a patient before she goes into the operating theatre for a Caesarean section?

options.A: Removable dentures and false teeth
options.B: Underwear and synthetic garments
options.C: Metallic jewelry and body piercings
options.D: Corrective spectacles or hearing aids

explanation: Essential items like spectacles or hearing aids are kept with the patient until anesthesia so she can communicate clearly, while jewelry and dentures are removed for safety. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h3)

question: What is the midwife's main responsibility right after the baby is born during an emergency Caesarean section?

options.A: Immediately transfer the baby to the neonatal intensive care unit
options.B: Complete the surgical instrument count with the scrub nurse
options.C: Administer intravenous oxytocin directly to the newborn infant
options.D: Receive, dry, assess, and provide initial resuscitation for the newborn

explanation: The midwife cares for the newborn immediately, making sure the airway is clear and the baby is warm and breathing well. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why is keeping a newborn warm right after a Caesarean birth so important?

options.A: It replaces the need for routine vitamin K prophylaxis administration
options.B: It directly prevents the development of neonatal jaundice
options.C: It prevents rapid heat loss and dangerous cold stress in the neonate
options.D: It ensures the baby passes meconium within the first hour of life

explanation: Newborns lose heat fast through evaporation; drying and warming them prevents hypothermia and other health issues. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h4)

question: How often should a mother's vital signs be checked during the first hour after a Caesarean section?

options.A: Every 2 hours
options.B: Once at the end of the hour
options.C: Every 15 minutes
options.D: Every 30 minutes

explanation: Checking vital signs every fifteen minutes in the first hour helps the midwife catch early signs of bleeding or anesthesia issues. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h5)

question: What does a soft, boggy uterine fundus mean when found during post-operative recovery?

options.A: It suggests that the surgical wound has become infected
options.B: It shows that the indwelling urinary catheter needs immediate removal
options.C: It indicates poor uterine contraction and a high risk of postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: It is a normal physiological finding after regional spinal anesthesia

explanation: A firm fundus squeezes blood vessels shut, but a soft fundus means the muscle is relaxed and bleeding might happen. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h5)

question: When is the indwelling urinary catheter usually taken out after an uncomplicated Caesarean section?

options.A: Immediately upon arrival in the recovery room
options.B: Only after the skin stitches are removed
options.C: After exactly 7 days in the ward
options.D: Within 24 hours post-surgery

explanation: Removing the catheter within twenty-four hours lowers the risk of urinary tract infection and helps the patient start moving and passing urine on her own. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is good pain relief a clinical priority after a Caesarean section, beyond just making the mother comfortable?

options.A: It enables the mother to cough, breathe deeply, and move around early
options.B: It stimulates immediate breast milk production in the mammary glands
options.C: It speeds up the complete involution of the postpartum uterus
options.D: It directly prevents the formation of internal abdominal adhesions

explanation: Good pain relief removes the barrier of incisional pain, letting the patient move and do breathing exercises to prevent chest infections and clots. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the main medical benefit of encouraging early movement after a Caesarean section?

options.A: Rapid closure of the internal uterine surgical scar tissue
options.B: Prevention of venous thromboembolism and deep vein thrombosis
options.C: Prevention of postpartum emotional baby blues
options.D: Immediate restoration of normal pre-pregnancy hormone levels

explanation: Moving early improves blood flow in the legs, which stops dangerous blood clots from forming in the veins. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h7)

question: A postpartum mother recovering from an emergency Caesarean section complains of sudden left calf pain, swelling, and tenderness on her second day post-op. What should the midwife suspect?

options.A: Uterine subinvolution
options.B: Normal postpartum muscle cramp
options.C: Deep vein thrombosis
options.D: Superficial wound dehiscence

explanation: Calf pain, swelling, and tenderness on one side are classic signs of deep vein thrombosis, which needs an urgent medical review. [learn more](BMP315_U1_T6#BMP315_U1_T6_h7)

question: What blood pressure reading is used to diagnose severe preeclampsia?

options.A: 160/110 mmHg or higher
options.B: 150/100 mmHg or higher
options.C: 170/120 mmHg or higher
options.D: 140/90 mmHg or higher

explanation: A blood pressure of 160/110 mmHg or higher measured twice is a key sign used to diagnose severe preeclampsia. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why might a pregnant woman with severe preeclampsia feel pain in her upper right belly?

options.A: Severe gastric reflux caused by the enlarging uterus
options.B: Irritation of the lower lung lobes by the diaphragm
options.C: Stretching of the liver capsule from inflammation
options.D: Infection of the gall bladder due to concentrated bile

explanation: Swelling and reduced blood flow in the liver stretch its outer covering, known as Glisson's capsule, causing pain in the upper right abdomen. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why should a pregnant woman having a seizure be turned onto her side?

options.A: To allow direct viewing of the uterine contractions
options.B: To speed up the absorption of oral emergency medicines
options.C: To make it easier to insert a padded tongue depressor
options.D: To prevent aspiration and maintain blood flow to the placenta

explanation: Placing her on her side keeps vomit out of her airway and stops the heavy uterus from pressing on major blood vessels. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h2)

question: What action must a midwife avoid during an active seizure?

options.A: Turning the body gently onto the side to keep the airway open
options.B: Placing a hard object into the patient's clenched mouth
options.C: Calling out loudly for immediate multidisciplinary assistance
options.D: Administering humidified oxygen through a tight face mask

explanation: Forcing objects into the mouth can break teeth, cut gums, and make it harder for the patient to breathe. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h2)

question: At what blood pressure level should urgent blood pressure treatment start in severe preeclampsia?

options.A: 130/80 mmHg
options.B: 140/90 mmHg

explanation: Urgent treatment is started when blood pressure reaches 160/110 mmHg or higher to help protect the mother from a stroke. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main risk of lowering a preeclamptic patient's blood pressure too quickly?

options.A: Immediate triggering of another generalized seizure
options.B: Sudden reduction of blood flow to the placenta
options.C: Rapid onset of severe gestational diabetes mellitus
options.D: Permanent damage to the maternal heart valves

explanation: Dropping blood pressure too fast can reduce blood flow to the baby because placental blood vessels cannot adjust instantly. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of giving magnesium sulfate in eclampsia?

options.A: Speed up the softening and dilation of the cervix
options.B: Eliminating excess protein from the maternal urine
options.C: Lowering high blood pressure down to normal
options.D: Preventing and controlling convulsive seizures

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is given specifically to stop seizures and prevent new ones from starting. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h4)

question: How does magnesium sulfate work to stop seizures?

options.A: By blocking potassium channels in the skeletal muscles
options.B: By acting as a calcium antagonist to block brain receptors
options.C: By increasing the amount of sodium entering nerve cells
options.D: By destroying extra red blood cells circulating in the brain

explanation: Magnesium blocks calcium in the brain, which calms nerve cells and stops abnormal electrical activity. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is the total initial starting dose of magnesium sulfate in the standard Pritchard regimen?

options.A: 4 grams total
options.B: 14 grams total
options.C: 20 grams total
options.D: 10 grams total

explanation: The starting dose includes 4 grams given through a vein and 10 grams given in the muscles, adding up to 14 grams. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h5)

question: A patient is due for her magnesium sulfate maintenance dose, but her breathing rate is 10 breaths per minute. What should the midwife do?

options.A: Proceed with the injection because seizures are worse
options.B: Withhold the dose and report to the doctor immediately
options.C: Give half the normal maintenance dose to be safe
options.D: Administer a dose of oral calcium gluconate right away

explanation: A breathing rate under 16 breaths per minute is a sign of magnesium toxicity. The dose must be held and the doctor called. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which sign is usually the earliest indicator that a patient has too much magnesium in their system?

options.A: Complete cessation of urine output
options.B: Sudden spike in blood pressure
options.C: Loss of deep tendon reflexes
options.D: Severe chest pain and palpitations

explanation: Knee reflexes disappear before breathing slows down, making it an early warning sign of a high magnesium level. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the specific antidote used to reverse magnesium sulfate toxicity?

options.A: Naloxone hydrochloride
options.B: Atropine sulfate
options.C: Protamine sulfate
options.D: Calcium gluconate

explanation: Calcium gluconate works against magnesium to quickly reverse breathing problems and muscle weakness. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why should a midwife avoid holding down a patient forcefully during a seizure?

options.A: It triggers longer and more severe seizures
options.B: It stops the magnesium sulfate from working
options.C: It can cause bone fractures and torn muscles
options.D: It cuts off the supply of oxygen to the brain

explanation: Using physical force against strong, involuntary muscle spasms can easily injure the patient's bones and muscles. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which of these actions should NOT be done right after a seizure stops?

options.A: Forcing the jaws open to insert a metal airway
options.B: Clearing excess mucus gently using oral suction
options.C: Administering oxygen through a clean face mask
options.D: Recording the duration and features of the fit

explanation: Forcing the mouth open during or after a seizure damages teeth and tissues and should not be done. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the only true cure for preeclampsia and eclampsia?

options.A: Delivery of the baby and placenta
options.B: Complete bed rest for two weeks
options.C: High doses of oral multivitamin tablets
options.D: Strict reduction of dietary salt

explanation: Symptoms of preeclampsia only go away after the placenta is delivered, because the placenta is what causes the condition. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h8)

question: A patient at 31 weeks is stabilized after a seizure, but then shows signs of fluid in her lungs. What is the next best step?

options.A: Delay delivery for 48 hours to complete steroid coverage
options.B: Stop all magnesium infusions and discharge the patient home
options.C: Increase intravenous fluids to flush out the lungs
options.D: Proceed with emergency delivery regardless of gestation

explanation: Serious complications like fluid in the lungs mean the pregnancy must be ended right away to protect the mother's life. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T1#BMP315_U2_T1_h8)

question: What amount of blood loss is traditionally used to define a primary postpartum haemorrhage after a vaginal birth?

options.A: Exceeding 500 mL
options.B: Exactly 250 mL
options.C: Exceeding 1,000 mL
options.D: More than 2,000 mL

explanation: Primary PPH is defined as blood loss greater than 500 mL within the first 24 hours following a vaginal delivery. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why can estimating blood loss just by looking at it be tricky during a delivery?

options.A: It usually leads to a severe underestimation of the actual volume lost.
options.B: It causes midwives to delay starting intravenous fluids unnecessarily.
options.C: It forces the surgical team to perform a premature emergency hysterectomy.
options.D: It makes the placenta separate much faster than normal physiological rates.

explanation: Fluids spread out and soak into drapes or pool on the floor, making visual guesses much lower than the actual amount lost. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which size of intravenous cannula is best for quickly replacing fluids during a heavy PPH?

options.A: Central line of any size
options.B: Small-bore 22G or 24G
options.C: Midline catheter of 20G
options.D: Large-bore 16G or 18G

explanation: Large-bore cannulas allow fluids and blood to flow in quickly when a mother is bleeding heavily. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h2)

question: Why is keeping a mother warm an important part of managing heavy blood loss?

options.A: Cold environments make the intravenous lines collapse faster.
options.B: Hypothermia worsens blood clotting problems and increases bleeding.
options.C: Low body temperature stops the uterine muscles from relaxing.
options.D: Warming the patient prevents the placenta from retaining fragments.

explanation: Cold body temperatures interfere with the body's natural ability to form clots, which can make bleeding harder to stop. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which medication should be avoided when treating a PPH in a mother with severe pre-eclampsia?

options.A: Ergometrine
options.B: Carboprost
options.C: Misoprostol
options.D: Oxytocin

explanation: Ergometrine constricts blood vessels throughout the body, which can cause a dangerous spike in blood pressure for hypertensive women. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h3)

question: A mother with severe asthma is experiencing a heavy postpartum hemorrhage that is not responding to initial drugs. Which medication should the team avoid?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Misoprostol
options.C: Carboprost
options.D: Tranexamic acid

explanation: Carboprost can cause the airways to narrow, making it unsafe for patients with a history of asthma. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h3)

question: How does an intrauterine balloon stop bleeding mechanically?

options.A: It releases strong chemical hormones that force the cervix to close tightly.
options.B: It applies direct outward pressure against the bleeding walls of the uterus.
options.C: It completely blocks blood flow through the main renal arteries.
options.D: It absorbs all circulating blood platelets directly into its rubber lining.

explanation: The inflated balloon pushes outward against the uterine walls, pressing on open blood vessels to slow or stop the bleeding. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is it important to keep the drainage channel open when using an intrauterine balloon?

options.A: To prevent hidden blood from collecting inside the uterus without the team noticing.
options.B: To allow the midwife to inject fresh oxytocin directly through the catheter.
options.C: To make it easier to pull the balloon out after twenty-four hours have passed.
options.D: To ensure the patient can still pass urine normally while resting in bed.

explanation: An open drainage tube ensures that any ongoing bleeding flows out where the team can see it, rather than building up silently inside. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the main goal of doing a B-Lynch suture during a major postpartum hemorrhage?

options.A: To permanently tie off both main uterine arteries to stop blood supply
options.B: To mechanically compress the uterine walls together and preserve fertility
options.C: To remove the entire muscular body of the uterus through the vagina
options.D: To repair deep lacerations found along the lateral walls of the cervix

explanation: The B-Lynch suture pulls the walls of the uterus together to stop bleeding from atony while keeping the uterus intact for future pregnancies. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which statement is NOT a requirement for performing a B-Lynch suture?

options.A: Using an appropriate absorbable suture material on a round-bodied needle
options.B: Ensuring the bleeding is primarily due to uterine atony rather than trauma
options.C: Performing a laparotomy to access the external surface of the uterus
options.D: Confirming that the patient has completed her family and wants no more children

explanation: A B-Lynch suture is specifically chosen because it preserves future fertility, so having completed a family is not a requirement. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the final surgical treatment used when bleeding from the uterus cannot be controlled by any other method?

options.A: Bimanual uterine compression
options.B: Emergency obstetric hysterectomy
options.C: Intrauterine balloon placement
options.D: Application of a B-Lynch suture

explanation: Removing the uterus is a lifesaving measure used as a last resort when all other conservative efforts fail to stop the bleeding. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h6)

question: A patient continues to bleed heavily despite trying bimanual compression, medications, a balloon, and a B-Lynch suture. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Perform manual removal of the placenta a second time
options.B: Remove all intravenous lines and transfer the patient home
options.C: Proceed immediately to emergency obstetric hysterectomy
options.D: Wait another two hours to see if oxytocin starts working

explanation: When all conservative measures fail to stop the bleeding, prompt removal of the uterus prevents fatal shock. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h6)

question: Where should a mother who has just survived a severe PPH be transferred for close monitoring?

options.A: Intensive Care Unit or High Dependency Unit
options.B: General postnatal ward with routine care
options.C: Her private home with oral medications
options.D: Outpatient clinic for follow-up next week

explanation: Mothers recovering from major blood loss need close, continuous monitoring of their vital signs and fluid balance in a high-care unit. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h7)

question: Why is psychological debriefing helpful after a mother experiences a severe PPH?

options.A: To test whether the mother's brain has suffered permanent damage from low blood pressure
options.B: To help the mother and family process the frightening near-miss experience and prevent trauma
options.C: To force the patient to remember every detail of the medications administered in theater
options.D: To convince the family to donate blood for future hospital emergency reserves

explanation: Severe obstetric emergencies can be very frightening, and talking through the experience helps reduce the risk of anxiety and post-traumatic stress. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T2#BMP315_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the main problem that happens in the body during obstetric shock?

options.A: Rapid destruction of platelets in the blood
options.B: Sudden rise in pressure inside the head
