options.C: Not enough blood flow reaching vital organs
options.D: Complete stopping of kidney filtering

explanation: Shock happens when the circulatory system fails to supply enough blood and oxygen to vital organs, causing cells to stop working properly. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why might a pregnant woman lose a lot of blood before her blood pressure actually drops?

options.A: The baby's heartbeat speeds up to make up for the blood loss
options.B: Pregnancy increases total blood volume, hiding early blood loss
options.C: Pregnancy hormones artificially stabilize blood pressure
options.D: The placenta acts as a backup tank to keep pressure steady

explanation: Because pregnancy increases total blood volume, the body compensates for initial bleeding, meaning blood pressure stays normal until shock is advanced. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which sign is usually the very first warning that a patient is developing shock from blood loss?

options.A: Changes in vision
options.B: High blood pressure
options.C: Fast heart rate
options.D: High body temperature

explanation: Tachycardia happens early because the heart pumps faster to make up for a drop in circulating blood volume. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h2)

question: A postpartum mother looks anxious, her skin is pale and sweaty, and her pulse is 120 beats per minute. What do these signs point to?

options.A: Normal postpartum recovery
options.B: A mild postpartum infection
options.C: Early signs of shock
options.D: A bad reaction to oxytocin

explanation: Anxiety, pale and sweaty skin, and a fast pulse are classic early warning signs of inadequate tissue perfusion and shock. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why should an unconscious pregnant woman in shock be placed with a tilt to her left side?

options.A: To keep her from swallowing her saliva
options.B: To stop the heavy uterus from pressing on major blood vessels
options.C: To help lochia drain out of the vagina
options.D: To make it easier to put in an IV line

explanation: Tilting the patient to the left relieves pressure off the aorta and inferior vena cava, keeping blood flowing back to the heart. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h3)

question: What size of intravenous cannula is best for quickly giving fluids in severe obstetric shock?

options.A: Large sizes like 16G or 14G
options.B: Standard pediatric needles
options.C: Small sizes like 22G or 24G
options.D: Only central lines

explanation: Large-bore cannulas allow rapid infusion of large volumes of fluids and blood products under pressure. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is a major danger of giving too much simple salt solution (crystalloid) during severe bleeding?

options.A: Causing a sudden allergic skin rash
options.B: Causing a sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: Diluting clotting factors and making bleeding worse
options.D: Permanently stopping all urine production

explanation: Too much crystalloid fluid dilutes the blood's natural clotting factors, making it harder for the body to stop bleeding. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h4)

question: What is the best type of fluid to replace blood when a patient has lost a dangerous amount of it?

options.A: High-concentration sugar solutions only
options.B: Oral rehydration salts mixed in water
options.C: Blood and appropriate blood products
options.D: Pure sterile water for injection

explanation: Replacing lost blood with actual blood or blood products restores oxygen-carrying capacity and clotting factors best. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is it not enough to just treat the symptoms of shock in an emergency?

options.A: Patients will develop an allergy to the IV cannula
options.B: Resuscitation fluids cannot work without extra drugs
options.C: Blood pressure will rise too high if the root cause is ignored
options.D: The underlying cause will keep making the patient worse

explanation: If the source of bleeding, infection, or vascular spasm is not stopped, the patient will continue to lose ground despite fluid therapy. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which medication is crucial for managing a patient with severe pre-eclampsia who is at risk of having seizures?

options.A: Broad-spectrum penicillin
options.B: Intravenous atropine
options.C: Magnesium sulfate
options.D: Oxytocin injection

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice for preventing and treating seizures associated with severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a recommended step when preparing a shocked obstetric patient for transport to another hospital?

options.A: Having a trained provider go along to monitor vitals
options.B: Sending a written record of all treatments given
options.C: Stopping all IV fluids so the bags do not spill
options.D: Making sure IV lines stay open and running

explanation: IV fluids and resuscitation must continue uninterrupted during transport to maintain stability; they should never be stopped. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why do midwives measure urine output every hour when resuscitating a patient in shock?

options.A: Good urine output shows that the kidneys and vital organs are getting enough blood flow
options.B: It proves the patient does not have a urinary tract infection
options.C: It shows that the bladder is empty and keeps the uterus in place
options.D: It proves that the IV fluids have no bacteria in them

explanation: The kidneys are sensitive to low blood volume and shut down early; seeing urine output return to normal confirms good systemic perfusion. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T3#BMP315_U2_T3_h6)

question: What three quick questions does a midwife ask right after a baby is born?

options.A: Heart rate, reflex irritability, and overall activity level
options.B: Gestational age, birth weight, and skin color
options.C: Gestational age, muscle tone, and breathing or crying effort
options.D: Presence of meconium, respiratory rate, and temperature

explanation: These three initial checks help identify newborns who need quick help versus those who can stay right with their mother. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h1)

question: A baby is born at 34 weeks, is limp, and is gasping. What should the midwife do first?

options.A: Move the infant to the radiant warmer for resuscitation
options.B: Administer oxygen via a simple nasal cannula
options.C: Bathe the infant quickly to stimulate breathing
options.D: Place the infant skin-to-skin on the mother's chest

explanation: Because this preterm baby has poor tone and is struggling to breathe, moving them to the radiant warmer allows for immediate care. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is drying a newborn baby thoroughly right after birth so important?

options.A: It triggers immediate closure of the ductus arteriosus
options.B: It prevents rapid heat loss and dangerous cold stress
options.C: It removes vernix caseosa to prevent skin infections
options.D: It stimulates the kidneys to begin producing urine

explanation: Wet skin causes heat to leave the baby's body very fast, which can lead to low body temperature and other complications. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h2)

question: How should a midwife position a newborn's head to keep the airway open?

options.A: Tilted backward into extreme hyperextension
options.B: In a neutral or slightly extended sniffing position
options.C: Turned fully sideways to one shoulder
options.D: Tucked firmly downward toward the chest

explanation: The sniffing position lines up the airway so air can flow easily into the lungs. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main sign that positive pressure ventilation (PPV) is working for a newborn?

options.A: Loud audible crying from the newborn
options.B: A rapid increase in the infant's heart rate
options.C: Immediate disappearance of acrocyanosis
options.D: Spontaneous passage of meconium stool

explanation: A rising heart rate is the clearest sign that the lungs are receiving air and oxygen during resuscitation. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h3)

question: What should a midwife do first if the newborn's chest is not rising during positive pressure ventilation?

options.A: Immediately begin emergency chest compressions
options.B: Administer emergency intravenous adrenaline
options.C: Check the mask seal and reposition the head
options.D: Double the peak inflation pressure on the device

explanation: If the chest is not moving, air is usually escaping because of a loose mask or the head position. Adjusting these fixes the problem most of the time. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h3)

question: Where should a midwife place the pulse oximeter sensor on a newborn to get a pre-ductal reading?

options.A: On the right wrist or hand
options.B: Around either ankle or foot
options.C: On the left wrist or hand
options.D: Directly over the apex of the heart

explanation: Blood reaches the right hand before passing through the ductus arteriosus, giving an accurate pre-ductal oxygen level. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h4)

question: A very ill newborn has poor circulation, and the pulse oximeter cannot catch a reliable heart rate. What device can be added right away?

options.A: A 3-lead electrocardiogram (ECG)
options.B: A peak flow meter for respiratory volume
options.C: A standard mercury sphygmomanometer
options.D: An electronic digital tympanic thermometer

explanation: ECG leads pick up the heart's electrical signals directly, which is helpful when weak pulses make other monitors unreliable. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which laryngoscope blade size is typically chosen for a full-term newborn baby?

options.A: Size 0
options.B: Size 1
options.C: Size 3
options.D: Size 00

explanation: A size 1 straight blade fits full-term babies best, while smaller sizes like size 0 are kept for preterm infants. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the best way to confirm that an endotracheal tube is placed correctly in the trachea?

options.A: Hearing air escaping around the edges of the lips
options.B: Observing immediate pinking of the infant's skin
options.C: Noticing gastric distention in the upper abdomen
options.D: Detecting exhaled carbon dioxide and symmetrical breath sounds

explanation: Carbon dioxide detectors and hearing breath sounds equally on both sides confirm the tube is in the windpipe and not the stomach. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is the correct ratio of chest compressions to breaths during neonatal resuscitation?

options.A: 3 compressions to 1 ventilation
options.B: 15 compressions to 2 ventilations
options.C: 30 compressions to 2 ventilations
options.D: 5 compressions to 1 ventilation

explanation: Resuscitating newborns focuses heavily on breathing, using a 3 to 1 ratio of compressions to breaths. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h6)

question: A newborn has received good PPV for 30 seconds, but the heart rate is still 45 beats per minute. What step is needed next?

options.A: Stop all resuscitation efforts and comfort the mother
options.B: Continue mask ventilation alone for another minute
options.C: Administer subcutaneous atropine immediately
options.D: Initiate chest compressions and prepare for intubation

explanation: If the heart rate stays below 60 beats per minute even with proper ventilation, chest compressions must be started. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the main emergency drug given during advanced newborn resuscitation if the heart rate stays below 60 beats per minute?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Atropine sulfate
options.C: Sodium bicarbonate
options.D: Adrenaline (Epinephrine)

explanation: Adrenaline helps constrict blood vessels and boosts heart rate and strength during severe bradycardia. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which blood vessel is the quickest and most practical route for emergency medicine in a newborn delivery suite?

options.A: Intramuscular injection into the anterior thigh
options.B: Central venous line via the internal jugular vein
options.C: Peripheral intravenous line in the scalp vein
options.D: Umbilical vein catheter placed in the delivery room

explanation: The umbilical vein is wide open and easy to access right after birth, making it the preferred emergency route. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common complication that needs careful monitoring after a baby undergoes resuscitation?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Hypoglycemia
options.C: Persistent pulmonary hypertension
options.D: Hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy

explanation: Gestational diabetes is a condition affecting the mother, whereas the other options are risks for a baby who experienced birth asphyxia. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h8)

question: A newborn has been successfully resuscitated. What is the key rule for giving oxygen during the recovery phase?

options.A: Switch exclusively to hyperbaric oxygen therapy chambers
options.B: Administer 100% pure oxygen continuously to prevent any risk of hypoxia
options.C: Titrate oxygen to avoid hyperoxia using pulse oximetry targets
options.D: Stop all supplemental oxygen entirely immediately after the heart rate stabilizes

explanation: Using too much oxygen can create harmful free radicals, so midwives carefully adjust the oxygen levels based on oximeter readings. [learn more](BMP315_U2_T4#BMP315_U2_T4_h8)

question: What is the main job of a midwife coordinating a ward shift?

options.A: Ordering all pharmacy drugs for the hospital
options.B: Conducting minor surgeries independently
options.C: Bridging hospital goals with bedside care
options.D: Writing the annual hospital financial budget

explanation: The coordinator connects administrative requirements with actual hands-on care delivered to mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is poor shift coordination dangerous in a maternity ward?

options.A: It forces the hospital to close the laboratory department
options.B: It automatically lowers the salary of the junior nurses
options.C: It increases the cost of purchasing medical textbooks
options.D: It can cause delayed emergency responses and missed care

explanation: Disorganization on the ward prevents quick action during obstetric emergencies, putting patients at risk. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h1)

question: What does 'acuity' mean when assessing a maternity ward?

options.A: The total number of beds available in the hospital
options.B: The speed at which laundry is washed on the ward
options.C: The severity of illness and care needs of the patients
options.D: The exact time the morning shift begins duty

explanation: Acuity refers to how sick patients are and how much nursing attention they require. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which patient requires the highest level of direct nursing observation?

options.A: An antenatal patient waiting for routine blood tests
options.B: A woman on her third day post-delivery breastfeeding well
options.C: A mother discharged and waiting for transport home
options.D: A patient with severe pre-eclampsia receiving magnesium sulfate

explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia and active medication infusions demand constant monitoring due to high risk of sudden complications. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is a key trait that helps a shift coordinator build good team morale?

options.A: Assigning yourself the easiest tasks every single day
options.B: Transparent duty rosters and fair work distribution
options.C: Refusing to listen to complaints from junior staff
options.D: Keeping all clinical information a secret from juniors

explanation: Fairness in scheduling stops staff from feeling cheated and keeps the working environment cooperative. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why must a shift coordinator maintain wide situational awareness?

options.A: To anticipate bottlenecks and prepare for patient surges
options.B: To avoid doing any physical nursing tasks themselves
options.C: To spend less time talking to incoming patients
options.D: To make sure no one takes a bathroom break all day

explanation: Watching the whole ward lets the coordinator spot trouble early and move staff before a crisis overwhelms them. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h3)

question: What does the letter 'S' stand for in the SBAR handover tool?

options.A: Salary
options.B: Schedule
options.C: Supplies
options.D: Situation

explanation: In SBAR, the first step is stating the current Situation clearly. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the best way to hand over care for a critically ill postpartum hemorrhage patient?

options.A: Wait until the morning meeting hours later to mention the bleeding
options.B: Walk to the bedside together to review lines, blood loss, and vitals
options.C: Announce it quickly across the room while walking out the door
options.D: Write it in a notebook and leave it on the nurses station desk

explanation: Bedside handovers for unstable patients ensure direct visual confirmation of critical clinical equipment and status. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h4)

question: Who keeps ultimate legal accountability when a task is delegated to a junior worker?

options.A: The senior midwife who made the delegation decision
options.B: The hospital security guard on duty at the gate
options.C: The patient receiving the nursing care
options.D: The federal ministry of health permanent secretary

explanation: The person delegating must ensure the recipient is competent and remains responsible for overall oversight. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which task is NOT appropriate to delegate to an untrained student midwife without direct supervision?

options.A: Administering intravenous oxytocin for postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Making up empty beds in the postnatal recovery room
options.C: Taking routine temperature and pulse observations
options.D: Distributing clean linen to stable mothers

explanation: High-risk medication administration requires advanced clinical judgment and supervision, making it unsafe for unsupervised students. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h5)

question: What should be your main priority during a severe staff shortage on a maternity ward?

options.A: Deep cleaning the empty rooms on the private wing
options.B: Conducting long lectures for junior student nurses
options.C: Immediate life-saving clinical care for unstable patients
options.D: Filing all routine monthly administrative paperwork

explanation: When resources are stretched thin, preserving patient survival takes precedence over clerical duties. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h6)

question: How should an acting manager handle sudden staff absence due to illness at the start of a shift?

options.A: Reallocate available staff from low-acuity areas and request emergency cover
options.B: Send half the patients home immediately without finishing their care
options.C: Ignore the missing staff and pretend the shift has normal numbers
options.D: Close the entire maternity ward gates until the next morning

explanation: Shifting existing staff to critical areas and seeking backup keeps the ward functional and safe. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T1#BMP324_U1_T1_h6)

question: If a ward manager hands a task over to a junior staff member, who remains responsible for the patient's overall outcome?

options.A: No responsibility once the task is handed over
options.B: Ultimate accountability for the patient outcome
options.C: Only the blame if the patient complains
options.D: Financial liability for hospital equipment

explanation: While the junior staff member performs the physical work, the manager who delegated the task retains the overarching responsibility for safe patient care. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is task delegation so important for a midwife manager in a busy hospital ward?

options.A: It allows the manager to distribute workloads safely and manage patient care efficiently
options.B: It completely frees the manager from ever checking on ward patients
options.C: It stops student midwives from asking too many questions
options.D: It punishes lazy workers by giving them extra duties

explanation: No single manager can handle every clinical need in a busy maternity unit alone. Proper task distribution is essential for safe, organized care. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is NOT one of the Five Rights of clinical delegation?

options.A: Right person
options.B: Right circumstance
options.C: Right hospital salary
options.D: Right task

explanation: Salary is an administrative employment matter, whereas the Five Rights focus entirely on safe clinical task distribution. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h2)

question: A midwife checks the patient's current stability and ward environment before passing a duty to a junior nurse. Which Right is being applied?

options.A: Right task
options.B: Right person
options.C: Right direction
options.D: Right circumstance

explanation: Evaluating the patient's current condition and the ward setting falls directly under the Right circumstance principle. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which Nigerian regulatory body defines the legal scope of practice for midwives?

options.A: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Labour and Productivity
options.D: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body responsible for setting training standards and defining the professional scope of practice for midwives in Nigeria. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h3)

question: What happens legally if a specialized midwifery procedure is delegated to someone not qualified to perform it, like a ward orderly?

options.A: It saves time without creating any professional risk
options.B: It constitutes professional misconduct and exposes the manager to legal liability
options.C: It is completely acceptable as long as the ward is busy
options.D: It transfers all legal blame entirely to the orderly

explanation: Assigning tasks outside a worker's legal scope violates professional rules and holds the delegating manager legally responsible. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why shouldn't a ward manager rely only on a staff member's job title when deciding to delegate a task?

options.A: Junior staff members always lie about their qualifications
options.B: Hospital management discourages looking at job titles
options.C: Job titles do not guarantee practical competence in every specific clinical skill
options.D: Titles change too often in Nigerian hospitals

explanation: Actual hands-on capability can vary widely among workers holding the exact same title, so individual competency checks are always necessary. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h4)

question: How can a ward manager best check if a junior nurse is truly ready to handle a complex task like monitoring postpartum bleeding?

options.A: Give them the task and wait for a complaint to arrive
options.B: Directly observe the nurse performing the skill or check recent competency records
options.C: Ask other patients if they trust the nurse
options.D: Assume they know how to do it because they finished nursing school

explanation: Direct observation and official competency records provide concrete proof of a worker's ability before assigning them independently. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the main reason for asking a staff member to repeat your instructions back to you?

options.A: To test their memory like a school examination
options.B: To confirm they fully understand the task and expected outcomes
options.C: To humiliate them in front of other ward colleagues
options.D: To waste time during a busy shift handover

explanation: The teach-back method ensures that verbal instructions were heard correctly and helps prevent costly misunderstandings in clinical care. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which instruction represents the best practice for clinical delegation?

options.A: Take care of the woman in the labour room when you have free time
options.B: Check Mrs. Bello's blood pressure in thirty minutes and report if it exceeds 140 over 90
options.C: Handle the ward emergencies properly while I am away
options.D: Do whatever is necessary for the antenatal patients today

explanation: Clear delegation requires a specific task, an exact timeframe, and precise parameters for when to report back. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h5)

question: At what point does the supervision and monitoring phase of clinical delegation officially end?

options.A: Only when a patient makes a formal complaint
options.B: The exact moment you give the initial instruction
options.C: After the task is completed and feedback is provided
options.D: When the staff member goes home for the day

explanation: Supervision continues throughout the task performance and wraps up with evaluation and feedback once the work is finished. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is giving timely feedback so important after a staff member completes a delegated task?

options.A: It is required to update the hospital financial payroll
options.B: It reinforces good clinical practices and corrects mistakes early
options.C: It prevents staff from ever asking questions again
options.D: It allows the manager to publicly punish poor workers

explanation: Constructive feedback helps staff grow professionally by validating correct actions and addressing errors before they affect patient safety. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main risk when a ward manager refuses to delegate because they believe nobody else can do the job right?

options.A: Managerial burnout and reduced overall ward efficiency
options.B: Greater trust from junior staff members
options.C: Improved clinical safety for every single patient
options.D: Faster career promotion within the hospital

explanation: Hoarding tasks leads to exhaustion, mistakes, and missed opportunities to mentor junior midwives on the ward. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h7)

question: What term describes the practice of assigning unpleasant ward chores to junior staff simply to avoid doing them yourself?

options.A: Effective mentorship
options.B: Right task assignment
options.C: Clinical supervision
options.D: Improper delegation

explanation: Dumping tasks inappropriately without regard for patient safety or fair workloads is considered improper delegation. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T2#BMP324_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the main goal of supervision in a maternity unit?

options.A: Guiding clinical practice and maintaining safety standards
options.B: Completing daily attendance registers for senior management
options.C: Punishing staff members who make documentation errors
options.D: Reducing the overall operational budget of the hospital

explanation: Supervision focuses on guiding practice and ensuring high standards of safety for mothers and babies rather than punishment or administrative tasks. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why should a ward manager create an environment where junior staff feel comfortable asking questions?

options.A: It eliminates the need for formal hospital training sessions entirely
options.B: It ensures that senior staff do not have to perform any clinical duties
options.C: It helps catch potential complications early and prevents hidden errors
options.D: It allows junior staff to take over total management of the ward

explanation: An open environment encourages honesty, allowing teams to address clinical mistakes and risks before they harm patients. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of these activities counts as clinical supervision?

options.A: Ordering new delivery kits from the central hospital store
options.B: Reviewing accurate partograph interpretation during active labor
options.C: Drafting the monthly leave roster for the nursing staff
options.D: Investigating missing inventory from the utility room

explanation: Clinical supervision directly addresses bedside patient care skills like monitoring labor progress with a partograph. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h2)

question: Nurse Ada spends her entire shift in the office organizing duty rosters and ignoring the labor ward floor. What is the most likely result?

options.A: Neonatal resuscitation outcomes will improve significantly
options.B: Staff morale will rise because administrative duties are cleared
options.C: Clinical standards and patient care quality will begin to slip
options.D: Supply stockouts will automatically resolve across the hospital

explanation: Neglecting the clinical floor to focus solely on paperwork leads to poor oversight of patient care and rising clinical risks. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of pairing experienced midwives with younger colleagues through mentorship?

options.A: To allow senior midwives to completely avoid night shifts
options.B: To pass down practical, real-world knowledge that textbooks often miss
options.C: To reduce the number of working hours required for junior staff
options.D: To enforce strict disciplinary actions for minor procedural delays

explanation: Mentorship allows veterans to share valuable hands-on wisdom and confidence with less experienced staff. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h3)

question: How should an effective supervisor handle a poor clinical outcome on the ward?

options.A: Transfer all responsibility immediately to the hospital director
options.B: Ignore the incident to prevent lowering overall department morale
options.C: Publicly reprimand the junior midwife during a busy handover
options.D: Hold a constructive audit meeting to examine team improvements

explanation: A learning culture uses adverse events as collective teaching moments rather than opportunities for unfair blame. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h3)

question: Who ultimately keeps the responsibility for a patient outcome when a task is delegated to another staff member?

options.A: The hospital security department on duty that day
options.B: The ward manager or nurse who delegated the task
options.C: The junior staff member who performed the physical action
options.D: The patient's family members who consented to care

explanation: Delegating a task shifts the execution, but the legal and professional accountability for appropriate delegation stays with the delegator. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is the first step a manager should take before assigning a clinical task to a junior staff member?

options.A: Evaluate the competency of the staff and the stability of the patient
options.B: Ensure that all administrative documentation for the shift is completed
options.C: Inform the medical director about the planned ward task
options.D: Check if the staff member has worked overtime during the week

explanation: Safe delegation requires matching the staff member's skill level with the clinical needs and stability of the patient. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h4)

question: When should an acting ward manager address a noticeable clinical performance gap?

options.A: After other colleagues complain about the individual
options.B: Only during the formal annual staff appraisal meeting
options.C: Promptly as soon as the performance gap is identified
options.D: When the hospital management requests a disciplinary review

explanation: Addressing issues immediately prevents bad habits from becoming ingrained and protects patient safety. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h5)

question: Why is it important to give constructive feedback privately rather than in front of patients or colleagues?

options.A: It reduces the amount of paperwork required for disciplinary records
options.B: It allows the supervisor to avoid documenting the incident officially
options.C: It prevents embarrassment and encourages an open, receptive discussion
options.D: It ensures that hospital administrators never find out about the mistake

explanation: Private feedback preserves the staff member's dignity and promotes a productive dialogue focused on correction rather than defense. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the best way to evaluate a student midwife's clinical competence?

options.A: A single written examination taken at the end of posting
options.B: The speed at which they complete administrative filing
options.C: Direct observation of skills over a period of time
options.D: Opinions gathered from patients during discharge interviews

explanation: Continuous observation provides a fair, accurate picture of true clinical competence compared to a one-time test. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why should a ward manager ask student midwives to check their own performance before giving feedback?

options.A: It ensures the student never argues with the final grade given
options.B: It completely replaces the need for the supervisor to grade them
options.C: It shortens the time needed to complete clinical rotation forms
options.D: It builds critical self-awareness essential for safe practice

explanation: Self-appraisal encourages learners to critically reflect on their own strengths and weaknesses, fostering professional growth. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T3#BMP324_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a primary clinical risk associated with high patient volume on a labor ward?

options.A: Too many empty beds for incoming admissions
options.B: Excessive availability of emergency drugs
options.C: Prolonged rest breaks for nursing staff
options.D: Delayed recognition of maternal complications

explanation: When a ward is overcrowded, staff can become overwhelmed, which increases the chance of missing early warning signs of distress in mothers or babies. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why does rapid bed turnover create a challenging environment for labor ward midwives?

options.A: It leaves little time for proper documentation and thorough assessment
options.B: It completely stops new emergency admissions from arriving
options.C: It forces midwives to work exclusively in outpatient clinics
options.D: It guarantees that patients will stay in the hospital for weeks

explanation: Moving women in and out quickly means midwives must perform fast assessments without missing critical clinical details. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which of the following conditions represents an immediate priority during obstetric triage?

options.A: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.B: Mild lower back pain at 36 weeks
options.C: Routine booking visit inquiry
options.D: Early latent phase contractions

explanation: Severe bleeding can lead to rapid shock and death, making it a top priority that requires instant resuscitation. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main goal of establishing an organized obstetric triage system?

options.A: To make sure every patient is discharged within one hour
options.B: To eliminate the need for doctors on the labor ward
options.C: To reduce the total number of pregnant women visiting the hospital
options.D: To ensure the sickest patients receive care first

explanation: Triage ensures that limited medical resources and staff attention are directed immediately to those whose lives are in the greatest danger. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which physiological measurement is typically included in a standard MEWS assessment?

options.A: Amniotic fluid volume
options.B: Respiratory rate
options.C: Fundal height measurement
options.D: Urine protein level

explanation: Respiratory rate is a vital sign monitored in MEWS because changes in breathing often indicate early systemic shock or distress. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h3)

question: A postpartum patient's MEWS suddenly increases due to a high heart rate and low blood pressure. What action should the midwife take next?

options.A: Tell the patient to walk around the ward to improve circulation
options.B: Escalate the score immediately to the medical team for urgent review
options.C: Discharge the patient home since her temperature is normal
options.D: Wait for the next shift change to report the vital signs

explanation: A rising MEWS score serves as an alarm bell requiring rapid professional intervention to prevent severe complications like hemorrhage shock. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h3)

question: When deploying staff during a busy shift, how should ward managers primarily assign midwives?

options.A: By assigning the newest interns to major surgical emergencies
options.B: By letting staff choose any room they prefer
options.C: Strictly according to alphabetical order of surnames
options.D: Based on clinical skill mix and patient acuity

explanation: Matching experienced staff to high-risk patients ensures safe care when the ward is under heavy pressure. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is keeping emergency equipment in a centralized, known location vital during a crisis?

options.A: It reduces the total number of nurses needed on duty
options.B: It ensures that equipment never breaks down or requires repairs
options.C: It prevents patients from touching the equipment
options.D: It minimizes time wasted searching for tools during an emergency

explanation: In obstetric emergencies, every second counts, and knowing exactly where supplies are saves critical time. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h4)

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the SBAR communication tool?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Background
options.C: Bleeding
options.D: Breathing

question: What is the primary benefit of using closed-loop communication during a resuscitation?

options.A: It allows the team to work completely in silence
options.B: It replaces the need to document events in the case note
options.C: It confirms that instructions were clearly heard and understood
options.D: It prevents doctors from speaking to midwives at all

explanation: Repeating an order back ensures the person executing it caught every detail correctly, reducing dangerous medical errors. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which strategy helps prevent overcrowding on a busy labor ward?

options.A: Refusing to admit any new pregnant women after midday
options.B: Using fast-track discharge protocols for normal births
options.C: Closing down the operating theater during peak hours
options.D: Keeping all postpartum mothers in the delivery suite for a week

explanation: Releasing stable mothers promptly frees up physical beds for incoming emergencies. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why is a separate space for women in early latent labor useful during high-volume surges?

options.A: It keeps the main delivery rooms open for active, high-risk emergencies
options.B: It stops babies from being born outside the hospital gates
options.C: It allows midwives to completely ignore latent labor patients
options.D: It guarantees that no woman will ever feel pain during childbirth

explanation: Segregating early labor prevents them from cluttering acute suites where intensive monitoring is required. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of conducting a clinical audit after a critical incident?

options.A: To identify systemic workflow problems and improve future care
options.B: To find a junior nurse to blame for the bad outcome
options.C: To increase the hospital's billing fees for the patient
options.D: To make sure no records are ever kept on the ward

explanation: Audits focus on how the system can be fixed to prevent repeat errors rather than punishing single workers. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why is regular debriefing important for midwives working in high-volume maternity units?

options.A: It ensures that paperwork is completed twice as fast
options.B: It helps process traumatic events and reduces emotional burnout
options.C: It stops patients from complaining about long waiting times
options.D: It replaces the need for annual financial salary reviews

explanation: Processing stressful cases with colleagues provides emotional support and prevents cumulative psychological fatigue. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T4#BMP324_U1_T4_h7)

question: During a busy obstetric emergency, what is the best physical stance for a midwife team leader?

options.A: Leaving the room to call senior consultants immediately
options.B: Performing all emergency procedures single-handedly
options.C: Writing the medical notes while waiting for orders
options.D: Stepping back to maintain overall situational awareness

explanation: Stepping back helps the leader oversee the entire scene, track vital signs, and spot problems early instead of getting trapped in a single task. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h1)

question: A midwife is leading a team during a severe eclamptic fit. Which action shows good leadership?

options.A: Taking over every task to ensure nothing goes wrong
options.B: Assigning team roles while monitoring the patient's overall response
options.C: Waiting quietly until the attending doctor arrives to give instructions
options.D: Focusing entirely on inserting an IV line and ignoring other team members

explanation: Effective leaders coordinate and oversee the broader clinical picture rather than getting bogged down in a single procedural step. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is pointing and calling a specific staff member's name important when delegating during an emergency?

options.A: It speeds up the process of writing the patient case notes
options.B: It ensures senior staff members always get the easiest tasks
options.C: It prevents diffusion of responsibility among team members
options.D: It is a strict legal requirement for nursing documentation

explanation: When a leader singles someone out by name, it removes ambiguity so everyone knows exactly who is responsible for the task. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which team member is mainly responsible for tracking the timing of given medications and fluid volumes?

options.A: Recorder and timekeeper
options.B: Airway management lead
options.C: Laboratory scientific officer
options.D: Primary surgeon on call

explanation: The recorder maintains a chronological log of events, drugs, and fluids so the team has accurate data during resuscitation. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of using closed-loop communication during a resuscitation?

options.A: To reduce the number of staff members needed in the room
options.B: To satisfy hospital accreditation requirements for record keeping
options.C: To make sure the patient falls asleep during the procedure
options.D: To confirm that orders are heard, understood, and executed

explanation: Repeating instructions back eliminates misunderstandings caused by background noise or stress in the emergency room. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h3)

question: A team member receives an instruction to give magnesium sulfate. What is the correct response in a closed-loop system?

options.A: Nod silently and begin searching for a syringe in the medication trolley
options.B: Ask another colleague if they think the dose is appropriate
options.C: Wait until the procedure is fully completed before speaking
options.D: Repeat the medication name and dose back to the leader immediately

question: What timeframe is known as the golden hour during critical obstetric complications?

options.A: The sixty minutes spent completing ward shift handovers

options.C: The first sixty minutes after the crisis begins
options.D: The final hour of labor before spontaneous delivery

question: Why should a midwife leader use structured checklists during the golden hour of resuscitation?

options.A: To punish team members who make minor procedural mistakes

options.C: To replace the need for physical examination of the patient

question: What is the main focus of a post-resuscitation team debriefing session?

options.A: Evaluating system performance and identifying communication gaps

question: Why is immediate post-resuscitation documentation essential for clinical safety?

options.A: It provides a clear baseline for ongoing care and legal protection
options.B: It replaces the need for verbal shift handover reports
options.C: It allows the team to leave the hospital premises much earlier

explanation: Accurate, timely records guide subsequent care providers and protect staff legally by documenting exact interventions. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T5#BMP324_U1_T5_h5)

question: What is the main goal of checking clinical skills before graduation?

options.C: To replace classroom exams with hospital tests
options.D: To cut down the working hours needed for trainees

explanation: This check ensures trainees have the practical skills needed to practice safely once they graduate. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h1)

question: Why are practical skills assessments so important in busy maternity units?

options.A: It removes the need for any future training
options.B: High patient numbers mean every student must master procedures to keep care safe
options.C: Patients refuse care without a laminated card
options.D: Government rules require daily written tests

explanation: Busy wards expose students to many cases, making proper skills checks essential for maintaining high standards and patient safety. [learn more](BMP324_U1_T6#BMP324_U1_T6_h1)

question: Which procedure is used during antenatal care to check the baby's position and lie?

question: You are monitoring a woman two hours after a normal delivery. Which finding needs an immediate response?

options.A: Moderate lochia rubra on the pad
options.B: A soft, relaxed uterus with heavy bleeding
options.C: An axillary temperature of 37.1 degrees Celsius

question: What is the main use of a clinical skills passport?

question: Why do assessment checklists include infection control along with the final result of a procedure?

question: What does DOPS stand for in clinical training?

options.D: Direct Observation of Procedural Skills

question: What is the main benefit of getting feedback right after a DOPS session?

options.A: It guarantees you will never make another clinical error
options.B: It removes the need for written exams
options.C: It lets you correct mistakes and improve your technique right away
options.D: It stops patients from ever complaining

question: Why is simulation training helpful even when students spend months working in active wards?

options.A: Simulation is only meant for doctors

question: What is a main goal of the discussion session after an emergency simulation?

question: What does SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: Staffing, Budget, Admission, Report

question: You are handling three patients at once: a woman in early latent labor, a woman with a severe headache and high protein in her urine, and a mother wanting a routine check. Who should you see first?

question: How should clinical preceptors view a skill a student struggles with during an assessment?

options.D: As a chance to provide extra support and targeted practice

question: Which of these is NOT part of a standard support plan for a student needing extra help?

options.C: Clear timelines for a future re-assessment

question: Who usually sits on the final review panel for graduating midwifery students?

question: What main responsibility starts as soon as you begin independent practice?
